# Azmara Platform Docs

> Documentation for the Azmara Platform packages.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs

Welcome to the Azmara Platform documentation. Use the sidebar to browse guides, package references, and security documentation.

This site is served from MDX files committed to this repository — content changes go through normal pull requests, same as the code it documents.

---

# Introduction

> Azmara Platform is a modern, data-first application runtime where your data layer is a first-class citizen, not an afterthought.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/introduction

Unlike modern stacks that bolt a database onto the side of a framework, Azmara puts data at the centre:

```
[ Reactive Signals ] → [ Query Engine ] → [ SQLite Persistence ] → [ React UI ]
                                ↑
                        [ AI Auto-Fix ]
```

## Core principles

- **Data-first** — your data layer is integrated, not external
- **Reactive by default** — UI updates automatically when data changes
- **Secure by design** — parameterised queries, sandboxed AI, tamper-evident logs
- **Type-safe throughout** — TypeScript with strict mode across all packages

## Packages

| Package                   | Purpose                                                                                         |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@azmr/core`              | Reactive signals, effects, computed values                                                      |
| `@azmr/query`             | Chainable, data-first query builder                                                             |
| `@azmr/db`                | Secure SQLite adapter                                                                           |
| `@azmr/db-core-interface` | The `DbAdapter` contract both database adapters implement, no dependencies                      |
| `@azmr/db-supabase`       | Supabase/PostgREST adapter, same interface as `@azmr/db`                                        |
| `@azmr/ui`                | React components wired to signals                                                               |
| `@azmr/ai`                | AI auto-fix with a capability-scoped `isolated-vm` sandbox                                      |
| `@azmr/security`          | Validation, RBAC, JWT, audit logging, sanitisation                                              |
| `@azmr/policycore`        | Security policy engine — rate limits, CORS, request signing, secrets, API keys, OWASP reporting |
| `@azmr/cli`               | Command-line tooling                                                                            |

---

# Installation

> Set up the Azmara Platform monorepo locally.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/installation

## Prerequisites

- Node.js >= 20.0.0
- pnpm >= 9.0.0
- **For `@azmr/ai`**: Visual Studio 2022 with "Desktop development with C++" workload

## Clone & install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/azmara-labs/platform.git
cd platform
pnpm install
```

## Environment setup

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

Fill in the required values:

```bash
# Generate an encryption key
node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))"
```

## Build all packages

```bash
pnpm build
```

## Try the playground

```bash
pnpm --filter @azmr/site dev
```

Then open `/playground` — a live, interactive demo of `@azmr/core`, `@azmr/query`, and `@azmr/ui`
working together, no separate app to run. See the [Playground](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/playground.md) guide for
what it demonstrates.

## Native module note

`@azmr/ai` uses `isolated-vm` which requires native compilation.

**Windows:**

1. Install **Visual Studio 2022** with "Desktop development with C++" workload
2. Run `pnpm rebuild isolated-vm`

**macOS:** Xcode Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`)

**Linux:** `sudo apt install build-essential python3`

---

# Playground

> A live, interactive demo of @azmr/core, @azmr/query, and @azmr/ui working together.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/playground

The [playground](https://platform.azmara.io/playground) is a live, in-browser demo — no local setup required. It's part of this docs site itself, built with the real `@azmr/core`, `@azmr/query`, and `@azmr/ui` packages, not a mockup.

## What it demonstrates

### 1. Reactive engine

The **Reactive Engine** panel wires a `Signal` and two `computed` values to on-screen controls — clicking `+`/`−`/`reset` updates the source signal, and every dependent value re-renders automatically:

```typescript
const count = new Signal(0);
const doubled = computed(() => count.get() * 2);

effect(() => {
  console.log(`count=${count.get()}  doubled=${doubled.get()}`);
});

count.set(1); // → count=1  doubled=2
count.set(5); // → count=5  doubled=10
```

### 2. Query engine

The **Query Engine** panel filters and sorts a live customer list as you drag a "balance ≥" slider — the query re-runs on every signal change, no manual re-fetching:

```typescript
const active = query(customers)
  .where(c => c.balance > 0)
  .orderBy((a, b) => b.balance - a.balance)
  .select();
```

### 3. Reactive grid

The **Reactive Grid** panel uses `@azmr/ui`'s `Grid` component over a `Signal<Product[]>` — adding or removing a product re-renders the table with no manual state wiring:

```tsx
const products = new Signal<Product[]>([...]);

function ProductGrid() {
  const data = useSignal(products);
  return <Grid signal={products} />;
}
```

### SQLite persistence

The playground doesn't run a live SQLite demo (a shared database file under concurrent public
requests isn't safe), but the same pattern applies directly to `@azmr/db`:

```typescript
const db = new SQLiteAdapter(".azmara/playground.db", ".azmara");

await db.createTable("products", { name: "string", price: "number", inStock: "boolean" });
await db.insertMany("products", [/* ... */]);

const available = query(await db.getAll("products"))
  .where(p => p.inStock === 1)
  .select();
```

---

# Reactivity

> Azmara's reactive system is built around three primitives — Signal, effect, and computed.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/reactivity

## Mental model

Think of it like a spreadsheet:

- **Signal** = a cell with a value
- **computed** = a formula cell that derives from other cells
- **effect** = a side-effect that runs when cells it reads change (like a chart that updates)

## Signals are the source of truth

```typescript
const price = new Signal(100);
const quantity = new Signal(3);
```

## Computed values derive from signals

```typescript
const subtotal = computed(() => price.get() * quantity.get());
const gst = computed(() => subtotal.get() * 0.15);
const total = computed(() => subtotal.get() + gst.get());
```

## Effects react to changes

```typescript
effect(() => {
  console.log(`Total: $${total.get().toFixed(2)}`);
});
// → Total: $345.00

price.set(200);
// → Total: $690.00
```

## Automatic dependency tracking

You don't declare dependencies manually. The reactive system tracks which Signals are read during each effect or computed run — and only re-runs when those specific signals change.

## Connecting to React

Use `useSignal` from `@azmr/ui` to bridge Signals into React components:

```tsx
import { useSignal } from "@azmr/ui";

function TotalDisplay({ total }: { total: Signal<number> }) {
  const value = useSignal(total);
  return <span>${value.toFixed(2)}</span>;
}
```

---

# Data-First Philosophy

> Azmara is built around a single idea — your data layer should not be an external dependency, it should be the foundation.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/data-first

## The problem with modern stacks

Modern application stacks have fragmented what should be a cohesive system. To show a list of records you now wire together:

- A database driver
- An ORM or query builder
- A state management library
- A UI framework
- An API layer to connect them all

Each layer has its own config, its own bugs, and its own version mismatch risks. The result is more glue than product.

## What Azmara does differently

Azmara treats data, reactivity, and UI as a single integrated system — not separate tools bolted together.

```
[ Data (SQLite) ] → [ Query Engine ] → [ Reactive Signals ] → [ React UI ]
```

Every layer speaks the same language. Query results flow directly into Signals. Signals drive React components. The UI stays in sync automatically — no manual wiring.

## The core model

```
@azmr/db      ← your data lives here, secured and persistent
@azmr/query   ← you express what you want, not how to get it
@azmr/core    ← the result becomes reactive automatically
@azmr/ui      ← your UI reflects reality at all times
```

## What this means in practice

```typescript
// 1. Define your data
const db = new SQLiteAdapter(".azmara/app.db", ".azmara");
await db.createTable("orders", { customer: "string", total: "number", paid: "boolean" });

// 2. Query it
const unpaid = query(await db.getAll("orders"))
  .where(o => !o.paid)
  .orderBy((a, b) => b.total - a.total)
  .select();

// 3. Make it reactive
const unpaidSignal = new Signal(unpaid);

// 4. Render it — updates automatically
<Grid signal={unpaidSignal} />
```

No reducers. No selectors. No store configuration. Data flows in one direction, from source to screen.

---

# Tailwind CSS setup

> What @azmr/ui needs from Tailwind CSS v4, how Tailwind finds the package's classes, and why class names are spelled out in full.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/tailwind

`@azmr/ui` is styled with Tailwind CSS v4. The package does not install Tailwind for you; your app provides it.

## What you need

- **Tailwind CSS v4.** The stylesheets use v4 directives (`@theme inline` and `@source`), so v3 does not work.
- **A build step for Tailwind.** With PostCSS (Next.js, for example), add Tailwind's plugin:

```js
// postcss.config.mjs
export default {
  plugins: { "@tailwindcss/postcss": {} },
};
```

This setup, Next.js with PostCSS, is the one the package's own consumer test installs and builds. Tailwind's Vite plugin (`@tailwindcss/vite`) is its standard alternative; it is not covered by that test yet, and the getting-started guides will add it.

## Import the stylesheet

In your global CSS, after Tailwind:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@azmr/ui/styles.css";
```

Use `@azmr/ui/tokens.css` instead if your app already has global styles. The [package page](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/ui.md#styles-and-design-tokens) explains the difference, and the [token reference](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/tokens.md) lists everything the stylesheet defines.

## How Tailwind finds the package's classes

Tailwind generates CSS only for the class names it finds in the files it scans. Your own files are scanned automatically, but the package's components are in `node_modules`. The stylesheet handles that with one rule:

```css
@source "./**/*.js";
```

A path in `@source` is relative to the stylesheet that contains it, so Tailwind scans the installed package's JavaScript, wherever your package manager put it. You add nothing to your config.

The package's consumer test checks this. It packs the package, installs it into a fresh Next.js and Tailwind v4 app outside this repository, builds the app, and confirms that classes which exist only inside the package's JavaScript are in the generated CSS. It also runs once with the `@source` rule removed and expects that run to fail, so the check is known to detect the problem.

Classes in other packages of your own, such as a shared component library in a monorepo, need their own `@source`:

```css
@source "../../packages/my-ui/src";
```

## Spell class names out in full

Tailwind finds a class by reading it as text. A class built at runtime is never seen, so it silently produces no CSS:

```tsx
// Not generated: "bg-success" never appears in the source as a whole.
const wrong = (tone: string) => `bg-${tone}`;

// Generated: every class appears in full.
const tones = {
  success: "bg-success",
  warning: "bg-warning",
  info: "bg-info",
} as const;
```

The package follows the same rule. Its responsive layout classes (`Stack` direction, `Grid` columns and spans) are tables of complete class strings, generated by a script, and a test recomputes the tables and fails if they drift. If you wrap a component and choose classes from a prop, use a lookup table like `tones` above.

---

# Theming

> Change the brand colours, switch between light and dark, set density, and see exactly what createTheme guarantees.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/theming

`@azmr/ui` is themed with CSS custom properties: the [design tokens](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/tokens.md). You can override a token in plain CSS, or call `createTheme` to derive a whole accessible set from your brand colours. The examples with an `// =>` line on this page are run by the docs tests, so the output shown is what the package returns.

## Change the brand colour with createTheme

```ts
import { createTheme } from "@azmr/ui/theme";

const theme = createTheme({ primary: "#1E88E5", radius: "0.5rem" });
const changed = Object.keys(theme.cssVariables);
// => ["--primary","--primary-foreground","--ring","--sidebar-primary","--sidebar-primary-foreground","--sidebar-ring","--radius"]
```

Setting `primary` sets six variables: the colour, the text on it, the focus ring, and the same three for the sidebar. Each colour value is a `light-dark()` pair, so it follows the page's mode. These are the options:

| Prop          | Type                                                    | Default | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `primary`     | `string \| Oklch \| undefined`                          |         | No       | Brand colour as `#rgb`, `#rrggbb`, `oklch(L C H)` or `{ l, c, h }`.                                                                                                                                      |
| `secondary`   | `string \| Oklch \| undefined`                          |         | No       | Secondary surfaces (secondary Button, Badge). Same accepted formats as `primary`.                                                                                                                        |
| `success`     | `string \| Oklch \| undefined`                          |         | No       | Status colours. Each is derived so its foreground is AA on it in both modes, and so it stays readable as text on the page and on cards (`Text tone`, form errors). `destructive` is the "danger" colour. |
| `warning`     | `string \| Oklch \| undefined`                          |         | No       |                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `info`        | `string \| Oklch \| undefined`                          |         | No       |                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `destructive` | `string \| Oklch \| undefined`                          |         | No       |                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `radius`      | `string`                                                |         | No       | `rem` or `px`, e.g. `0.5rem`.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `font`        | `string`                                                |         | No       | A CSS font-family list, e.g. `Inter, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`.                                                                                                                                            |
| `density`     | `"compact" \| "comfortable" \| "spacious" \| undefined` |         | No       |                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

Every option is optional and keeps its default when left out. Colours are `#rgb`, `#rrggbb`, `oklch(L C H)` or `{ l, c, h }`.

### What it guarantees

The colour you pass is a starting point. `createTheme` moves its lightness, and picks white or near-black text, until these hold in both light and dark mode:

- Each `-foreground` is at least **4.5:1** on its colour, **including on a solid button's hover surface**. A button blends with the page on hover, which can pull a colour that only just passes below 4.5:1, so the derivation checks the blended colour too.
- `success`, `info` and `destructive` are also readable as **text** on the page and on cards (`Text tone`, form errors). `warning` is a yellow surface, so it gets a separate, darker `--warning-text` for text.
- The focus ring is at least **3:1** on the page and on cards.

Because of this, the result can differ from your input. The light-mode primary above is darker than `#1E88E5`, so that white text on it stays readable when the pointer is over it. A very light brand colour such as `#FFEB3B` goes the other way and gets dark text:

```ts
const theme = createTheme({ primary: "#FFEB3B" });
const foreground = theme.cssVariables["--primary-foreground"];
// => "light-dark(oklch(0.145 0 0), oklch(0.145 0 0))"
```

Print `theme.cssVariables` to see what you get. The package's tests check these ratios for a range of brand colours, and the [token reference](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/tokens.md#contrast-the-tests-guarantee) lists the ratios for the default tokens.

### Invalid input

`createTheme` validates every option and throws an `Error` that names it, because its output is CSS:

```ts
let message;
try {
  createTheme({ primary: "blue" });
} catch (error) {
  message = error.message;
}
// => "createTheme: primary must be #rgb, #rrggbb, oklch(L C H) or { l, c, h }; got \"blue\""
```

`radius` must be a number in `rem` or `px`, `font` must be a short font-family list (letters, digits, spaces, commas, quotes, dots, hyphens and underscores, 200 characters at most), and `density` must be `compact`, `comfortable` or `spacious`.

## Apply the theme

A theme is a set of custom properties, so apply it to `<html>`, or to any element to theme only what is inside it:

```tsx
import { createTheme } from "@azmr/ui/theme";

const theme = createTheme({ primary: "#1E88E5", destructive: "#D32F2F" });

// Whole app: the variables as a style attribute, density as data-density.
<html lang="en-NZ" style={theme.cssVariables} {...theme.htmlAttributes}>

// One section only.
<section style={createTheme({ primary: "#7B1FA2" }).cssVariables}>…</section>
```

You can also emit the variables as CSS:

```ts
const theme = createTheme({ radius: "0.5rem", font: "Inter, sans-serif" });
const css = theme.css;
// => ":root {\n  --radius: 0.5rem;\n  --font-sans-stack: Inter, sans-serif;\n}"
```

Prefer the `style` attribute: an inline style always wins. If you output `theme.css` in a `<style>` tag, put it **after** the `@azmr/ui` stylesheet. The tokens' own scopes (`.dark`, `[data-theme]`) have the same specificity as `:root`, so for the same element the later rule wins.

A theme's colours set on an outer element do not reach inside a nested `data-theme` or `.dark` scope, because that scope re-declares every colour token. Put the theme's variables on the scope element itself, or inside it.

To change one token by hand, override it for light and for dark:

```css
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.55 0.2 260);
}

.dark,
[data-theme="dark"] {
  --primary: oklch(0.75 0.15 260);
}
```

## Dark mode

By default the page follows the operating system. The colours use OKLCH with `light-dark()` and `color-scheme: light dark`, so there is no JavaScript and no flash.

To force a mode, put `class="dark"` or `class="light"`, or `data-theme="dark"` or `data-theme="light"`, on `<html>` or on any element. Scopes nest: a `data-theme="light"` panel inside a dark page is light.

```html
<html data-theme="dark">
  <body>
    <aside data-theme="light">Always light, even on a dark page.</aside>
  </body>
</html>
```

Each scope declares every colour token explicitly instead of relying on `light-dark()` alone. Some bundlers (Next.js does, for older browser targets) rewrite `light-dark()` into variables that resolve where they are declared, which would stop a nested scope from changing anything. Declaring the colours in each scope works however the CSS is processed, and a test keeps those copies identical to `:root`.

### Remember the choice without a flash

Store the preference in a cookie and render it into `<html>` on the server, so the first paint is already right. This needs no inline script, so it works under a strict Content-Security-Policy:

```ts
import { htmlAttributes } from "@azmr/ui/theme";

const attributes = htmlAttributes.fromCookies("azmr-theme=dark; azmr-density=compact");
// => {"data-theme":"dark","data-density":"compact"}
```

Only known values are accepted. Anything else in the cookie is ignored, and `system` needs no attribute at all:

```ts
const ignored = htmlAttributes.fromCookies("azmr-theme=evil; azmr-density=huge");
// => {}
```

`ThemeProvider` and `useTheme()` change the theme and density on the client and write the cookie; see [Theme, density and locale](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/ui.md#theme-density-and-locale) for a Next.js layout. A static site that cannot read cookies on the server can inline `themeInitScript()` instead; give the `<script>` tag your CSP nonce.

## Density

Density changes control heights, horizontal padding, gaps and row height together. Set `data-density="compact"` or `data-density="spacious"` on `<html>` or on any element; comfortable is the default and needs no attribute.

```html
<div data-density="compact">
  <!-- Buttons, inputs and table rows in here are compact. -->
</div>
```

The [token reference](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/tokens.md#density-levels) lists the four values at each level. `createTheme` can set it too, through `htmlAttributes`:

```ts
const compact = createTheme({ density: "compact" }).htmlAttributes;
const comfortable = createTheme({ density: "comfortable" }).htmlAttributes;
const attributes = { compact, comfortable };
// => {"compact":{"data-density":"compact"},"comfortable":{}}
```

## Reduced motion

When the operating system asks for reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`), every `--motion-duration-*` token collapses to `0.01ms` and the stagger step to `0ms`. A safety net also shortens other animations and transitions on the page. Reduced motion follows the system setting; the tokens have no per-subtree switch.

Mark motion that is genuinely essential, such as a spinner that shows work is happening, with `data-motion="essential"` to keep it. See [Motion](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/motion.md#tokens) for the motion tokens and what each component does.

---

# Customising components

> Four ways to change how a component looks or behaves, from a className override to copying its source with the shadcn CLI.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/customising

There are four ways to change a component, from lightest to heaviest. Start at the top and move down only when the lighter one cannot do what you need. Every example here is a live demo that the docs tests render, or code that the docs tests run.

## 1. Pass a className

Every component accepts `className` and merges it last with [tailwind-merge](https://github.com/dcastil/tailwind-merge), so a class you pass replaces the default it conflicts with:

```tsx
import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";

// `className` is merged last, so each class below replaces the default it conflicts with.
export default function ClassOverride() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Button>Default</Button>
      <Button className="rounded-full px-8">Pill, wider</Button>
      <Button variant="outline" className="border-primary text-primary">
        Branded outline
      </Button>
      <Button className="h-14 text-base">Taller</Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

The merge is the `cn` helper, and you can use it for your own components. It is exported from `@azmr/ui/lib`, which is server-safe:

```ts
import { cn } from "@azmr/ui/lib";

const merged = cn("size-8", "size-10");
// => "size-10"
```

It resolves conflicts per Tailwind utility group, so a wider padding replaces only the padding it conflicts with:

```ts
const padding = cn("px-4 py-2", "px-6");
// => "py-2 px-6"
```

And it accepts strings, arrays, objects and falsy values, like `clsx`:

```ts
const classes = cn("text-sm", false && "hidden", ["font-bold"], { underline: true });
// => "text-sm font-bold underline"
```

Prefer the token utilities (`bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`) over raw colours in your overrides, so they follow the theme, dark mode and any [scoped theme](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/theming.md).

## 2. Reuse the button's styles with buttonVariants

When a link or a router component should look like a button, use `buttonVariants`. It returns the button's classes as a string for the `variant` and `size` you ask for, so any element can wear them:

```tsx
"use client";

import { buttonVariants } from "@azmr/ui/button";

// `buttonVariants` returns the button's classes as a string, so any element can look like a button.
// It lives in a client entry, so call it from a Client Component.
export default function LinkAsButton() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <a href="#documentation" className={buttonVariants({ variant: "outline" })}>
        Documentation
      </a>
      <a href="#start" className={buttonVariants({ size: "lg" })}>
        Get started
      </a>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`buttonVariants` is exported from `@azmr/ui/button`, which is a client entry, so call it from a Client Component. If the element should also behave like a button (a real `<button>`, a loading state), use `<Button render={<a href="…" />}>` instead; see [Button](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/button.md).

## 3. Wrap a component to set defaults

To give your app a house style, wrap the component. Forward `ref` and spread the remaining props, so `className`, `onClick` and `aria-*` still reach the real element:

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button, type ButtonProps } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { forwardRef } from "react";

/** A Button with house defaults. Whatever a caller passes, including `className` and `ref`, wins. */
const ActionButton = forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement, ButtonProps>(function ActionButton(props, ref) {
  return <Button ref={ref} variant="outline" size="sm" {...props} />;
});

export default function WrappedButton() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <ActionButton>Save draft</ActionButton>
      <ActionButton variant="default">Publish</ActionButton>
      <ActionButton className="rounded-full">Custom shape</ActionButton>
    </div>
  );
}
```

The wrapper's defaults apply only when a caller does not pass the prop, and the wrapper still gets everything the component guarantees: the tokens, the focus ring and the keyboard behaviour.

## 4. Copy the source with the shadcn CLI

When you need to change the structure, not just the style, copy the component into your app and edit it. The same components are published to a shadcn-compatible registry; see [Or copy the source with the shadcn CLI](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components.md#or-copy-the-source-with-the-shadcn-cli) for the setup.

Today the registry has `button`, `spinner` and a `tokens` item (the density, motion and elevation tokens plus the colours a standard shadcn app lacks). Other components are available from the package only.

The cost of copying is ownership: you take on updates, and fixes that ship in the package do not reach your copy. Keep using the tokens in the copy, so theming and dark mode keep working.

## Which one to use

| You want to                                          | Use                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Change a colour, size, shape or spacing in one place | `className`                                                                               |
| Make a link or a router link look like a button      | `buttonVariants`                                                                          |
| Give every use in your app the same defaults         | A wrapper component                                                                       |
| Change what the component renders or how it behaves  | Copy the source                                                                           |
| Change the whole palette, radius, font or density    | [`createTheme`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/theming.md), not a component change |

---

# Design tokens

> Every design token in @azmr/ui, with its light and dark values, the Tailwind utilities that use it, and the contrast it is tested against.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/tokens

Every colour, radius, motion, elevation, layering and density value in `@azmr/ui` is a CSS custom property declared in `@azmr/ui/tokens.css`. This page is generated from that file when the docs are built, so it cannot drift from it.

In the colour tables the swatch shows the light value on the left and the dark value on the right. Colours are OKLCH. The names follow shadcn/ui, so components from any shadcn registry fit alongside ours.

To change a token, override it in your own CSS after the import, for any scope:

```css
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.55 0.2 260);
}

.dark {
  --primary: oklch(0.75 0.15 260);
}
```

## Shape

| Token      | Value      | Tailwind                                               | Notes |
| ---------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----- |
| `--radius` | `0.625rem` | `rounded-sm`, `rounded-md`, `rounded-lg`, `rounded-xl` |       |

## Categorical chart palette

8 series), tuned for contrast and colour-vision deficiency. Found with a constrained search (>= 3.2:1 on surfaces, inside sRGB, maximising the worst pairwise CIEDE2000 under normal, protan, deutan and tritan vision); tokens.test.ts holds the thresholds.

|   | Token       | Light                   | Dark                    | Tailwind     |
| - | ----------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------ |
|   | `--chart-1` | `oklch(0.52 0.19 266)`  | `oklch(0.69 0.165 273)` | `bg-chart-1` |
|   | `--chart-2` | `oklch(0.64 0.105 45)`  | `oklch(0.8 0.17 73)`    | `bg-chart-2` |
|   | `--chart-3` | `oklch(0.58 0.062 173)` | `oklch(0.64 0.152 158)` | `bg-chart-3` |

|   | `--chart-5` | `oklch(0.64 0.124 231)` | `oklch(0.86 0.12 204)`  | `bg-chart-5` |

## Density

Comfortable by default.

| Token                         | Value     | Tailwind | Notes |
| ----------------------------- | --------- | -------- | ----- |
| `--density-control-height`    | `2.25rem` |          |       |
| `--density-control-padding-x` | `0.75rem` |          |       |

| `--density-row-height`        | `2.75rem` |          |       |

### Density levels

Set `data-density="compact"` or `data-density="spacious"` on any element to change the density of everything inside it.

| Token                         | Compact    | Comfortable (default) | Spacious  |
| ----------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------- | --------- |
| `--density-control-height`    | `2rem`     | `2.25rem`             | `2.75rem` |
| `--density-control-padding-x` | `0.625rem` | `0.75rem`             | `1rem`    |
| `--density-gap`               | `0.375rem` | `0.5rem`              | `0.75rem` |
| `--density-row-height`        | `2.25rem`  | `2.75rem`             | `3.25rem` |

## Contrast the tests guarantee

The values below are computed from the tokens above with the WCAG 2.x contrast formula. The package's own tests fail if any of them drops below its threshold, so a token change cannot make a component unreadable without a test failing.

# Accessibility

> The accessibility target for @azmr/ui, what is tested automatically, what is not tested yet, and how to build accessible screens with it.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/accessibility

Accessibility is a design goal of `@azmr/ui`, not an add-on. The target is **WCAG 2.2 level AA**: components are keyboard-complete, name themselves to assistive technology, keep a visible focus ring and follow the reduced-motion setting.

This page says what is checked, and where the checking stops. Every component page has its own Accessibility section with a keyboard map, and the [accessibility reference](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/accessibility-reference.md) lists all of them in one place.

## What is tested automatically

- **Every component runs axe in its tests.** More than thirty of the package's test files render components and fail on any [axe](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core) violation, in the states the tests reach, such as a menu closed and open.
- **Every live demo on this site is checked.** The docs tests render every demo and fail the build on an axe violation, so a demo cannot ship inaccessible.
- **Keyboard use is exercised.** Tests drive components with simulated key presses (Tab, arrows, Home, End, Enter, Space, Escape) and check where focus goes and what happens.
- **Colour contrast is computed.** Every foreground and background token pair is calculated from the tokens and tested for WCAG contrast in light and dark mode. The [token reference](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/tokens.md#contrast-the-tests-guarantee) lists the ratios.
- **Reduced motion is tested.** The motion tokens collapse under `prefers-reduced-motion`, and the tests check it. See [reduced motion](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/theming.md#reduced-motion).

## What is not tested yet

- **Real devices.** Animation playback, touch gestures (such as swiping a toast away) and hover behaviour are verified by unit and CSS tests in a simulated browser, not on real devices.
- **Screen readers.** Results of manual screen-reader testing are not published here yet. The design plans a manual pass for each phase of the library.
- **Everything axe cannot see.** Automated checks find only part of the problems. They do not replace trying a screen on a keyboard and with a screen reader.

If you find a barrier, please [open an issue](https://github.com/azmara-labs/platform/issues).

## Building accessible screens

### Name every icon-only control

A control with no text needs an accessible name. `IconButton` requires a `label`, and a `Button` with `size="icon"` must be given `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`: TypeScript enforces both. If you add a tooltip, keep the `label` too, because a tooltip is not an accessible name on touch devices. See [Button](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/button.md).

### Pair errors with text

`Input` exposes an invalid state through `aria-invalid`, not through colour alone. Always show a text message next to the field as well. See [Input](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/input.md).

### Return focus after a dialog

A dialog traps focus, makes the page behind it inert and returns focus to the control that opened it when it closes. An alert dialog starts focus on its cancel button, so pressing Enter by reflex cannot confirm something destructive. Give every dialog a title. See [Modal](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/modal.md).

### Announce changes

Toasts live in a polite live region named "Notifications", and errors are also written to a separate alert so they are spoken at once. A button with `loading` sets `aria-busy` instead of changing its label silently. See [Toast](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/toast.md).

### Respect the motion setting

Animation follows the operating system's reduced-motion setting automatically. Mark only motion that is genuinely essential with `data-motion="essential"`. See [Theming](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/theming.md#reduced-motion) and [Motion](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/motion.md).

---

# Accessibility reference

> Which components take keyboard input, every component's key map in one place, and what is checked for each page.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/accessibility-reference

This page is generated from the component pages when the docs are built, so it lists every component and cannot drift from them. For what is tested and what is not, see [Accessibility](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/accessibility.md).

## By component

| Component                                                                 | Group        | Takes keyboard input | Key map rows | Live demos (axe-checked) | Notes                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | -------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Layout](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/layout.md)            | Layout       | No                   | n/a          | 3                        | [Accessibility](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/layout.md#accessibility)       |
| [ScrollArea](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/scroll-area.md)   | Layout       | Yes                  | 5            | 1                        | [Accessibility](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/scroll-area.md#accessibility)  |
| [Button](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/button.md)            | Inputs       | Yes                  | 3            | 5                        | [Accessibility](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/button.md#accessibility)       |

| [Progress](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/progress.md)        | Feedback     | No                   | n/a          | 2                        | [Accessibility](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/progress.md#accessibility)     |
| [Spinner](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/spinner.md)          | Feedback     | No                   | n/a          | 1                        | [Accessibility](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/spinner.md#accessibility)      |
| [Toast](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/toast.md)              | Feedback     | Yes                  | 3            | 3                        | [Accessibility](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/toast.md#accessibility)        |
| [Floating](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/floating.md)        | Overlays     | Yes                  | 4            | 3                        | [Accessibility](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/floating.md#accessibility)     |
| [Modal](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/modal.md)              | Overlays     | Yes                  | 3            | 4                        | [Accessibility](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/modal.md#accessibility)        |
| [Menu](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/menu.md)                | Overlays     | Yes                  | 10           | 3                        | [Accessibility](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/menu.md#accessibility)         |
| [Breadcrumb](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/breadcrumb.md)    | Navigation   | Yes                  | 2            | 1                        | [Accessibility](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/breadcrumb.md#accessibility)   |
| [Pagination](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/pagination.md)    | Navigation   | Yes                  | 3            | 2                        | [Accessibility](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/pagination.md#accessibility)   |
| [Stepper](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/stepper.md)          | Navigation   | Yes                  | 1            | 1                        | [Accessibility](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/stepper.md#accessibility)      |
| [Motion](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/motion.md)            | Utils        | No                   | n/a          | 7                        | [Accessibility](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/motion.md#accessibility)       |

"Live demos" counts the demos embedded on the page. The docs tests render every demo and fail on an axe violation, so each one is accessibility-checked. "Key map rows" counts the rows of the key map on the page.

## Keyboard reference

15 components take keyboard input. Each key map below is the one on the component's own page.

### [ScrollArea](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/scroll-area.md#accessibility)

| Key                         | Action                                           |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `Tab`                       | Moves focus to the scrollable region.            |
| `ArrowDown` or `ArrowUp`    | Scrolls the region vertically.                   |
| `ArrowRight` or `ArrowLeft` | Scrolls horizontally when it overflows that way. |
| `PageDown` or `PageUp`      | Scrolls by a page.                               |
| `Home` or `End`             | Scrolls to the start or end.                     |

### [Button](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/button.md#accessibility)

| Key                | Action                                                              |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter` or `Space` | Activates the button. Ignored while loading.                        |
| `Tab`              | Moves focus to the button. A loading button stays in the tab order. |
| `Shift` or `Tab`   | Moves focus to the previous control.                                |

### [SplitButton](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/split-button.md#accessibility)

| Key                | Action                                                                     |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`              | Moves to the main button, then to the arrow button.                        |
| `Enter` or `Space` | On the main button: runs the primary action. On the arrow: opens the menu. |
| `ArrowDown`        | On the arrow button: opens the menu on its first item.                     |
| `Escape`           | Closes the menu and returns focus to the arrow button.                     |

### [Input](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/input.md#accessibility)

| Key              | Action                                                              |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`            | Moves focus into and out of the field. Disabled inputs are skipped. |
| `Shift` or `Tab` | Moves focus to the previous control.                                |
| `Esc`            | Not captured, so a parent dialog can use it to close.               |

### [Toggle](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/toggle.md#accessibility)

| Key                         | Action                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`                       | Enters the group at a single tab stop, then moves on. Only one item is in the tab order at a time (roving tabindex).      |
| `ArrowRight` or `ArrowLeft` | Moves focus to the next or previous item and wraps (ArrowDown and ArrowUp when vertical). It never changes the selection. |
| `Home` or `End`             | Moves focus to the first or last item.                                                                                    |
| `Space` or `Enter`          | Presses or releases the focused item.                                                                                     |

### [Display](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/display.md#accessibility)

| Key                | Action                                                      |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`              | Moves focus to the dismiss button of an Alert that has one. |
| `Enter` or `Space` | Dismisses the Alert (calls onDismiss).                      |

### [Table](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/table.md#accessibility)

| Key                                                     | Action                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`                                                   | Moves to the scroll region when the table has a label. Nothing else in a static table is focusable. |
| `ArrowDown` or `ArrowUp` or `ArrowRight` or `ArrowLeft` | Scrolls a focused, labelled region.                                                                 |
| `PageDown` or `PageUp` or `Home` or `End`               | Scrolls by a page, or to the start or end.                                                          |

### [Disclosure](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/disclosure.md#accessibility)

#### Accordion keys

| Key                      | Action                                                                            |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`                    | Moves to the next trigger (or the first focusable element in an open panel).      |
| `Enter` or `Space`       | Opens or closes the focused section.                                              |
| `ArrowDown` or `ArrowUp` | Moves focus to the next or previous trigger and wraps. It does not open anything. |
| `Home` or `End`          | Moves focus to the first or last trigger.                                         |

#### Tabs keys

| Key                         | Action                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`                       | Enters the tab list at the selected tab, then moves on to the panel.      |
| `ArrowRight` or `ArrowLeft` | Moves focus between tabs and wraps (ArrowDown and ArrowUp when vertical). |
| `Home` or `End`             | Moves focus to the first or last tab.                                     |
| `Enter` or `Space`          | Selects the focused tab (not needed with activateOnFocus).                |

### [Toast](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/toast.md#accessibility)

| Key                  | Action                                                                                           |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `F6`                 | Moves focus into the notifications region. Tab then moves between the actions and close buttons. |
| `Tab` or `Shift+Tab` | Moves between the toasts' buttons. The timers pause while focus is inside.                       |
| `Enter` or `Space`   | Activates the focused action or close button.                                                    |

### [Floating](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/floating.md#accessibility)

| Key                  | Action                                                                             |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`                | Focusing a tooltip trigger or hover-card link shows its surface; leaving hides it. |
| `Enter` or `Space`   | Opens a popover from its trigger.                                                  |
| `Tab` or `Shift+Tab` | Moves through the content of an open popover.                                      |
| `Escape`             | Closes the open tooltip, popover or hover card. Focus returns to the trigger.      |

### [Modal](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/modal.md#accessibility)

| Key                  | Action                                                               |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab` or `Shift+Tab` | Moves through the controls inside the surface and wraps at the ends. |
| `Escape`             | Closes the top surface. Focus returns to the control that opened it. |
| `Enter` or `Space`   | Opens from a trigger, and activates the focused button inside.       |

### [Menu](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/menu.md#accessibility)

| Key                               | Action                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter` or `Space` or `ArrowDown` | On the trigger: opens the menu on the first item.                                                          |
| `ArrowUp`                         | On the trigger: opens the menu on the last item.                                                           |
| `ArrowDown` or `ArrowUp`          | Moves to the next or previous item and wraps at the ends.                                                  |
| `Home` or `End`                   | Jumps to the first or last item.                                                                           |
| `A–Z`                             | Typeahead: jumps to the item that starts with the letters you type. Letters typed together are one search. |
| `Enter` or `Space`                | Runs the focused item and closes the menu. A checkbox or radio item toggles.                               |
| `ArrowRight`                      | On a submenu trigger: opens the submenu and focuses its first item.                                        |
| `ArrowLeft`                       | In a submenu: closes it and returns to its trigger.                                                        |
| `Escape`                          | Closes the open submenu, or the menu. Focus returns to the trigger.                                        |
| `Tab`                             | Closes the menu and moves on. Focus is never trapped.                                                      |

### [Breadcrumb](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/breadcrumb.md#accessibility)

| Key     | Action                                                                                   |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`   | Moves through the links in order. The current page and the separators are not focusable. |
| `Enter` | Follows the focused link.                                                                |

### [Pagination](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/pagination.md#accessibility)

| Key     | Action                                                                      |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`   | Moves through the page controls. A disabled Previous or Next is skipped.    |
| `Enter` | Follows a link, or activates a button.                                      |
| `Space` | Activates a button page. (Links respond to Enter only, as native links do.) |

### [Stepper](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/stepper.md#accessibility)

| Key   | Action                                                       |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Tab` | Nothing in a stepper is focusable: it only reports progress. |

# Components

> The @azmr/ui component library, built on Base UI primitives and the Azmara design tokens.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components

`@azmr/ui` is a component library for React 18 and 19, built on [Base UI](https://base-ui.com) primitives, styled with Tailwind v4 and a small set of design tokens. Every component page has live demos you can preview in light and dark and at each density, the source of each demo, a props table generated from the TypeScript types, and an accessibility section with the keyboard map.

> **Using Vue, Svelte or another framework?**
>
> The components are React-only today. These parts have no React dependency:
> [`@azmr/core`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/core.md) (signals), [`@azmr/query`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/query.md),
> [`@azmr/security`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/security.md), the database packages
> ([`@azmr/db`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/db.md) and
> [`@azmr/db-core-interface`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/db-core-interface.md)), and the design tokens in
> `@azmr/ui/tokens.css`, which are plain CSS for any Tailwind v4 project.

## All components

Grouped by purpose. Each badge shows the component's maturity: stable, new or beta.

### Layout

- [Layout](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/layout.md): Stack, Grid with a responsive column count, Container, Separator and AspectRatio. All Server Components.
- [ScrollArea](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/scroll-area.md): A scrollable region with token-styled scrollbars that is keyboard-focusable and named. Built on Base UI.

### Inputs

- [Button](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/button.md): Triggers an action. Six variants, density-aware sizes, a loading state that keeps keyboard focus, and an icon-only form the types force you to name.
- [SplitButton](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/split-button.md): A primary action with a menu of related actions attached. Button plus DropdownMenu.
- [Input](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/input.md): A text input whose ref is the real input element, so react-hook-form works without a Controller.
- [Toggle](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/toggle.md): Toggle and ToggleGroup. A button that stays pressed, and a group of them that acts as one control with arrow-key navigation. Built on Base UI.

### Data display

- [Display](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/display.md): Card, Badge, Alert, Skeleton and EmptyState. Server Components with status colours checked for contrast in both themes.
- [Table](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/table.md): A semantic, non-interactive table with a caption, sticky header, striping and a named scroll region. Server-safe.
- [Avatar](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/avatar.md): A person or entity as an image with initials as the fallback, plus a group with a labelled overflow count. Built on Base UI.
- [Typography](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/typography.md): A type scale where the variant picks the semantic element, with Heading, Text, Link, Code and Kbd. All Server Components.
- [Icon](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/icon.md): Renders Lucide, Tabler or your own SVG with consistent size, stroke, motion and accessibility. A Server Component.
- [Disclosure](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/disclosure.md): Accordion, Collapsible and Tabs. Show and hide content with the keyboard maps users expect. Built on Base UI.

### Feedback

- [Progress](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/progress.md): A linear or circular progress indicator with a required name, a determinate and an indeterminate state, and tones that stay visible against the track.
- [Spinner](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/spinner.md): An indeterminate progress indicator that is a Server Component and keeps spinning under reduced motion.
- [Toast](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/toast.md): Short notifications raised from anywhere with toast.success(), toast.error() and toast.promise(). Stacked, pausable, swipeable and announced to screen readers. Built on Base UI.

### Overlays

- [Floating](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/floating.md): Tooltip, Popover and HoverCard. Surfaces anchored to a trigger, collision-aware, portalled, and animated with the motion tokens. Built on Base UI.
- [Modal](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/modal.md): Dialog, AlertDialog and Drawer. Surfaces that take over the screen, with a focus trap, an inert page, scroll lock and focus return. Built on Base UI.
- [Menu](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/menu.md): DropdownMenu and ContextMenu. Menus of actions with items, checkbox and radio items, groups and submenus. Built on Base UI.

### Navigation

- [Breadcrumb](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/breadcrumb.md): A trail showing where you are and the way back up. Built from parts or from data, collapsible, router-friendly. Server-safe.
- [Pagination](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/pagination.md): A page control that is real links on the server or buttons for client state, with a stable-width page range the data grid reuses. Server-safe.
- [Stepper](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/stepper.md): Shows where someone is in a fixed sequence of steps. A status display with each state said in text, horizontal or vertical. Server-safe.

### Utils

- [Motion](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/motion.md): CSS-first motion presets driven by tokens, a Collapse that never measures height, a count-up, a ViewTransition wrapper, useReducedMotion and an optional module for the motion library. Reduced motion is built in. (new)

## Set up

```css
/* global.css */
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@azmr/ui/styles.css";
```

Use `@azmr/ui/tokens.css` instead if the app already has global styles. See the [package page](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/ui.md) for the tokens, theming and locale.

## Or copy the source with the shadcn CLI

If you would rather own the code than import a package, the same components are published to a shadcn-compatible registry. Add the namespace to your `components.json`:

```json
{
  "registries": {
    "@azmr": "https://platform.azmara.io/r/{name}.json"
  }
}
```

Then, in a project that has run `npx shadcn@latest init`:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @azmr/button
```

This copies `button.tsx` and the components it needs (`spinner.tsx`) into `components/ui`, installs `@base-ui/react` and `class-variance-authority`, and adds a small `tokens` item to your `globals.css`: density, motion and elevation tokens, plus colours a standard shadcn setup lacks (`--destructive-foreground`, `--success`, `--warning`, `--info`). It never changes the tokens you already have, so your palette stays yours. The copied source is generated from the package source with only the import paths rewritten, so it behaves identically. Available now: `button`, `spinner`, `tokens`; more arrive with each component.

## What every component guarantees

- **Tokens only.** No raw colours; a test enforces it, so a theme change reaches every component.
- **Accessible by default.** Each component is tested with axe, by keyboard, and under reduced motion.
- **Server-safe where it can be.** Stateless components such as `Spinner` and `Icon` are Server Components; the rest carry `"use client"` on their own entry only.
- **Tree-shakeable, with budgets.** Each entry has a size budget checked in CI.
- **`className` merges last,** and `ref` is the real DOM element.

---

# Layout

> Stack, Grid with a responsive column count, Container, Separator and AspectRatio. All Server Components.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/layout

Group: Layout · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import { Stack, Grid, GridItem, Container, Separator, AspectRatio } from "@azmr/ui/layout";
```

Everything here is a **Server Component**: no hooks, no `"use client"`, safe in layouts and `loading.tsx`. They replace MUI's `Box`, `Stack`, `Grid` and `Container`.

## Stack

```tsx
import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { Separator, Stack } from "@azmr/ui/layout";

export default function LayoutStack() {
  return (
    <Stack gap={6}>
      {/* A column on phones, a row from md, with the gap following the density token. */}
      <Stack direction={{ base: "column", md: "row" }} gap="density" align="center">
        <Button>Save</Button>
        <Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
        <Button variant="ghost">Reset</Button>
      </Stack>

      {/* A divider goes between children only. */}
      <Stack direction="row" gap={4} align="center" divider={<Separator orientation="vertical" />}>
        <span>Overview</span>
        <span>Activity</span>
        <span>Settings</span>
      </Stack>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

`Stack` lays children out in a column (default) or a row with a consistent `gap`. `direction` accepts a responsive object, so a column on phones becomes a row from `md`. `gap` is on the 4px scale (0 to 12), or `density` to follow the density token. `divider` places an element between children, never before the first or after the last, and skips empty children.

## Grid

```tsx
import { Grid, GridItem } from "@azmr/ui/layout";

const cell = "rounded-md border border-border bg-muted p-4 text-sm";

export default function LayoutGrid() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-6">
      {/* One column on phones, two from sm, four from lg. */}
      <Grid cols={{ base: 1, sm: 2, lg: 4 }} gap={4}>
        <div className={cell}>One</div>
        <div className={cell}>Two</div>
        <div className={cell}>Three</div>
        <div className={cell}>Four</div>
      </Grid>

      {/* The 12-column pattern: cols={12} with a span per breakpoint. */}
      <Grid cols={12} gap={4}>
        <GridItem span={{ base: 12, md: 8 }} className={cell}>
          Main (12, then 8 of 12 from md)
        </GridItem>
        <GridItem span={{ base: 12, md: 4 }} className={cell}>
          Aside
        </GridItem>
      </Grid>

      {/* As many columns as fit, each at least 12rem wide. */}
      <Grid minItemWidth="12rem" gap={4}>
        <div className={cell}>Card</div>
        <div className={cell}>Card</div>
        <div className={cell}>Card</div>
        <div className={cell}>Card</div>
        <div className={cell}>Card</div>
      </Grid>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`Grid` is a CSS grid with a responsive `cols` prop (1 to 12). It is **not** MUI's 12-column item system: for that pattern use `cols={12}` and give children a `GridItem` with a `span` per breakpoint. For card layouts, `minItemWidth="16rem"` fills each row with as many columns as fit. `minItemWidth` is validated as a plain CSS length because it lands in a style attribute.

Breakpoints are Tailwind's: `sm` 640, `md` 768, `lg` 1024, `xl` 1280, `2xl` 1536px.

## Container, Separator and AspectRatio

```tsx
import { AspectRatio, Container, Separator, Stack } from "@azmr/ui/layout";

export default function LayoutContainer() {
  return (
    <Container size="sm" className="rounded-md border border-dashed border-border py-4">
      <Stack gap={4}>
        <p className="text-sm">A container centres its content and limits the width.</p>
        <Separator />
        <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4">
          <AspectRatio ratio="video" className="rounded-md bg-muted">
            <div className="grid size-full place-items-center text-sm">16 / 9</div>
          </AspectRatio>
          <AspectRatio ratio="square" className="rounded-md bg-muted">
            <div className="grid size-full place-items-center text-sm">1 / 1</div>
          </AspectRatio>
        </div>
      </Stack>
    </Container>
  );
}
```

- **`Container`** centres content, limits the width (`sm` 42rem to `xl` 80rem, `2xl` 96rem, or `full`) and adds gutters that grow with the screen (`gutters={false}` removes them).
- **`Separator`**: a horizontal one is a real `<hr>`; a vertical one is `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`. `decorative` hides it from assistive technology.
- **`AspectRatio`** keeps a ratio (`square`, `video`, `4/3`, `3/2`, `21/9`, `3/4`, or a number). Direct `img`, `video` and `iframe` children fill it.

## Migrating from MUI

`@azmr/ui/layout/mui-map` is plain data and helper functions for the codemod.

| MUI                                   | `@azmr/ui`                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<Grid container spacing={2}>`        | `<Grid cols={12} gap={4}>` (MUI spacing is 8px, ours 4px: `muiSpacingToGap`)                         |
| `<Grid item xs={12} md={6}>`          | `<GridItem span={{ base: 12, md: 6 }}>`                                                              |
| `alignItems`, `justifyContent`        | `align`, `justify`                                                                                   |
| `<Stack spacing={2} direction="row">` | `<Stack gap={4} direction="row">`                                                                    |
| `<Container maxWidth="md">`           | `<Container size="md">` (`xl` becomes `2xl`, 96rem = 1536px; `xs` is approximate; `false` is `full`) |
| `disableGutters`                      | `gutters={false}`                                                                                    |

A spacing with no matching step (such as 7), and item props that cannot be expressed (`xs="auto"`, `xs={true}`), are reported by the helpers as `undefined` or in `unsupported` so the codemod flags them rather than guessing. MUI's breakpoints are 0/600/900/1200/1536px and Tailwind's are 0/640/768/1024/1280px, so check layouts near the boundaries.

## Props

| Prop        | Type                                                                                                                                         | Default | Required | Description                                                                                       |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `direction` | `"row" \| "column" \| Partial<Record<"base" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| "2xl", "row" \| "column">> \| undefined`                      |         | No       | `column` (default) or `row`, or one per breakpoint: `{ base: "column", md: "row" }`.              |
| `gap`       | `0 \| 6 \| 1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 8 \| 10 \| 12 \| "density" \| undefined`                                                                 |         | No       | The space between children, on the 4px scale (0 to 12), or `density` to follow the density token. |
| `align`     | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch" \| "baseline" \| undefined`                                                                       |         | No       |                                                                                                   |
| `justify`   | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "between" \| "around" \| "evenly" \| undefined`                                                             |         | No       |                                                                                                   |
| `wrap`      | `boolean \| undefined`                                                                                                                       |         | No       |                                                                                                   |
| `divider`   | `ReactNode`                                                                                                                                  |         | No       | An element placed between children (never before the first or after the last).                    |
| `as`        | `"div" \| "section" \| "article" \| "aside" \| "nav" \| "header" \| "footer" \| "main" \| "ul" \| "ol" \| "form" \| "fieldset" \| undefined` |         | No       | The element to render. Default `div`.                                                             |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                                                                                                                                  |         | No       |                                                                                                   |

| Prop           | Type                                                                                                                                                        | Default | Required | Description                                                                                                                         |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cols`         | `6 \| 1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 7 \| 8 \| 9 \| 10 \| 11 \| 12 \| Partial<Record<"base" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| "2xl", ColumnCount>> \| undefined` |         | No       | Column count, or one per breakpoint: `{ base: 1, md: 3 }`. Default 1.                                                               |
| `minItemWidth` | `string`                                                                                                                                                    |         | No       | Fill the row with as many columns as fit, each at least this wide (`"16rem"`), instead of a fixed count. Takes the place of `cols`. |
| `gap`          | `0 \| 6 \| 1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 8 \| 10 \| 12 \| "density" \| undefined`                                                                                |         | No       |                                                                                                                                     |
| `align`        | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch" \| "baseline" \| undefined`                                                                                      |         | No       | Vertical alignment of items within their cell.                                                                                      |
| `justify`      | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch" \| undefined`                                                                                                    |         | No       | Horizontal alignment of items within their cell.                                                                                    |
| `as`           | `"div" \| "section" \| "article" \| "aside" \| "nav" \| "header" \| "footer" \| "main" \| "ul" \| "ol" \| "form" \| "fieldset" \| undefined`                |         | No       |                                                                                                                                     |
| `children`     | `ReactNode`                                                                                                                                                 |         | No       |                                                                                                                                     |

## Accessibility

- Layout components render no roles of their own; pass `as` for a landmark (`main`, `nav`, `aside`, `header`, `footer`, `section`) so the page has a real structure.
- Source order is the reading and tab order: do not rely on a grid to reorder content visually.
- A horizontal `Separator` is announced as a separator; mark it `decorative` when the content either side already reads as separate.

---

# ScrollArea

> A scrollable region with token-styled scrollbars that is keyboard-focusable and named. Built on Base UI.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/scroll-area

Group: Layout · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import { ScrollArea } from "@azmr/ui/scroll-area";
```

```tsx
import { ScrollArea } from "@azmr/ui/scroll-area";

const items = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, i) => `Customer ${i + 1}`);

export default function ScrollAreaBasic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-6">
      {/* Tab to focus it, then the arrow keys and Page Up/Down scroll. It needs a name. */}
      <ScrollArea aria-label="Customers" className="h-48 w-64 border border-border">
        <ul className="p-3 text-sm">
          {items.map((item) => (
            <li key={item} className="border-b border-border py-2 last:border-b-0">
              {item}
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </ScrollArea>

      {/* Horizontal, with the scrollbar always visible. */}
      <ScrollArea
        aria-label="Wide table"
        orientation="horizontal"
        scrollbar="always"
        className="w-64 border border-border"
      >
        <p className="w-[40rem] whitespace-nowrap p-3 pb-5 text-sm">
          A long line of content that is wider than the area it sits in, so it scrolls sideways.
        </p>
      </ScrollArea>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Give the area a size (`h-48`, `max-h-96`, `w-64`) with `className` and put long content inside. The scrollbars are styled from tokens and fade in on hover and while scrolling (`scrollbar="always"` keeps them visible, `orientation` picks vertical, horizontal or both). They only mount when something overflows; `keepMounted` keeps them in the DOM so layout never jumps.

## Why it needs a name

A scrollable region has to be reachable with the keyboard, otherwise a keyboard user cannot scroll it at all. The viewport is therefore a focusable `role="region"`, and a focusable region needs an accessible name: pass `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at a heading. TypeScript requires one of them.

Use a `ScrollArea` when you want consistent scrollbars. For simple overflow, plain CSS `overflow: auto` is fine, and modern browsers already make scrollable regions focusable.

## Props

| Prop                | Type                                                | Default | Required | Description                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `orientation`       | `"vertical" \| "horizontal" \| "both" \| undefined` |         | No       | Which scrollbars to show. Default `vertical`.                                                                                 |
| `scrollbar`         | `"always" \| "hover" \| undefined`                  |         | No       | `hover` (default) fades the scrollbar in on hover and while scrolling, like the desktop platforms; `always` keeps it visible. |
| `keepMounted`       | `boolean \| undefined`                              |         | No       | Keep the scrollbars in the DOM even when nothing overflows, so layout never jumps.                                            |
| `viewportClassName` | `string`                                            |         | No       | Classes for the scrollable viewport (padding, for example); `className` styles the root.                                      |
| `viewportRef`       | `Ref<HTMLDivElement> \| undefined`                  |         | No       | A ref to the scrollable element, to read or set the scroll position.                                                          |
| `className`         | `string`                                            |         | No       |                                                                                                                               |
| `children`          | `ReactNode`                                         |         | No       |                                                                                                                               |

`className` styles the root; `viewportClassName` styles the scrollable element (padding, for example). `ref` is the root and `viewportRef` is the scrollable element, to read or set the scroll position.

## Accessibility

- The viewport is a focusable `role="region"` with the name you provide.
- Scrollbars fade with the motion tokens, so they stop animating under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- The focus ring is full strength and inset, so it is never clipped by the area's edge.

| Key                         | Action                                           |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `Tab`                       | Moves focus to the scrollable region.            |
| `ArrowDown` or `ArrowUp`    | Scrolls the region vertically.                   |
| `ArrowRight` or `ArrowLeft` | Scrolls horizontally when it overflows that way. |
| `PageDown` or `PageUp`      | Scrolls by a page.                               |
| `Home` or `End`             | Scrolls to the start or end.                     |

---

# Button

> Triggers an action. Six variants, density-aware sizes, a loading state that keeps keyboard focus, and an icon-only form the types force you to name.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/button

Group: Inputs · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
```

```tsx
import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";

export default function ButtonVariants() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
        <Button>Default</Button>
        <Button variant="secondary">Secondary</Button>
        <Button variant="outline">Outline</Button>
        <Button variant="ghost">Ghost</Button>
        <Button variant="destructive">Destructive</Button>
        <Button variant="success">Success</Button>
        <Button variant="warning">Warning</Button>
        <Button variant="info">Info</Button>
        <Button variant="link">Link</Button>
      </div>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
```
