```tsx
        <Button size="sm">Small</Button>
        <Button>Medium</Button>
        <Button size="lg">Large</Button>
        <Button disabled>Disabled</Button>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Use `default` for the primary action on a screen, `secondary` and `outline` for supporting ones, `ghost` for toolbars, `destructive` for irreversible actions and `link` for navigation that should read as text. `success`, `warning` and `info` are solid status buttons for confirmations and alerts that need an action; their labels are checked for contrast on the hover surface as well as at rest. The `md` size follows the density token: switch the preview above to Compact or Spacious and it resizes, exactly as it will inside an app that sets `data-density`.

A button is `type="button"` unless you say otherwise, so one inside a form never submits by accident. Pass `type="submit"` to opt in.

## Loading

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";

export default function ButtonLoading() {
  const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false);
  const timer = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined>(undefined);
  useEffect(() => () => clearTimeout(timer.current), []);

  function save() {
    setSaving(true);
    timer.current = setTimeout(() => setSaving(false), 1500);
  }

  // While loading the button ignores clicks and keys but stays focusable, so a keyboard user
  // keeps their place.
  return (
    <Button loading={saving} loadingText="Saving" onClick={save}>
      Save changes
    </Button>
  );
}
```

`loading` shows a spinner, sets `aria-busy`, and ignores clicks **and** keyboard activation. It stays in the tab order, so a keyboard user who pressed Enter does not lose their place and a screen reader still finds the button. `loadingText` replaces the label while it is busy.

## Icons and links

```tsx
import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { Icon } from "@azmr/ui/icons";
import { ArrowRight, Plus, X } from "lucide-react";

export default function ButtonIcons() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Button startIcon={<Icon icon={Plus} />}>New customer</Button>
      <Button variant="outline" endIcon={<Icon icon={ArrowRight} />}>
        Continue
      </Button>
      {/* An icon-only button needs an accessible name; the types require it. */}
      <Button size="icon" variant="ghost" aria-label="Close">
        <Icon icon={X} />
      </Button>
      {/* Render as a link, with button styling and the right semantics. */}
      <Button
        variant="link"
        nativeButton={false}
        render={<a href="https://platform.azmara.io/docs" />}
      >
        Read the docs
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`startIcon` and `endIcon` sit either side of the label; while `loading`, the spinner replaces the start icon. An icon-only button must be given an accessible name: with `size="icon"` TypeScript requires `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. To render a link with button styling, pass `render={<a href="..." />}` and `nativeButton={false}`.

## IconButton

```tsx
import { IconButton } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { Icon } from "@azmr/ui/icons";
import { Pencil, Plus, Trash2 } from "lucide-react";

export default function IconButtonBasic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      {/* The label is required: it is the button's accessible name. */}
      <IconButton icon={<Icon icon={Plus} />} label="Add item" />
      <IconButton icon={<Icon icon={Pencil} />} label="Edit" variant="outline" />
      <IconButton icon={<Icon icon={Trash2} />} label="Delete" variant="destructive" />
      <IconButton
        icon={<Icon icon={Plus} />}
        label="Add item (small)"
        size="sm"
        variant="secondary"
      />
      <IconButton icon={<Icon icon={Plus} />} label="Saving" loading variant="outline" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { IconButton } from "@azmr/ui/button";
```

A square button with only an icon, passed as an element: `<IconButton icon={<Icon icon={Plus} />} label="Add item" />`. (An element rather than a component, so it also works from a Server Component.) `label` is **required** and becomes the accessible name: an icon alone cannot be announced, so the types do not let you leave it out (and an empty string throws in development). It is `ghost` by default so a row of them stays quiet, takes the same variants as `Button`, and `loading` swaps the icon for a spinner while keeping the button focusable. `size` is `sm`, `md` (follows the density token) or `lg`.

For a tooltip on an icon button, wrap it in a `Tooltip`, and keep the `label` too: a tooltip is not an accessible name on touch devices.

## ButtonGroup

```tsx
import { Button, ButtonGroup } from "@azmr/ui/button";

export default function ButtonGroupBasic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-6">
      <ButtonGroup aria-label="Page navigation">
        <Button variant="outline">Previous</Button>
        <Button variant="outline">Today</Button>
        <Button variant="outline">Next</Button>
      </ButtonGroup>
      <ButtonGroup aria-label="Export format" orientation="vertical">
        <Button variant="outline">PDF</Button>
        <Button variant="outline">CSV</Button>
        <Button variant="outline">Excel</Button>
      </ButtonGroup>
      <ButtonGroup aria-label="Spaced actions" attached={false}>
        <Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
        <Button>Save</Button>
      </ButtonGroup>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { ButtonGroup } from "@azmr/ui/button";
```

A named group (`role="group"`, with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` required) of related buttons, joined into one control: inner corners squared, one shared border, and the hovered or focused button raised so its focus ring is never hidden by a neighbour. `orientation="vertical"` stacks them, and `attached={false}` keeps them apart with a gap.

It is **only a grouping**: Tab still visits every button. If the buttons should act as one control with arrow keys and a pressed state, use [ToggleGroup](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/toggle.md). If one of them opens a menu, use [SplitButton](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/split-button.md).

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                                                                                                           | Default | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`     | `"default" \| "secondary" \| "outline" \| "ghost" \| "destructive" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "info" \| "link" \| undefined` |         | No       | Visual style. `default` is the primary action; use `destructive` for irreversible ones.                                                                                 |
| `size`        | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "icon" \| undefined`                                                                                  |         | No       | `md` follows the density token, so it grows or shrinks with `data-density`. `icon` is a square button for an icon alone and requires `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. |
| `loading`     | `boolean \| undefined`                                                                                                         |         | No       | Show a spinner, mark the button busy and ignore activation. It stays focusable.                                                                                         |
| `loadingText` | `ReactNode`                                                                                                                    |         | No       | Replaces the label while `loading`.                                                                                                                                     |
| `startIcon`   | `ReactNode`                                                                                                                    |         | No       | Shown before the label; replaced by the spinner while `loading`.                                                                                                        |
| `endIcon`     | `ReactNode`                                                                                                                    |         | No       | Shown after the label.                                                                                                                                                  |

Everything a native button accepts passes through (`onClick`, `type`, `disabled`, `aria-*`, `ref`, ...), plus these from the underlying primitive:

| Prop                    | Type                       | Description                                                                               |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `render`                | `ReactElement` or function | Render a different element (such as `<a>`) with the button's behaviour and styles.        |
| `nativeButton`          | `boolean`                  | Set to `false` when `render` is not a native `<button>`.                                  |
| `focusableWhenDisabled` | `boolean`                  | Keep a disabled button in the tab order. `loading` does this for you.                     |
| `className`             | `string`                   | Merged last, so it can override defaults: `className="h-12"` replaces the default height. |

## Accessibility

- It is a real `<button>` (or the element you `render`), so it has the right role, name from its content, and disabled semantics with no ARIA added.
- Focus uses a full-strength ring that meets WCAG 2.2 focus appearance; the same ring is used on every control.
- `loading` communicates busy state with `aria-busy` rather than changing the label silently.

| Key                | Action                                                              |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter` or `Space` | Activates the button. Ignored while loading.                        |
| `Tab`              | Moves focus to the button. A loading button stays in the tab order. |
| `Shift` or `Tab`   | Moves focus to the previous control.                                |

---

# SplitButton

> A primary action with a menu of related actions attached. Button plus DropdownMenu.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/split-button

Group: Inputs · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import { SplitButton } from "@azmr/ui/split-button";
import { DropdownMenuItem } from "@azmr/ui/menu";
```

```tsx
"use client";

import { DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuSeparator } from "@azmr/ui/menu";
import { SplitButton } from "@azmr/ui/split-button";
import { useState } from "react";

export default function SplitButtonBasic() {
  const [last, setLast] = useState("Nothing saved yet");
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
      <SplitButton
        menuLabel="More save options"
        onClick={() => setLast("Saved")}
        menu={
          <>
            <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setLast("Saved as a new file")}>
              Save as…
            </DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setLast("Saved a copy")}>Save a copy</DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuSeparator />
            <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setLast("Saved and closed")}>
              Save and close
            </DropdownMenuItem>
          </>
        }
      >
        Save
      </SplitButton>
      <SplitButton
        variant="outline"
        menuLabel="More export options"
        menu={<DropdownMenuItem>PDF</DropdownMenuItem>}
      >
        Export
      </SplitButton>
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground" aria-live="polite">
        {last}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx
<SplitButton
  menuLabel="More save options"
  onClick={save}
  menu={
    <>
      <DropdownMenuItem onClick={saveAs}>Save as…</DropdownMenuItem>
      <DropdownMenuItem onClick={saveCopy}>Save a copy</DropdownMenuItem>
    </>
  }
>
  Save
</SplitButton>
```

The main button runs the common action. The arrow opens a menu of alternatives, so the common case stays one click. `menu` takes any `DropdownMenu` parts: items, separators, groups, even checkbox items.

`menuLabel` is required. The arrow button has no text, so it needs a name ("More save options"), and the types enforce it. The arrow also announces that it opens a menu (`aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`).

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                                                                                                           | Default | Required | Description                                                                    |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `children`    | `ReactNode`                                                                                                                    |         | Yes      | The primary action's label.                                                    |
| `menu`        | `ReactNode`                                                                                                                    |         | Yes      | The extra actions: `DropdownMenuItem`s (and groups, separators, and so on).    |
| `menuLabel`   | `string`                                                                                                                       |         | Yes      | Names the arrow button ("More save options"). Required: the arrow has no text. |
| `variant`     | `"link" \| "default" \| "secondary" \| "outline" \| "ghost" \| "destructive" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "info" \| undefined` |         | No       |                                                                                |
| `size`        | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| undefined`                                                                                            |         | No       |                                                                                |
| `loading`     | `boolean \| undefined`                                                                                                         |         | No       | Shows a spinner on the primary button and ignores it. The menu stays usable.   |
| `loadingText` | `ReactNode`                                                                                                                    |         | No       |                                                                                |
| `startIcon`   | `ReactNode`                                                                                                                    |         | No       |                                                                                |
| `disabled`    | `boolean \| undefined`                                                                                                         |         | No       |                                                                                |
| `className`   | `string`                                                                                                                       |         | No       |                                                                                |

`variant` and `size` apply to both halves, so the pair stays level; filled variants get a divider between them and `outline` shares one border.

- `loading` shows a spinner on the **main button** and ignores it, while the menu stays usable: a slow "Save" should not stop someone choosing "Save as…". `loadingText` and `startIcon` work as on `Button`.
- `disabled` disables **both** halves.

Everything else a `Button` accepts (`onClick`, `type`, `aria-*`) goes to the main button.

## Keyboard

| Key                | Action                                                                     |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`              | Moves to the main button, then to the arrow button.                        |
| `Enter` or `Space` | On the main button: runs the primary action. On the arrow: opens the menu. |
| `ArrowDown`        | On the arrow button: opens the menu on its first item.                     |
| `Escape`           | Closes the menu and returns focus to the arrow button.                     |

Once the menu is open it follows the [DropdownMenu keys](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/menu.md#keyboard).

## Size

The menu is loaded with the split button, so this entry carries the menu's cost (about the same as `@azmr/ui/menu`). If a page only needs a plain `Button`, import that instead.

## Accessibility

- Two real buttons: the primary action, and the arrow that opens the menu. Tab visits both, in that order.
- The arrow has no text, so `menuLabel` is required and the types enforce it. It becomes the arrow's accessible name ("More save options").
- The arrow carries `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`, which changes from `false` to `true` while the menu is open.
- `disabled` disables both halves, and `loading` leaves the menu usable. The menu follows the [DropdownMenu](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/menu.md#accessibility) semantics.
- The component's tests run axe with the menu closed and open.

---

# Input

> A text input whose ref is the real input element, so react-hook-form works without a Controller.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/input

Group: Inputs · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import { Input } from "@azmr/ui/input";
```

```tsx
import { Input } from "@azmr/ui/input";

export default function InputBasic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-sm flex-col gap-2">
      <label htmlFor="demo-input-email" className="text-sm font-medium">
        Email
      </label>
      <Input
        id="demo-input-email"
        type="email"
        placeholder="aroha@example.co.nz"
        autoComplete="email"
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Always pair an input with a visible `<label htmlFor>` (or `aria-label` when the design has no label). `Input` does not add one for you, because the label belongs to the form layout.

## States

```tsx
import { Input } from "@azmr/ui/input";

export default function InputStates() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-sm flex-col gap-4">
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
        <label htmlFor="demo-input-disabled" className="text-sm font-medium">
          Disabled
        </label>
        <Input id="demo-input-disabled" disabled defaultValue="Locked" />
      </div>
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
        <label htmlFor="demo-input-readonly" className="text-sm font-medium">
          Read only
        </label>
        <Input id="demo-input-readonly" readOnly defaultValue="Can focus, cannot edit" />
      </div>
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
        <label htmlFor="demo-input-invalid" className="text-sm font-medium">
          Invalid
        </label>
        <Input
          id="demo-input-invalid"
          aria-invalid="true"
          aria-describedby="demo-input-invalid-message"
          defaultValue="not-an-email"
        />
        <p id="demo-input-invalid-message" className="text-sm text-destructive">
          Enter a valid email address.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`aria-invalid="true"` styles the error state and is what assistive technology announces; point `aria-describedby` at the message so it is read with the field. A read-only input stays focusable and can be selected and copied, while a disabled one is skipped by Tab.

## With react-hook-form

The `ref` is the real `<input>`, so `register()` works directly:

```tsx
import { useForm } from "react-hook-form";
import { Input } from "@azmr/ui/input";

function EmailField() {
  const { register } = useForm<{ email: string }>();
  return <Input type="email" {...register("email")} />;
}
```

Native `onChange` and a typed `onValueChange(value)` both fire.

## Props

| Prop            | Type                                                                             | Default | Required | Description                                                   |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `className`     | `string`                                                                         |         | No       |                                                               |
| `value`         | `string \| number \| readonly string[] \| undefined`                             |         | No       | The value of the input. Use when controlled.                  |
| `defaultValue`  | `string \| number \| readonly string[] \| undefined`                             |         | No       | The default value of the input. Use when uncontrolled.        |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string, eventDetails: Input.ChangeEventDetails) => void) \| undefined` |         | No       | Callback fired when the `value` changes. Use when controlled. |

All native `<input>` attributes pass through. `className` is merged last, so it can override the defaults, and `onValueChange` gives you the new value directly instead of `event.target.value`.

Height and horizontal padding follow the density tokens, so the input lines up with `Button` at every density.

## Accessibility

- A real `<input>`: name, role and value come from the platform.
- The focus ring is full strength (WCAG 2.2 focus appearance), never faded.
- Invalid state is exposed through `aria-invalid`, not colour alone: pair it with a text message.

| Key              | Action                                                              |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`            | Moves focus into and out of the field. Disabled inputs are skipped. |
| `Shift` or `Tab` | Moves focus to the previous control.                                |
| `Esc`            | Not captured, so a parent dialog can use it to close.               |

---

# Toggle

> Toggle and ToggleGroup. A button that stays pressed, and a group of them that acts as one control with arrow-key navigation. Built on Base UI.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/toggle

Group: Inputs · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import { Toggle, ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@azmr/ui/toggle";
```

These are interactive, so they are client components.

## Toggle

```tsx
import { Toggle } from "@azmr/ui/toggle";
import { Bold, Italic } from "lucide-react";

export default function ToggleBasic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Toggle aria-label="Bold" size="icon">
        <Bold className="size-4" />
      </Toggle>
      <Toggle aria-label="Italic" size="icon" variant="outline" defaultPressed>
        <Italic className="size-4" />
      </Toggle>
      <Toggle variant="outline">Notify me</Toggle>
    </div>
  );
}
```

A button that is either pressed or not, exposed as `aria-pressed`. Use `pressed` and `onPressedChange` to control it, or `defaultPressed` to start on. `variant` is `default` or `outline`, `size` is `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

An icon-only toggle (`size="icon"`) has no text, so it needs an accessible name: the types require `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

Use a toggle for a state that is **on or off right now** (bold, mute, show grid). For a setting that is saved with a form, use a switch or checkbox instead.

## ToggleGroup

```tsx
"use client";

import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@azmr/ui/toggle";
import { AlignCenter, AlignLeft, AlignRight, Bold, Italic, Underline } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";

export default function ToggleGroupBasic() {
  const [align, setAlign] = useState<string[]>(["left"]);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-4">
      {/* One at a time (the default). The value is always an array. */}
      <ToggleGroup
        aria-label="Text alignment"
        variant="outline"
        value={align}
        onValueChange={(v) => setAlign(v as string[])}
      >
        <ToggleGroupItem value="left" size="icon" aria-label="Align left">
          <AlignLeft className="size-4" />
        </ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="center" size="icon" aria-label="Align centre">
          <AlignCenter className="size-4" />
        </ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="right" size="icon" aria-label="Align right">
          <AlignRight className="size-4" />
        </ToggleGroupItem>
      </ToggleGroup>
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground" aria-live="polite">
        Aligned: {align[0] ?? "nothing"}
      </p>

      {/* Any number at once. */}
      <ToggleGroup aria-label="Text style" variant="outline" multiple defaultValue={["bold"]}>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="bold" size="icon" aria-label="Bold">
          <Bold className="size-4" />
        </ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="italic" size="icon" aria-label="Italic">
          <Italic className="size-4" />
        </ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="underline" size="icon" aria-label="Underline">
          <Underline className="size-4" />
        </ToggleGroupItem>
      </ToggleGroup>
    </div>
  );
}
```

A named group (`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is required) of toggles that behaves as **one control**:

- By default **one item can be pressed at a time**. Pressing the pressed one releases it, so nothing selected is allowed. With `multiple`, any number can be pressed.
- The value is **always an array** of the pressed items' `value`s, even in single mode. Use `value` and `onValueChange` (or `defaultValue`) to control it.
- `variant` and `size` on the group apply to every item unless an item sets its own.
- The items are joined into one control; `attached={false}` keeps them apart, and `orientation="vertical"` stacks them.

## Keyboard

| Key                         | Action                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`                       | Enters the group at a single tab stop, then moves on. Only one item is in the tab order at a time (roving tabindex).      |
| `ArrowRight` or `ArrowLeft` | Moves focus to the next or previous item and wraps (ArrowDown and ArrowUp when vertical). It never changes the selection. |
| `Home` or `End`             | Moves focus to the first or last item.                                                                                    |
| `Space` or `Enter`          | Presses or releases the focused item.                                                                                     |

Disabled items are skipped by the arrow keys, which differs from menus (where disabled items stay focusable).

## Accessibility

- Each item is a real button with `aria-pressed`; the group is `role="group"` with the name you give it.
- The pressed state is shown by background and text colour from tokens, not by colour alone: it is also in `aria-pressed`, so screen readers announce "pressed".
- Focus uses the standard full-strength ring.

## Props

| Prop        | Type                                          | Default | Required | Description                                                               |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `className` | `string`                                      |         | No       |                                                                           |
| `variant`   | `"default" \| "outline" \| undefined`         |         | No       | Applied to every item unless it sets its own.                             |
| `size`      | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "icon" \| undefined` |         | No       |                                                                           |
| `attached`  | `boolean \| undefined`                        |         | No       | Join the items into one control (default), or keep them apart with a gap. |

---

# Display

> Card, Badge, Alert, Skeleton and EmptyState. Server Components with status colours checked for contrast in both themes.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/display

Group: Data display · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import { Card, Badge, Alert, Skeleton, EmptyState } from "@azmr/ui/display";
```

All of these are **Server Components**: no hooks, no `"use client"`.

## Card and Badge

```tsx
import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import {
  Badge,
  Card,
  CardContent,
  CardDescription,
  CardFooter,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
} from "@azmr/ui/display";

export default function DisplayCards() {
  return (
    <Card className="max-w-sm">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Business plan</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>
          <Badge variant="success">Active</Badge> Renews on 1 November
        </CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent className="text-sm">
        Up to 25 users, priority support and audit logs.
      </CardContent>
      <CardFooter className="gap-2">
        <Button size="sm">Manage plan</Button>
        <Button size="sm" variant="ghost">
          View invoices
        </Button>
      </CardFooter>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

A `Card` is a bordered surface from tokens, with `CardHeader`, `CardTitle` (an `h3` by default; pass `as` to fit your outline), `CardDescription`, `CardContent` and `CardFooter`. A `Badge` is a small label for status or a count, with the semantic variants `info`, `success`, `warning` and `destructive`.

## Chip

```tsx
"use client";

import { Chip } from "@azmr/ui/display";
import { useState } from "react";

export default function DisplayChips() {
  const [tags, setTags] = useState(["React", "Accessibility", "Tailwind", "Base UI"]);

  // The Chip does not hide itself: you own the list.
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      {tags.map((tag) => (
        <Chip
          key={tag}
          variant="secondary"
          onRemove={() => setTags((all) => all.filter((t) => t !== tag))}
        >
          {tag}
        </Chip>
      ))}
      {tags.length === 0 && <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">No tags left.</span>}
    </div>
  );
}
```

A `Chip` is a Badge that can be removed: a selected filter, a tag. `onRemove` adds a button named `Remove <label>` (`removeLabel` for non-text content or another language), reachable and operable with Tab, Enter and Space. The Chip does not hide itself; you own the list.

## Alert

```tsx
"use client";

import { Alert, AlertDescription, AlertTitle } from "@azmr/ui/display";
import { useState } from "react";

export default function DisplayAlerts() {
  const [dismissed, setDismissed] = useState(false);

  return (
    <div className="flex max-w-xl flex-col gap-3">
      <Alert variant="info">
        <AlertTitle>Heads up</AlertTitle>
        <AlertDescription>Your trial ends in 3 days.</AlertDescription>
      </Alert>
      <Alert variant="success">
        <AlertTitle>Saved</AlertTitle>
        <AlertDescription>Your changes are live.</AlertDescription>
      </Alert>
      <Alert variant="warning">
        <AlertTitle>Plan renews tomorrow</AlertTitle>
        <AlertDescription>Update your card to avoid an interruption.</AlertDescription>
      </Alert>
      {/* The Alert does not hide itself: you own that state. */}
      {!dismissed && (
        <Alert variant="destructive" onDismiss={() => setDismissed(true)}>
          <AlertTitle>Payment failed</AlertTitle>
          <AlertDescription>We could not charge the card on file.</AlertDescription>
        </Alert>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

Problems (`warning`, `destructive`) are announced assertively with `role="alert"`; `info` and `success` politely with `role="status"`, so a screen reader is not interrupted for good news. An icon is shown per variant (replace it with `icon`, remove it with `icon={null}`). `onDismiss` adds a labelled dismiss button (`dismissLabel` to localise it); the Alert does not hide itself, so you own that state. The dismiss handler works when the Alert is rendered from a Client Component.

## Badge, Skeleton and EmptyState

```tsx
import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { Badge, EmptyState, Skeleton } from "@azmr/ui/display";
import { Icon } from "@azmr/ui/icons";
import { Inbox } from "lucide-react";

export default function DisplayPlaceholders() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-8">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Badge>Default</Badge>
        <Badge variant="secondary">Secondary</Badge>
        <Badge variant="outline">Outline</Badge>
        <Badge variant="info">Info</Badge>
        <Badge variant="success">Success</Badge>
        <Badge variant="warning">Warning</Badge>
        <Badge variant="destructive">Destructive</Badge>
      </div>

      {/* Mark the loading container aria-busy; the skeleton itself is decorative. */}
      <div aria-busy="true" className="flex max-w-xs items-center gap-3">
        <Skeleton className="size-10 rounded-full" />
        <div className="flex flex-1 flex-col gap-2">
          <Skeleton className="h-3 w-3/4" />
          <Skeleton className="h-3 w-1/2" />
        </div>
      </div>

      <EmptyState
        icon={<Icon icon={Inbox} size="xl" />}
        title="No messages yet"
        description="When customers write to you, their messages will appear here."
        action={<Button size="sm">Compose a message</Button>}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

- **`Skeleton`** is a decorative placeholder (`aria-hidden`). Mark the loading container `aria-busy` and announce the result instead. It pulses, and the global reduced-motion rule stills it for people who ask.
- **`EmptyState`** says what is missing and what to do about it: a title, optional description, icon and action, with a heading level (`headingLevel`) that fits your page outline.

## Status colours are checked

Alerts and badges paint a tint of a status colour over the page and put text on it. The test suite computes the contrast on the **blended surface**, in light and dark, over both the page and a card, from the same class names the components use: body text at 4.5:1 or better, badge text at 4.5:1, icons at 3:1. This caught a real failure while the components were being built (the destructive badge was 4.26:1 on a dark card), so its tint is lighter than first designed.

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                                             | Default | Required | Description                                                                                |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `variant`      | `"info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "destructive" \| undefined` |         | No       |                                                                                            |
| `icon`         | `ReactNode`                                                      |         | No       | Replaces the default icon; `null` removes it.                                              |
| `onDismiss`    | `(() => void) \| undefined`                                      |         | No       | Adds a dismiss button that calls this. The Alert does not hide itself: you own that state. |
| `dismissLabel` | `string`                                                         |         | No       | The accessible name of the dismiss button. Default "Dismiss".                              |

## Accessibility

- Alerts use `role="alert"` or `role="status"` according to urgency; the icon is decorative and the text carries the meaning, so colour is never the only signal.
- The dismiss button is a real button with an accessible name, reachable and operable with Tab, Enter and Space.
- Skeletons are hidden from assistive technology; use `aria-busy` on the container.

| Key                | Action                                                      |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`              | Moves focus to the dismiss button of an Alert that has one. |
| `Enter` or `Space` | Dismisses the Alert (calls onDismiss).                      |

---

# Table

> A semantic, non-interactive table with a caption, sticky header, striping and a named scroll region. Server-safe.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/table

Group: Data display · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Table, TableCaption, TableHeader, TableBody, TableFooter, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell,
} from "@azmr/ui/table";
```

```tsx
import {
  Table,
  TableBody,
  TableCaption,
  TableCell,
  TableFooter,
  TableHead,
  TableHeader,
  TableRow,
} from "@azmr/ui/table";

const invoices = [
  { id: "INV-001", status: "Paid", amount: 250 },
  { id: "INV-002", status: "Pending", amount: 1250 },
  { id: "INV-003", status: "Paid", amount: 480.5 },
  { id: "INV-004", status: "Overdue", amount: 90 },
];

const nzd = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-NZ", { style: "currency", currency: "NZD" });

export default function TableBasic() {
  const total = invoices.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.amount, 0);
  return (
    <Table striped hoverable className="max-w-xl">
      <TableCaption>Invoices for October</TableCaption>
      <TableHeader>
        <TableRow>
          <TableHead>Invoice</TableHead>
          <TableHead>Status</TableHead>
          <TableHead align="right">Amount</TableHead>
        </TableRow>
      </TableHeader>
      <TableBody>
        {invoices.map((invoice) => (
          <TableRow key={invoice.id}>
            <TableHead scope="row" className="font-normal text-foreground">
              {invoice.id}
            </TableHead>
            <TableCell>{invoice.status}</TableCell>
            <TableCell numeric>{nzd.format(invoice.amount)}</TableCell>
          </TableRow>
        ))}
      </TableBody>
      <TableFooter>
        <TableRow>
          <TableCell colSpan={2}>Total</TableCell>
          <TableCell numeric>{nzd.format(total)}</TableCell>
        </TableRow>
      </TableFooter>
    </Table>
  );
}
```

`Table` is a native `<table>`, so it already has the table, row and column roles with no ARIA added. It is a Server Component: no hooks, no `"use client"`. It replaces hand-built `Table*` markup (for example MUI's `TableCell`) with the same structure and sensible styling from tokens.

Name every table with a `TableCaption`. Use `srOnly` to keep it for assistive technology and hide it visually.

## Header cells

`TableHead` is a `<th>`. It defaults to `scope="col"`. For the first cell of a row (a row header), pass `scope="row"`, as in the demo, so a screen reader announces the row's name with each value. Put `aria-sort` on a header cell when the column is sorted.

## Numbers and alignment

`TableCell numeric` right-aligns and uses tabular figures, so a column of amounts lines up. `align` (`left`, `center`, `right`) works on both `TableHead` and `TableCell`: align a numeric column's header the same way as its cells.

## Scrolling and the sticky header

```tsx
import {
  Table,
  TableBody,
  TableCaption,
  TableCell,
  TableHead,
  TableHeader,
  TableRow,
} from "@azmr/ui/table";

const rows = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, i) => ({
  id: `CUST-${String(i + 1).padStart(3, "0")}`,
  name: ["Aroha Ngata", "Tane Walker", "Mere Parata", "Hemi Rangi"][i % 4],
  city: ["Hamilton", "Auckland", "Wellington", "Dunedin"][i % 4],
  orders: (i * 7) % 31,
}));

export default function TableSticky() {
  return (
    <Table
      label="Customers (scrollable)"
      stickyHeader
      hoverable
      containerClassName="max-h-64 max-w-xl rounded-md border border-border"
    >
      <TableCaption srOnly>Customers, with their city and order count</TableCaption>
      <TableHeader>
        <TableRow>
          <TableHead>ID</TableHead>
          <TableHead>Name</TableHead>
          <TableHead>City</TableHead>
          <TableHead align="right">Orders</TableHead>
        </TableRow>
      </TableHeader>
      <TableBody>
        {rows.map((r) => (
          <TableRow key={r.id}>
            <TableCell>{r.id}</TableCell>
            <TableCell>{r.name}</TableCell>
            <TableCell>{r.city}</TableCell>
            <TableCell numeric>{r.orders}</TableCell>
          </TableRow>
        ))}
      </TableBody>
    </Table>
  );
}
```

A table wider than its space scrolls **inside its own container**, so it never breaks the page. Give the table a `label` and the container becomes a named, focusable region, so a keyboard user can scroll it with the arrow keys. Do this for any table that may overflow.

`stickyHeader` keeps the header row in view while the body scrolls; give the container a height with `containerClassName` (such as `max-h-64`). The header cells sit on an opaque background, so rows slide cleanly beneath them.

## Striped, hoverable, selected

`striped` tints every other body row and `hoverable` tints the row under the pointer. `TableRow selected` marks a row with `data-selected` and tints it. These are styling only: a hover tint is not interactive, and a selected row is not announced as selected unless you also make it a control (for example with a checkbox in the row).

Rows follow the density token (`--density-row-height`), so a table grows or shrinks with `data-density`.

## Not a data grid

This is a presentational table. Sorting, filtering, selection, virtualised rows and editing belong to the data grid (Phase 4), which builds on this.

## Props

| Prop                 | Type                   | Default | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------- | ---------------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`              | `string`               |         | No       | Names the scrolling container. When set it becomes a labelled, focusable region, so a keyboard user can scroll a table that is wider than its space. Give a wide table a label. |
| `containerClassName` | `string`               |         | No       | Classes for the scrolling container, such as a `max-h-96` so the table scrolls vertically.                                                                                      |
| `stickyHeader`       | `boolean \| undefined` |         | No       | Keep the header row in view while the body scrolls. Give the container a height.                                                                                                |
| `striped`            | `boolean \| undefined` |         | No       | Tint every other body row.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `hoverable`          | `boolean \| undefined` |         | No       | Tint the row under the pointer.                                                                                                                                                 |

## Accessibility

- Native table semantics: `table`, `rowgroup`, `row`, `columnheader`, `rowheader`, `cell`. Nothing is overridden.
- A caption names the table; row headers use `scope="row"`.
- The scroll container, when labelled, is a `region` with a tab stop and a full-strength focus ring.
- Striping and hover tints are never the only way information is conveyed.

| Key                                                     | Action                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`                                                   | Moves to the scroll region when the table has a label. Nothing else in a static table is focusable. |
| `ArrowDown` or `ArrowUp` or `ArrowRight` or `ArrowLeft` | Scrolls a focused, labelled region.                                                                 |
| `PageDown` or `PageUp` or `Home` or `End`               | Scrolls by a page, or to the start or end.                                                          |

---

# Avatar

> A person or entity as an image with initials as the fallback, plus a group with a labelled overflow count. Built on Base UI.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/avatar

Group: Data display · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from "@azmr/ui/avatar";
```

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from "@azmr/ui/avatar";

const team = ["Aroha Ngata", "Mere Walker", "Hemi Te Rangi", "Tane Smith", "Rangi Bell"];

export default function AvatarBasic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-6">
      <div className="flex items-end gap-3">
        <Avatar name="Aroha Ngata" size="sm" />
        <Avatar name="Aroha Ngata" />
        <Avatar name="Aroha Ngata" size="lg" />
        <Avatar name="Aroha Ngata" size="xl" shape="square" />
      </div>

      {/* An image that cannot load falls back to the initials, still labelled. */}
      <Avatar src="/does-not-exist.png" name="Mere Walker" />

      <AvatarGroup max={3} aria-label="Project team">
        {team.map((person) => (
          <Avatar key={person} name={person} />
        ))}
      </AvatarGroup>
    </div>
  );
}
```

When `src` is missing, still loading, or fails (offline, a 404), the **initials of `name`** are shown instead, so an avatar never turns into a broken-image icon. `getInitials` is exported: the first character of the first two words, uppercased, counting whole characters so an emoji or a rare character is never cut in half. Pass `fallback` to show something else, and `delayMs` to avoid a flash of initials while a fast image loads.

## Naming

An avatar must say who it is, so the types require one of `name`, `alt` or `decorative`:

- `name` labels the avatar and supplies the initials. `alt` overrides the label ("Aroha, account owner").
- `decorative` hides it from assistive technology, for an avatar beside a name that already says who it is.

The avatar element carries the label; the image inside is `alt=""` so it is not announced twice.

## AvatarGroup

`AvatarGroup` overlaps its avatars and shows at most `max`, then a `+N` avatar labelled "N more" (`overflowLabel` to localise). It is a `role="group"`: give it an `aria-label` ("Project team").

## Props

| Prop            | Type                                        | Default | Required | Description                                               |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `max`           | `number`                                    |         | No       | Show at most this many avatars, then a `+N` for the rest. |
| `overflowLabel` | `((hidden: number) => string) \| undefined` |         | No       | The accessible name of the `+N` avatar. Default `N more`. |
| `children`      | `ReactNode`                                 |         | No       |                                                           |

## Accessibility

- `role="img"` with the name as its label, or `aria-hidden` when decorative.
- The overflow avatar says how many people are hidden.
- No keyboard interaction; put an avatar inside a button or link when it should be interactive, and give that control the name.

---

# Typography

> A type scale where the variant picks the semantic element, with Heading, Text, Link, Code and Kbd. All Server Components.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/typography

Group: Data display · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import { Typography, Heading, Text, Link, Code, Kbd } from "@azmr/ui/typography";
```

```tsx
import { Typography } from "@azmr/ui/typography";

export default function TypographyScale() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      <Typography variant="overline">Overline</Typography>
      <Typography variant="h1">Heading 1</Typography>
      <Typography variant="h2">Heading 2</Typography>
      <Typography variant="h3">Heading 3</Typography>
      <Typography variant="h4">Heading 4</Typography>
      <Typography variant="h5">Heading 5</Typography>
      <Typography variant="h6">Heading 6</Typography>
      <Typography variant="lead">A lead paragraph introduces the page.</Typography>
      <Typography>Body text is the default variant and renders a paragraph.</Typography>
      <Typography variant="small">Small text for secondary detail.</Typography>
      <Typography variant="caption">Caption text</Typography>
    </div>
  );
}
```

A `variant` chooses a step on the type scale **and** the semantic element: `h1` to `h6` render real headings, `lead`, `body` and `small` render paragraphs, `caption` and `overline` render spans. Colours are tokens only, so the whole scale follows the theme. Pass `as` to render a different element without changing the look: `<Typography variant="h1" as="h2">` is a visually large `<h2>`.

Everything here is a **Server Component**: no hooks, no `"use client"`, safe in layouts and `loading.tsx`.

## Heading, Text, Link, Code and Kbd

```tsx
import { Code, Heading, Kbd, Link, Text } from "@azmr/ui/typography";

export default function TypographyInline() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
      {/* The level is the document outline; the size is the look. They are separate decisions. */}
      <Heading level={2} size="h4">
        A quiet section heading
      </Heading>
      <Text>
        Press <Kbd>Enter</Kbd> to open a record, or run <Code>pnpm dev</Code> to start. Read the{" "}
        <Link href="/docs/components">components guide</Link> or visit{" "}
        <Link href="https://base-ui.com" external>
          Base UI
        </Link>
        .
      </Text>
      <Text tone="muted" size="sm">
        Muted, small text for secondary information.
      </Text>
      <Text tone="destructive" weight="medium">
        Something needs your attention.
      </Text>
    </div>
  );
}
```

- **`Heading`** separates the semantic `level` from the visual `size`, so you can keep the document outline correct and still choose how loud a heading looks.
- **`Text`** is running text, a paragraph by default. `tone` uses semantic tokens (`muted`, `destructive`, `success`, `warning`, `info`); `size` and `weight` adjust it.
- **`Link`** is underlined by default, so links are distinguishable without relying on colour alone, and has a full-strength focus ring. `external` adds `target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and a screen-reader-only "(opens in a new tab)". To use your router's link, pass it as `as`: `<Link as={NextLink} href="/x">`.
- **`Code`** and **`Kbd`** are inline code and a keyboard key, styled from tokens.

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                                                                                                  | Default | Required | Description                                                                      |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`      | `"h1" \| "h2" \| "h3" \| "h4" \| "h5" \| "h6" \| "lead" \| "body" \| "small" \| "caption" \| "overline" \| undefined` |         | No       | The type-scale step. It picks the semantic element and the look. Default `body`. |
| `align`        | `"left" \| "center" \| "right" \| "justify" \| undefined`                                                             |         | No       |                                                                                  |
| `noWrap`       | `boolean \| undefined`                                                                                                |         | No       | Truncate to one line with an ellipsis.                                           |
| `gutterBottom` | `boolean \| undefined`                                                                                                |         | No       | Add a small bottom margin (MUI's `gutterBottom`).                                |

Everything else a native element accepts passes through, and `ref` is the rendered element.

## Migrating from MUI Typography

`@azmr/ui/typography/mui-map` is plain data the migration codemod uses. Exact mappings are rewritten; approximate ones (a small difference in weight, case or colour) are flagged for a person to look at.

| MUI `variant`           | `@azmr/ui`            | Note                                                                                 |
| ----------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `h1` to `h6`            | `h1` to `h6`          | exact                                                                                |
| `subtitle1`             | `lead`                | `lead` is muted; add `className="text-foreground"` for MUI's colour                  |
| `subtitle2`             | `small`               | MUI is medium weight: add `weight="medium"` on `Text`                                |
| `body1` (MUI's default) | `body`                | exact                                                                                |
| `body2`                 | `small`               | exact                                                                                |
| `caption`, `overline`   | `caption`, `overline` | ours are muted; add `className="text-foreground"` for MUI's colour                   |
| `button`                | `small`               | MUI is uppercase medium: add `weight="medium"` and `className="uppercase"`           |
| `inherit`               | `body`                | takes the parent's font in MUI; use `className="text-inherit"` if that is the intent |

Props: `component` becomes `as`; `gutterBottom`, `noWrap` and `align` keep their names; `paragraph` becomes a `Text`; `color` becomes `tone` or a `text-*` class; `sx` becomes `className`.

## Accessibility

- Variants render the right semantic element, so headings form a real outline for assistive technology.
- Keep one `h1` per page and do not skip levels; use `Heading`'s `size` when you want a different look at the right level.
- Links are underlined by default and external links announce that they open a new tab.
- There is no keyboard interaction beyond native links; `Kbd` only documents shortcuts and does not bind them.

---

# Icon

> Renders Lucide, Tabler or your own SVG with consistent size, stroke, motion and accessibility. A Server Component.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/icon

Group: Data display · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import { Icon } from "@azmr/ui/icons";
import { Search } from "lucide-react";

<Icon icon={Search} />
```

```tsx
import { Icon } from "@azmr/ui/icons";
import { Bell, LoaderCircle, Search } from "lucide-react";

export default function IconBasic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
      <div className="flex items-end gap-4">
        <Icon icon={Search} size="xs" />
        <Icon icon={Search} size="sm" />
        <Icon icon={Search} size="md" />
        <Icon icon={Search} size="lg" />
        <Icon icon={Search} size="xl" />
        <Icon icon={Search} size={40} />
      </div>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
        {/* Decorative by default; aria-label makes it a labelled image. */}
        <Icon icon={Bell} aria-label="Notifications" size="lg" />
        <Icon icon={Bell} size="lg" strokeWidth={1} />
        <Icon icon={Bell} size="lg" strokeWidth={2.5} />
        {/* spin keeps moving under reduced motion: a frozen loader reads as a hung page. */}
        <Icon icon={LoaderCircle} size="lg" spin aria-label="Loading" />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`Icon` takes the icon component you pass it, so only the icons you import are bundled (this is tested). Lucide is the default set; Tabler and your own SVG components work through the same `icon` prop with no adapter. Sizes `xs` to `xl` follow the size tokens, and a number is a pixel size.

An icon is **decorative by default** (`aria-hidden`). Give it `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` to make it a labelled image. `spin` is for loaders and, like `Spinner`, keeps moving under reduced motion.

## By name

```tsx
import { Icon } from "@azmr/ui/icons/lucide";

export default function IconNamed() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
      <Icon name="house" size="lg" />
      <Icon name="circle-alert" size="lg" aria-label="Warning" />
      <Icon name="trash-2" size="lg" aria-label="Delete" />
      <Icon name="chevrons-up-down" size="lg" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

The curated set at `@azmr/ui/icons/lucide` gives about 60 everyday icons by Lucide's own kebab-case names, with the names type-checked. For your own typed set use `createIconSet`, and for custom SVGs `registerIcons`:

```tsx
import { createIconSet, registerIcons } from "@azmr/ui/icons";

export const { Icon } = createIconSet({ check: Check, "my-logo": MyLogo });

registerIcons({ "my-logo": MyLogo }); // global, untyped names: <Icon name="my-logo" />
```

An unknown name renders nothing and warns once in development; it never crashes a page.

## Props

| Prop              | Type                                                          | Default | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `icon`            | `IconComponent \| undefined`                                  |         | No       | The icon to render: a Lucide or Tabler icon, or your own SVG component.                                                                                     |
| `name`            | `string`                                                      |         | No       | Looks the icon up in the registry (`registerIcons`). `icon` wins when both are given.                                                                       |
| `size`            | `number \| "xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| undefined` |         | No       | `xs` .. `xl` follow the size tokens; a number is a pixel size. Default `md`.                                                                                |
| `spin`            | `boolean \| undefined`                                        |         | No       | Turns the icon into a loading indicator. It keeps spinning under reduced motion.                                                                            |
| `strokeWidth`     | `string \| number \| undefined`                               |         | No       |                                                                                                                                                             |
| `aria-label`      | `string`                                                      |         | No       | Decorative by default (`aria-hidden`). Give `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` to make the icon meaningful: it then has `role="img"` and an accessible name. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string`                                                      |         | No       | Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.                                                                                       |
| `className`       | `string`                                                      |         | No       |                                                                                                                                                             |

Any other SVG attribute passes through. `className` is merged last, so `size-8` replaces the size token.

## Migrating from Material icons

`@azmr/ui/icons/mui-map` maps over 300 `@mui/icons-material` names (including the `Outlined`, `Rounded`, `Sharp` and `TwoTone` variants) to Lucide and Tabler, and lists the common ones it deliberately does not map. The migration codemod uses it.

## Accessibility

- Decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology; meaningful ones are `role="img"` with a name.
- An icon-only button is named by the labelled icon inside it, or by the button's own `aria-label`.
- Licences: Lucide is ISC, Tabler is MIT. `react-icons` is deliberately not bundled.

---

# Disclosure

> Accordion, Collapsible and Tabs. Show and hide content with the keyboard maps users expect. Built on Base UI.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/disclosure

Group: Data display · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionContent,
  Collapsible, CollapsibleTrigger, CollapsibleContent,
  Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent,
} from "@azmr/ui/disclosure";
```

These are interactive, so they are client components: import them from a file (or a tree) that is already `"use client"`, or use them from a client page.

## Collapsible

One region that shows and hides. Use it for a single "show more".

```tsx
import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger } from "@azmr/ui/disclosure";

export default function CollapsibleBasic() {
  return (
    <Collapsible className="max-w-md">
      <CollapsibleTrigger render={<Button variant="outline">Show advanced options</Button>} />
      <CollapsibleContent className="pt-3 text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        Advanced options live here. The panel animates its height and is instant when the visitor
        prefers reduced motion.
      </CollapsibleContent>
    </Collapsible>
  );
}
```

The trigger is a real `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. Pass `render={<Button … />}` to use your own element.

## Accordion

A stack of collapsible sections. One section is open at a time; add `multiple` to allow several.

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger } from "@azmr/ui/disclosure";

export default function AccordionBasic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-lg flex-col gap-8">
      <Accordion defaultValue={["billing"]} aria-label="Billing questions">
        <AccordionItem value="billing">
          <AccordionTrigger>How does billing work?</AccordionTrigger>
          <AccordionContent>
            You are billed monthly in NZD. Invoices are emailed on the first of each month.
          </AccordionContent>
        </AccordionItem>
        <AccordionItem value="cancel">
          <AccordionTrigger>Can I cancel at any time?</AccordionTrigger>
          <AccordionContent>
            Yes. Your plan runs to the end of the period you paid for.
          </AccordionContent>
        </AccordionItem>
        <AccordionItem value="legacy" disabled>
          <AccordionTrigger>Legacy plans (unavailable)</AccordionTrigger>
          <AccordionContent>Not shown.</AccordionContent>
        </AccordionItem>
      </Accordion>

      {/* `multiple` lets several sections stay open at once. */}
      <Accordion multiple defaultValue={["a", "b"]} aria-label="Release notes">
        <AccordionItem value="a">
          <AccordionTrigger headingLevel={4}>New</AccordionTrigger>
          <AccordionContent>Tabs, accordion and collapsible.</AccordionContent>
        </AccordionItem>
        <AccordionItem value="b">
          <AccordionTrigger headingLevel={4}>Fixed</AccordionTrigger>
          <AccordionContent>Scoped themes now work when light-dark() is lowered.</AccordionContent>
        </AccordionItem>
      </Accordion>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Each trigger sits inside a heading so assistive technology can list the sections. It defaults to an `<h3>`: set `headingLevel` to fit the page outline. `defaultValue` (uncontrolled) or `value` and `onValueChange` (controlled) take an array of item values, even when only one can be open.

## Tabs

```tsx
import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from "@azmr/ui/disclosure";

export default function TabsBasic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-lg flex-col gap-8">
      <Tabs defaultValue="overview">
        <TabsList aria-label="Account sections">
          <TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value="billing">Billing</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value="team" disabled>
            Team
          </TabsTrigger>
        </TabsList>
        <TabsContent value="overview" className="p-2 text-sm">
          A summary of your account.
        </TabsContent>
        <TabsContent value="billing" className="p-2 text-sm">
          Invoices and payment methods.
        </TabsContent>
        <TabsContent value="team" className="p-2 text-sm">
          Not available on your plan.
        </TabsContent>
      </Tabs>

      <Tabs defaultValue="profile" orientation="vertical">
        <TabsList aria-label="Settings">
          <TabsTrigger value="profile">Profile</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value="security">Security</TabsTrigger>
        </TabsList>
        <TabsContent value="profile" className="p-2 text-sm">
          Name, photo and contact details.
        </TabsContent>
        <TabsContent value="security" className="p-2 text-sm">
          Password and two-factor sign-in.
        </TabsContent>
      </Tabs>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Give the `TabsList` an accessible name with `aria-label`. Tabs are selected **manually** by default: arrows move focus, Enter or Space selects. That is the safer default when a panel is expensive to render or load. Add `activateOnFocus` to `TabsList` to select as you arrow. Disabled tabs stay focusable (and are announced as disabled) so people can discover them; they cannot be selected.

Panels are focusable (`tabindex="0"`), so a keyboard user can reach and scroll a panel that has no controls in it. Only the selected panel is in the DOM unless you pass `keepMounted`.

### Keep the tab in the URL

`useUrlTab` stores the selected tab in a search parameter, so a tab can be linked to and reloaded, and Back restores it.

```tsx
"use client";

import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from "@azmr/ui/disclosure";
import { useUrlTab } from "@azmr/ui/hooks";

const VALUES = ["usage", "api"] as const;

export default function TabsUrl() {
  const [tab, setTab] = useUrlTab({ param: "demo-tab", values: VALUES, defaultValue: "usage" });
  return (
    <Tabs value={tab} onValueChange={(next) => setTab(next as (typeof VALUES)[number])}>
      <TabsList aria-label="Example">
        <TabsTrigger value="usage">Usage</TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="api">API</TabsTrigger>
      </TabsList>
      <TabsContent value="usage" className="p-2 text-sm">
        Select API, then look at the address bar: <code>?demo-tab=api</code>. Reload, or press Back.
      </TabsContent>
      <TabsContent value="api" className="p-2 text-sm">
        The tab is in the URL, so it can be linked to.
      </TabsContent>
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

```tsx
const [tab, setTab] = useUrlTab({ values: ["usage", "api"], defaultValue: "usage" });
<Tabs value={tab} onValueChange={(v) => setTab(v as typeof tab)}>…</Tabs>
```

- The URL is untrusted input. A value that is not in `values` is ignored and the default is used.
- The default tab has no parameter, so URLs stay clean. Other parameters and the hash are kept.
- `history: "replace"` (default) rewrites the current entry. Use `"push"` if each tab should be a Back step.
- On the server and during hydration it returns the default, so there is no mismatch.
- It is router-agnostic: it reads and writes `window.location` and the History API. In a framework with its own router you can drive `Tabs` from that router's search params instead.

## Motion

Accordion and Collapsible panels animate their **height**. Base UI measures the panel and exposes `--accordion-panel-height` (or `--collapsible-panel-height`); the styles transition from `0` to that height with `--motion-duration-base`. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` those tokens collapse to near zero, so panels open and close instantly.

The original plan was a `grid-template-rows` trick with no JavaScript measuring. Base UI already measures the panel to keep `hidden` and `aria-expanded` correct, and a second mechanism fighting it is how animations get stuck, so the shipped components use Base UI's own height variable.

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                      | Default | Required | Description                                                                 |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `headingLevel` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6 \| undefined` |         | No       | The heading level wrapping the trigger, to fit the page outline. Default 3. |
| `className`    | `string`                                  |         | No       |                                                                             |

The rest are Base UI's props, passed through. `className` on `AccordionContent` and `CollapsibleContent` styles an inner wrapper, so padding never fights the height animation.

## Accessibility

- Accordion triggers are buttons in headings with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.
- Tabs follow the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: `tablist`, `tab` with `aria-selected`, `tabpanel` with `aria-labelledby`, and a roving tab stop.
- Focus rings are full strength.
- Chevron icons are decorative (`aria-hidden`).

### Accordion keys

| Key                      | Action                                                                            |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`                    | Moves to the next trigger (or the first focusable element in an open panel).      |
| `Enter` or `Space`       | Opens or closes the focused section.                                              |
| `ArrowDown` or `ArrowUp` | Moves focus to the next or previous trigger and wraps. It does not open anything. |
| `Home` or `End`          | Moves focus to the first or last trigger.                                         |

Base UI 1.9 declares `loopFocus` but does not implement arrow navigation for the accordion, so `@azmr/ui` adds it. Keys pressed inside a panel (in a text field, say) are never taken, and a nested accordion handles its own keys.

### Tabs keys

| Key                         | Action                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`                       | Enters the tab list at the selected tab, then moves on to the panel.      |
| `ArrowRight` or `ArrowLeft` | Moves focus between tabs and wraps (ArrowDown and ArrowUp when vertical). |
| `Home` or `End`             | Moves focus to the first or last tab.                                     |
| `Enter` or `Space`          | Selects the focused tab (not needed with activateOnFocus).                |

---

# Progress

> A linear or circular progress indicator with a required name, a determinate and an indeterminate state, and tones that stay visible against the track.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/progress

Group: Feedback · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import { Progress } from "@azmr/ui/progress";
```

```tsx
import { Progress } from "@azmr/ui/progress";

export default function ProgressBasic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex max-w-md flex-col gap-5">
      <Progress value={40} showValue aria-label="Upload progress" />
      <Progress value={75} tone="success" size="lg" aria-label="Storage used" />
      <Progress value={90} tone="warning" aria-label="Quota" />
      <Progress value={100} tone="destructive" size="sm" aria-label="Disk full" />
      {/* value={null}: the amount is unknown. It pulses and stays partial, so it never looks done. */}
      <Progress value={null} aria-label="Preparing your export" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

`value` is the current amount in the range `min` to `max` (default 0 to 100), clamped to it. `value={null}` means the amount is **unknown**: the bar is partial and pulses, and carries no `aria-valuenow`. A value that is not a finite number is treated the same way rather than rendered as `NaN`.

## Circular

```tsx
import { Progress } from "@azmr/ui/progress";

export default function ProgressCircular() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
      <Progress variant="circular" size="sm" value={30} aria-label="Sync" />
      <Progress variant="circular" value={65} showValue tone="info" aria-label="Profile complete" />
      <Progress
        variant="circular"
        size="lg"
        value={90}
        showValue
        tone="success"
        aria-label="Tasks done"
      />
      <Progress variant="circular" value={null} aria-label="Loading" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Why it needs a name

A progress bar with no name is announced as just "progress bar". `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby` pointing at a heading) is required by the types. The percentage is the default `aria-valuetext`; pass `valueText` for something better ("Step 3 of 10"). `showValue` prints the percentage as text, hidden from assistive technology because the bar already says it.

## Reduced motion and indeterminate

An indeterminate bar pulses. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` it **keeps pulsing**, because a frozen full-width bar would read as "done". It is also never full width, and the pulse is opacity, not movement.

## Tones are checked

`tone` is `default`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive` or `info`. The indicator colour must show up against both the track and the page (3:1 for non-text content), and the test suite checks it for every tone in light and dark. The `warning` tone uses the readable `--warning-text` colour, not the pale yellow surface colour, which would be far too faint on a light track.

## Props

| Prop        | Type                                                                          | Default | Required | Description                                                                                           |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`     | `number \| null`                                                              |         | Yes      | The current value, or `null` when the amount is not known (indeterminate). Default range is 0 to 100. |
| `min`       | `number`                                                                      |         | No       |                                                                                                       |
| `max`       | `number`                                                                      |         | No       |                                                                                                       |
| `variant`   | `"linear" \| "circular" \| undefined`                                         |         | No       | `linear` (default) is a bar; `circular` is a ring.                                                    |
| `size`      | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| undefined`                                           |         | No       |                                                                                                       |
| `tone`      | `"success" \| "destructive" \| "info" \| "default" \| "warning" \| undefined` |         | No       |                                                                                                       |
| `showValue` | `boolean \| undefined`                                                        |         | No       | Show the percentage as text next to (linear) or inside (circular) the indicator.                      |
| `valueText` | `((value: number \| null) => string) \| undefined`                            |         | No       | The text a screen reader announces, instead of the default percentage.                                |
| `className` | `string`                                                                      |         | No       |                                                                                                       |

## Accessibility

- Native `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` (from Base UI), and a required accessible name.
- The circular ring is decorative (`aria-hidden`); the progressbar carries the meaning.
- No keyboard interaction: a progress bar is not focusable.

---

# Spinner

> An indeterminate progress indicator that is a Server Component and keeps spinning under reduced motion.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/spinner

Group: Feedback · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@azmr/ui/spinner";
```

```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@azmr/ui/spinner";

export default function SpinnerBasic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
      {/* Decorative: the surrounding control already says it is busy. */}
      <Spinner />
      <Spinner className="size-6" />
      {/* Announced as a status. */}
      <Spinner className="size-8 text-primary" label="Loading customers" />
    </div>
  );
}
```
