`Spinner` is a **Server Component** (no hooks, no `"use client"`), so it works in `loading.tsx` and Suspense fallbacks without a client boundary. Size it with a class (`size-6`); colour follows `currentColor`.

## Decorative or announced

A spinner inside a control that already says it is busy (such as `Button loading`) should be decorative: it is `aria-hidden` by default. A spinner on its own needs a `label`, which makes it a `role="status"` that screen readers announce.

## Reduced motion

Most motion in `@azmr/ui` stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`. A spinner does not: a frozen spinner reads as a hung page, which is worse than motion the user asked to avoid. It is marked `data-motion="essential"` to opt out of the reduced-motion rule.

## Props

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`     | `string` |         | No       | Accessible name. When set the spinner is announced as a status ("Loading customers"); when omitted it is decorative and hidden from assistive technology (use that when the surrounding control already says it is busy, as `Button loading` does). |
| `className` | `string` |         | No       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

Any SVG attribute passes through, and `ref` is the `<svg>`. `className` is merged last: `size-8 text-primary`.

## Accessibility

- Decorative by default, announced only when you give it a `label`.
- No keyboard interaction; it is not focusable.

---

# Toast

> Short notifications raised from anywhere with toast.success(), toast.error() and toast.promise(). Stacked, pausable, swipeable and announced to screen readers. Built on Base UI.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/toast

Group: Feedback · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

Mount one `Toaster` near the root of your app, then raise toasts from anywhere, including outside React.

```tsx
import { Toaster, toast } from "@azmr/ui/toast";

// Once, in the root layout:
<Toaster />

// Anywhere:
toast.success("Invoice sent");
```

`Toaster` is a client component. A toast raised before it has mounted has nowhere to render, so put it in the layout rather than in a page.

This site has a `Toaster` in its layout, so the demos below raise real toasts in the corner of the screen.

## Types

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { toast } from "@azmr/ui/toast";

export default function ToastTypes() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => toast("Draft saved")}>
        Plain
      </Button>
      <Button
        variant="outline"
        onClick={() =>
          toast.success("Invoice sent", { description: "Aroha will get it within a minute." })
        }
      >
        Success
      </Button>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => toast.info("New version available")}>
        Info
      </Button>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => toast.warning("Your plan renews tomorrow")}>
        Warning
      </Button>
      {/* Errors are announced urgently (role="alert"); the others politely. */}
      <Button
        variant="outline"
        onClick={() => toast.error("Could not save", { description: "Check your connection." })}
      >
        Error
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

| Call            | Icon     | Announced                     |
| --------------- | -------- | ----------------------------- |
| `toast(title)`  | none     | politely                      |
| `toast.success` | check    | politely                      |
| `toast.info`    | info     | politely                      |
| `toast.warning` | triangle | politely                      |
| `toast.error`   | alert    | **urgently** (`role="alert"`) |
| `toast.loading` | spinner  | politely                      |

Each takes `(title, options)`. Options: `description`, `duration`, `id`, `priority`, `action` and `onClose`. Every call returns the toast's id.

Icons are decorative; the type is also in the text you write. Do not rely on colour alone.

## Actions and updating a toast

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { toast } from "@azmr/ui/toast";
import { useState } from "react";

export default function ToastActions() {
  const [items, setItems] = useState(["Quarterly report", "Team photo"]);

  function remove(name: string) {
    setItems((all) => all.filter((n) => n !== name));
    toast(`Deleted “${name}”`, {
      // The same id replaces the toast instead of stacking another.
      id: `deleted-${name}`,
      action: {
        label: "Undo",
        onClick: () => setItems((all) => (all.includes(name) ? all : [...all, name])),
      },
    });
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <ul className="flex flex-col gap-2 text-sm">
        {items.map((name) => (
          <li key={name} className="flex items-center gap-3">
            {name}
            <Button size="sm" variant="ghost" onClick={() => remove(name)}>
              Delete
            </Button>
          </li>
        ))}
        {items.length === 0 && <li className="text-muted-foreground">Nothing left.</li>}
      </ul>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`action: { label, onClick }` adds a button, and the toast dismisses itself after it runs. Undo is the classic use.

Giving a toast an `id` that is already showing **updates it instead of stacking another**, so repeating an action does not flood the screen. `toast.update(id, { title, type, … })` changes a toast in place, and `toast.dismiss(id)` removes one (`toast.dismiss()` removes them all).

## Promises

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { toast } from "@azmr/ui/toast";

const wait = (ms: number) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

export default function ToastPromise() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      <Button
        variant="outline"
        onClick={() =>
          toast.promise(
            wait(1500).then(() => 12),
            {
              loading: "Exporting…",
              success: (rows) => `Exported ${rows} rows`,
              error: "Export failed",
            },
          )
        }
      >
        Export (succeeds)
      </Button>
      <Button
        variant="outline"
        onClick={() =>
          toast
            .promise(
              wait(1500).then(() => Promise.reject(new Error("Disk full"))),
              {
                loading: "Exporting…",
                success: "Exported",
                error: (e: Error) => `Export failed: ${e.message}`,
              },
            )
            .catch(() => {})
        }
      >
        Export (fails)
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`toast.promise(promise, { loading, success, error })` shows a loading toast, then replaces it with the result. `success` and `error` can be functions of the value or the error. It returns the same promise, so it still rejects for you to handle; a failure is announced urgently.

## Timing

A toast dismisses itself after `duration` (5000 ms by default; set it on the `Toaster` or per toast). `duration: 0` keeps it until dismissed, and `toast.loading` never times out. The timer **pauses while the pointer is over the stack or focus is inside it**, so nobody loses a toast they are reading.

Do not use a toast for anything the person must act on. Auto-dismissing messages are easy to miss, so keep errors that need a decision in the page (or an `AlertDialog`).

## Stacking and position

The `Toaster` shows `limit` toasts (3 by default); older ones wait behind and the stack fans out on hover or focus. `position` is `top-left`, `top-center`, `top-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-center` or `bottom-right` (default), and new toasts come in from that edge. The stack sits on the `--z-toast` layer, above dialogs and menus.

## Motion

Toasts slide in from their edge, fade out, and the stack reflows on `--motion-duration-slow`. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` those collapse to near zero. While a finger is dragging a toast there is no easing, so it tracks exactly.

## Accessibility

| Key                  | Action                                                                                           |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `F6`                 | Moves focus into the notifications region. Tab then moves between the actions and close buttons. |
| `Tab` or `Shift+Tab` | Moves between the toasts' buttons. The timers pause while focus is inside.                       |
| `Enter` or `Space`   | Activates the focused action or close button.                                                    |

- The region is named "Notifications" (change it with `label`) and is a polite live region. Errors are also written to a separate alert, so they are spoken at once.
- The close button is labelled "Dismiss notification"; its icon is decorative.
- A toast can be swiped away toward the edge it came from on touch.

## Props

| Prop        | Type                                                                                                           | Default | Required | Description                                                                         |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `position`  | `"top-left" \| "top-center" \| "top-right" \| "bottom-left" \| "bottom-center" \| "bottom-right" \| undefined` |         | No       | Where the stack sits. Default `bottom-right`. New toasts come in from that edge.    |
| `limit`     | `number`                                                                                                       |         | No       | The most toasts shown at once; older ones wait behind. Default 3.                   |
| `duration`  | `number`                                                                                                       |         | No       | Default milliseconds before a toast dismisses itself. `0` never does. Default 5000. |
| `label`     | `string`                                                                                                       |         | No       | The accessible name of the notifications region. Default "Notifications".           |
| `className` | `string`                                                                                                       |         | No       |                                                                                     |

| Prop          | Type                                                       | Default | Required | Description                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description` | `ReactNode`                                                |         | No       | A second line under the title.                                                                                                                           |
| `duration`    | `number`                                                   |         | No       | Milliseconds before it dismisses itself. `0` keeps it until dismissed. Defaults to the `Toaster`'s `duration` (5000), and loading toasts never time out. |
| `id`          | `string`                                                   |         | No       | Showing a toast with an id that is already visible updates that toast instead of stacking another.                                                       |
| `priority`    | `"low" \| "high" \| undefined`                             |         | No       | `high` is announced urgently (`role="alert"`), `low` politely. Errors are `high` by default, everything else `low`.                                      |
| `action`      | `{ label: ReactNode; onClick?: () => void; } \| undefined` |         | No       | A button in the toast, such as Undo. It runs `onClick` and then dismisses the toast.                                                                     |
| `onClose`     | `(() => void) \| undefined`                                |         | No       | Called when the toast is dismissed, by the person or by the timer.                                                                                       |

---

# Floating

> Tooltip, Popover and HoverCard. Surfaces anchored to a trigger, collision-aware, portalled, and animated with the motion tokens. Built on Base UI.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/floating

Group: Overlays · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Tooltip, TooltipTrigger, TooltipContent, TooltipProvider,
  Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverContent, PopoverTitle, PopoverDescription, PopoverClose,
  HoverCard, HoverCardTrigger, HoverCardContent,
} from "@azmr/ui/floating";
```

These are interactive, so they are client components. Each one renders its surface in a portal on `document.body`, above overlays (the `--z-tooltip` and `--z-popover` layers), and flips to the other side of the trigger when there is no room. The surface is also capped to the space available, so it never runs off the viewport.

Which one to use:

| You need                                                | Use         |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| A short label for a control                             | `Tooltip`   |
| Anything interactive (a form, a menu of actions, links) | `Popover`   |
| A preview of a link's target                            | `HoverCard` |

## Tooltip

```tsx
import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipProvider, TooltipTrigger } from "@azmr/ui/floating";
import { Icon } from "@azmr/ui/icons";
import { Bold, Italic, Underline } from "lucide-react";

const tools = [
  { label: "Bold", icon: Bold, shortcut: "Ctrl+B" },
  { label: "Italic", icon: Italic, shortcut: "Ctrl+I" },
  { label: "Underline", icon: Underline, shortcut: "Ctrl+U" },
] as const;

export default function TooltipBasic() {
  return (
    // One provider: the first tip waits half a second, then its neighbours open at once.
    <TooltipProvider>
      <div className="flex gap-1">
        {tools.map(({ label, icon, shortcut }) => (
          <Tooltip key={label}>
            <TooltipTrigger
              render={
                <Button size="icon" variant="ghost" aria-label={label}>
                  <Icon icon={icon} />
                </Button>
              }
            />
            <TooltipContent>{shortcut}</TooltipContent>
          </Tooltip>
        ))}
      </div>
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

A tooltip shows on hover and on **keyboard focus**, closes on Escape, and never takes the pointer, so it cannot block what is under it. Put one `TooltipProvider` around a toolbar (or the app): the first tooltip waits `TOOLTIP_DELAY_MS` (500 ms), then its neighbours open at once while one is showing, and moving between them does not replay the animation.

### Touch, and what a tooltip is not

There is no hover on touch, so **a tooltip does not open on touch**. That makes it a convenience for people with a pointer or keyboard, and the rule follows:

- Never put essential information in a tooltip. Use a `Popover` if touch users need it.
- An icon-only button still needs its own accessible name (`aria-label`). The tooltip adds to it, it does not replace it.

While open, the trigger points at the tooltip with `aria-describedby`, and the tooltip has `role="tooltip"`. Base UI 1.9 does neither, so a screen reader would never hear the text; `@azmr/ui` adds it. One consequence: if the tooltip repeats the button's `aria-label` word for word, a screen reader reads it twice. Prefer tooltip text that adds something, such as the shortcut, as in the demo.

## Popover

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import {
  Popover,
  PopoverClose,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from "@azmr/ui/floating";
import { Input } from "@azmr/ui/input";

export default function PopoverBasic() {
  return (
    <Popover>
      <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline">Rename</Button>} />
      <PopoverContent align="start">
        <PopoverTitle>Rename project</PopoverTitle>
        <PopoverDescription>Shown to everyone on the team.</PopoverDescription>
        <form className="mt-3 flex flex-col gap-3" onSubmit={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
          <Input aria-label="Project name" defaultValue="Website relaunch" />
          <div className="flex justify-end gap-2">
            <PopoverClose render={<Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button>} />
            <PopoverClose render={<Button type="submit">Save</Button>} />
          </div>
        </form>
      </PopoverContent>
    </Popover>
  );
}
```

Opens on click, Enter or Space. Focus moves into the panel, Tab moves through its content, and Escape or a click outside closes it and returns focus to the trigger. The panel is a `role="dialog"` named by `PopoverTitle` (or `aria-label`) and described by `PopoverDescription`. Use `PopoverClose` for a button that dismisses it.

Inputs inside keep their own keys: arrow keys and typing are never taken by the popover.

## HoverCard

```tsx
import { HoverCard, HoverCardContent, HoverCardTrigger } from "@azmr/ui/floating";

export default function HoverCardBasic() {
  return (
    <p className="max-w-md text-sm">
      The design was led by{" "}
      <HoverCard>
        <HoverCardTrigger
          href="https://platform.azmara.io/docs"
          className="font-medium underline underline-offset-4"
        >
          Aroha Ngata
        </HoverCardTrigger>
        <HoverCardContent>
          <p className="text-sm font-medium">Aroha Ngata</p>
          <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-muted-foreground">
            Product designer in Hamilton. Leads the design system.
          </p>
        </HoverCardContent>
      </HoverCard>
      . Hover or focus the name to preview; it is a normal link without the card.
    </p>
  );
}
```

The trigger is a real link (`<a>`), so the page works without the card. The card opens on hover and on keyboard focus of the link and closes on Escape. It is not announced as a dialog and does not open on touch, so nothing in it may be the only way to reach something.

## Positioning

Every content component takes `side`, `align`, `sideOffset` (default 6) and `collisionPadding` (default 8, the minimum distance kept from the viewport edge).

| Prop               | Type                                                                                    | Default | Required | Description                                                                              |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `side`             | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "inline-start" \| "inline-end" \| undefined` |         | No       | The side of the trigger to open on. It flips to the opposite side when there is no room. |
| `align`            | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| undefined`                                             |         | No       | Alignment along that side.                                                               |
| `sideOffset`       | `number`                                                                                |         | No       | Gap between the trigger and the surface, in px. Default 6.                               |
| `collisionPadding` | `number`                                                                                |         | No       | Minimum distance kept from the viewport edge, in px. Default 8.                          |

## Motion

Surfaces fade and scale from the trigger (`transform-origin` follows the trigger through `--transform-origin`) using Base UI's `data-starting-style` and `data-ending-style` and `--motion-duration-fast`. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the duration tokens collapse to near zero, so surfaces appear and disappear instantly.

## Accessibility

| Key                  | Action                                                                             |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`                | Focusing a tooltip trigger or hover-card link shows its surface; leaving hides it. |
| `Enter` or `Space`   | Opens a popover from its trigger.                                                  |
| `Tab` or `Shift+Tab` | Moves through the content of an open popover.                                      |
| `Escape`             | Closes the open tooltip, popover or hover card. Focus returns to the trigger.      |

---

# Modal

> Dialog, AlertDialog and Drawer. Surfaces that take over the screen, with a focus trap, an inert page, scroll lock and focus return. Built on Base UI.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/modal

Group: Overlays · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogDescription, DialogFooter, DialogClose,
  AlertDialog, AlertDialogTrigger, AlertDialogContent, AlertDialogHeader, AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogDescription, AlertDialogFooter, AlertDialogCancel, AlertDialogAction,
  Drawer, DrawerTrigger, DrawerContent, DrawerHeader, DrawerTitle, DrawerDescription, DrawerFooter, DrawerClose,
} from "@azmr/ui/modal";
```

These are interactive, so they are client components. Every modal surface does the same four things while it is open:

- **Traps focus.** Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside. At the ends focus wraps.
- **Makes the page inert.** The page behind is hidden from assistive technology and cannot be focused.
- **Locks scroll.** The page does not scroll behind it.
- **Returns focus.** Closing puts focus back on the control that opened it.

They render in a portal above the page, with a scrim (`--scrim`) behind them on the `--z-overlay` layer and the surface on `--z-modal`.

| You need                                                         | Use           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| A task or form that needs the person's full attention            | `Dialog`      |
| A yes or no before something destructive or irreversible         | `AlertDialog` |
| A side panel or a bottom sheet (filters, details, a mobile menu) | `Drawer`      |

## Dialog

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { Input } from "@azmr/ui/input";
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@azmr/ui/modal";

export default function DialogBasic() {
  return (
    <Dialog>
      <DialogTrigger render={<Button>Edit profile</Button>} />
      <DialogContent>
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle>Edit profile</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>Change how you appear to the rest of your team.</DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>
        <form className="grid gap-3" onSubmit={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
          <div className="grid gap-1.5">
            <label htmlFor="display-name" className="text-sm font-medium">
              Display name
            </label>
            <Input id="display-name" defaultValue="Aroha Ngata" />
          </div>
          <DialogFooter>
            <DialogClose render={<Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>} />
            <DialogClose render={<Button type="submit">Save changes</Button>} />
          </DialogFooter>
        </form>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}
```

Name every dialog with `DialogTitle` and describe it with `DialogDescription`; they become the dialog's accessible name and description. Escape, the corner close button (`showClose`, on by default) and a click on the scrim all close it. Set `disablePointerDismissal` on `Dialog` when an accidental click outside must not lose the person's work.

`size` is `sm`, `md` (default), `lg`, `xl` or `full`. Every size stays inside the viewport, and a dialog taller than the screen scrolls inside the viewport instead of running off it.

### Stacked dialogs

```tsx
import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@azmr/ui/modal";

export default function DialogStacked() {
  return (
    <Dialog>
      <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline">Open the first dialog</Button>} />
      <DialogContent size="lg">
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle>Invite people</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>
            Press Escape to close only the top dialog: the one underneath stays open.
          </DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>
        <Dialog>
          <DialogTrigger
            render={
              <Button variant="secondary" className="justify-self-start">
                Review permissions
              </Button>
            }
          />
          <DialogContent size="sm">
            <DialogHeader>
              <DialogTitle>Permissions</DialogTitle>
              <DialogDescription>Invited people can view and comment.</DialogDescription>
            </DialogHeader>
            <DialogFooter>
              <DialogClose render={<Button>Got it</Button>} />
            </DialogFooter>
          </DialogContent>
        </Dialog>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}
```

A dialog can open another. Escape closes only the top one, focus is trapped in the top one, and closing it returns focus to the control that opened it, which sits inside the dialog underneath.

## AlertDialog

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogAction,
  AlertDialogCancel,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
} from "@azmr/ui/modal";
import { useState } from "react";

export default function AlertDialogBasic() {
  const [deleted, setDeleted] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
      <AlertDialog>
        <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="destructive">Delete project</Button>} />
        <AlertDialogContent>
          <AlertDialogHeader>
            <AlertDialogTitle>Delete this project?</AlertDialogTitle>
            <AlertDialogDescription>
              Its files and history are removed for everyone. This cannot be undone.
            </AlertDialogDescription>
          </AlertDialogHeader>
          <AlertDialogFooter>
            <AlertDialogCancel>Keep it</AlertDialogCancel>
            <AlertDialogAction onClick={() => setDeleted(true)}>Delete</AlertDialogAction>
          </AlertDialogFooter>
        </AlertDialogContent>
      </AlertDialog>
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground" aria-live="polite">
        {deleted ? "Project deleted." : "Focus starts on “Keep it”, never on “Delete”."}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

An alert dialog interrupts to ask for a decision. It differs from a `Dialog` in three ways, all deliberate:

1. It is announced as an **alert dialog**.
2. A click outside does **not** close it. The person has to choose.
3. Focus starts on `AlertDialogCancel`, the least destructive choice, **even when the destructive button comes first in the page order**. Pressing Enter by reflex cannot delete anything. If there is no `AlertDialogCancel`, focus starts on the first control.

`AlertDialogAction` is destructive by default; pass `tone="default"` for a plain confirmation. It runs its `onClick` and then closes the dialog. Escape cancels.

## Drawer

```tsx
import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import {
  Drawer,
  DrawerClose,
  DrawerContent,
  DrawerDescription,
  DrawerFooter,
  DrawerHeader,
  type DrawerSide,
  DrawerTitle,
  DrawerTrigger,
} from "@azmr/ui/modal";

const sides: DrawerSide[] = ["right", "left", "top", "bottom"];

export default function DrawerBasic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      {sides.map((side) => (
        <Drawer key={side} side={side}>
          <DrawerTrigger render={<Button variant="outline">From the {side}</Button>} />
          <DrawerContent>
            <DrawerHeader>
              <DrawerTitle>Filters</DrawerTitle>
              <DrawerDescription>
                On a touch screen, swipe toward the {side} to dismiss.
              </DrawerDescription>
            </DrawerHeader>
            <DrawerFooter>
              <DrawerClose render={<Button>Apply</Button>} />
            </DrawerFooter>
          </DrawerContent>
        </Drawer>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

A drawer slides in from `side` (`right` by default, `left`, `top` or `bottom`) and is a full modal. On touch it can be dismissed by swiping back toward the edge it came from; the panel follows the finger exactly and the scrim fades with the swipe. Gesture handling comes from Base UI's drawer, so there is no extra module to install.

## Motion

The scrim fades and a dialog fades and scales in from slightly smaller, using `--motion-duration-base`. A drawer slides on `--motion-duration-slow`. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` those tokens collapse to near zero, so everything appears and disappears instantly. While a finger is dragging a drawer there is no easing at all, so it tracks exactly.

## Accessibility

| Key                  | Action                                                               |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab` or `Shift+Tab` | Moves through the controls inside the surface and wraps at the ends. |
| `Escape`             | Closes the top surface. Focus returns to the control that opened it. |
| `Enter` or `Space`   | Opens from a trigger, and activates the focused button inside.       |

- The surface is named by its title and described by its description. Always include a title.
- The corner close button is labelled "Close"; its icon is decorative.
- The scrim colour is a token, so it follows light and dark mode and scoped themes.

## Props

| Prop        | Type                                                  | Default | Required | Description                                                                       |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `className` | `string`                                              |         | No       |                                                                                   |
| `size`      | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| "full" \| undefined` |         | No       | Maximum width. Default `md`. All sizes stay inside the viewport on small screens. |
| `showClose` | `boolean \| undefined`                                |         | No       | Show the corner close button (labelled "Close"). Default true.                    |

| Prop                      | Type                                                                                                                          | Default | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `side`                    | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| undefined`                                                                         |         | No       | The edge it slides in from. Default `right`. It is dismissed by swiping back toward that edge.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `children`                | `React.ReactNode \| PayloadChildRenderFunction<unknown>`                                                                      |         | No       | The content of the drawer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `open`                    | `boolean \| undefined`                                                                                                        |         | No       | Whether the drawer is currently open.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `modal`                   | `boolean \| "trap-focus" \| undefined`                                                                                        | `true`  | No       | Determines if the drawer enters a modal state when open. - `true`: user interaction is limited to just the drawer: focus is trapped, document page scroll is locked, and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled. - `false`: user interaction with the rest of the document is allowed. - `'trap-focus'`: focus is trapped inside the drawer, but document page scroll is not locked and pointer interactions outside of it remain enabled. |
| `disablePointerDismissal` | `boolean \| undefined`                                                                                                        | `false` | No       | Whether to prevent the drawer from closing on outside presses. For non-modal drawers, this also prevents the drawer from closing when focus moves outside of it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `defaultOpen`             | `boolean \| undefined`                                                                                                        | `false` | No       | Whether the drawer is initially open. To render a controlled drawer, use the `open` prop instead.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `onOpenChange`            | `((open: boolean, eventDetails: DrawerPrimitive.Root.ChangeEventDetails) => void) \| undefined`                               |         | No       | Event handler called when the drawer is opened or closed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `onOpenChangeComplete`    | `((open: boolean) => void) \| undefined`                                                                                      |         | No       | Event handler called after any animations complete when the drawer is opened or closed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `actionsRef`              | `React.RefObject<DrawerRootActions \| null> \| undefined`                                                                     |         | No       | A ref to imperative actions. - `unmount`: Ends the closing phase of the drawer after an externally controlled closing animation finishes. Call `preventUnmountOnClose()` in `onOpenChange` first, otherwise the drawer completes closing on its own. Whether it leaves the DOM is decided by `keepMounted` on the portal. - `close`: Closes the drawer imperatively when called.                                                                          |
| `handle`                  | `DrawerPrimitive.Handle<unknown> \| undefined`                                                                                |         | No       | A handle to associate the drawer with a trigger. If specified, allows detached triggers to control the drawer's open state. Can be created with the Drawer.createHandle() method.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `triggerId`               | `string \| null \| undefined`                                                                                                 |         | No       | ID of the trigger that the drawer is associated with. This is useful in conjunction with the `open` prop to create a controlled drawer. There's no need to specify this prop when the drawer is uncontrolled (that is, when the `open` prop is not set).                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `defaultTriggerId`        | `string \| null \| undefined`                                                                                                 |         | No       | ID of the trigger that the drawer is associated with. This is useful in conjunction with the `defaultOpen` prop to create an initially open drawer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `snapPoints`              | `DrawerSnapPoint[] \| undefined`                                                                                              |         | No       | Snap points used to position the drawer. Use numbers between 0 and 1 to represent fractions of the viewport height, numbers greater than 1 as pixel values, or strings in `px`/`rem` units (for example, `'148px'` or `'30rem'`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `snapToSequentialPoints`  | `boolean \| undefined`                                                                                                        | `false` | No       | Disables velocity-based snap skipping so drag distance determines the next snap point.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `snapPoint`               | `DrawerSnapPoint \| null \| undefined`                                                                                        |         | No       | The currently active snap point. Use with `onSnapPointChange` to control the snap point.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `defaultSnapPoint`        | `DrawerSnapPoint \| null \| undefined`                                                                                        |         | No       | The initial snap point value when uncontrolled.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `onSnapPointChange`       | `((snapPoint: DrawerSnapPoint \| null, eventDetails: DrawerPrimitive.Root.SnapPointChangeEventDetails) => void) \| undefined` |         | No       | Callback fired when the snap point changes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

The rest are Base UI's props, passed through (`open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal`, `initialFocus`, `finalFocus`, and so on).

---

# Menu

> DropdownMenu and ContextMenu. Menus of actions with items, checkbox and radio items, groups and submenus. Built on Base UI.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/menu

Group: Overlays · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuTrigger, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuLinkItem,
  DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, DropdownMenuRadioGroup, DropdownMenuRadioItem,
  DropdownMenuGroup, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuShortcut,
  DropdownMenuSub, DropdownMenuSubTrigger, DropdownMenuSubContent,
  ContextMenu, ContextMenuTrigger, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuItem, // …and the same parts as above
} from "@azmr/ui/menu";
```

These are interactive, so they are client components. A menu renders in a portal on the `--z-popover` layer, so one opened from inside a dialog appears above it. It flips when there is no room and scrolls inside the space available.

Use a menu for **actions** (things that happen). For choosing a value in a form, use a select. For showing information, use a popover.

## DropdownMenu

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { Icon } from "@azmr/ui/icons";
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuCheckboxItem,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuGroup,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuLabel,
  DropdownMenuRadioGroup,
  DropdownMenuRadioItem,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  DropdownMenuShortcut,
  DropdownMenuSub,
  DropdownMenuSubContent,
  DropdownMenuSubTrigger,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@azmr/ui/menu";
import { ChevronDown } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";

export default function DropdownBasic() {
  const [showGrid, setShowGrid] = useState(true);
  const [density, setDensity] = useState("comfortable");
  const [last, setLast] = useState("Nothing chosen yet");

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
      <DropdownMenu>
        <DropdownMenuTrigger
          render={
            <Button variant="outline" endIcon={<Icon icon={ChevronDown} />}>
              Project
            </Button>
          }
        />
        <DropdownMenuContent>
          <DropdownMenuGroup>
            <DropdownMenuLabel>Project</DropdownMenuLabel>
            <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setLast("Saved")}>
              Save
              <DropdownMenuShortcut>Ctrl+S</DropdownMenuShortcut>
            </DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setLast("Renamed")}>Rename</DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem disabled>Archive (needs an owner)</DropdownMenuItem>
          </DropdownMenuGroup>
          <DropdownMenuSeparator />
          <DropdownMenuCheckboxItem checked={showGrid} onCheckedChange={setShowGrid}>
            Show grid
          </DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>
          <DropdownMenuRadioGroup value={density} onValueChange={(v) => setDensity(v as string)}>
            <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="comfortable">Comfortable</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
            <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="compact">Compact</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
          </DropdownMenuRadioGroup>
          <DropdownMenuSeparator />
          <DropdownMenuSub>
            <DropdownMenuSubTrigger>Share</DropdownMenuSubTrigger>
            <DropdownMenuSubContent>
              <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setLast("Shared by email")}>Email</DropdownMenuItem>
              <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setLast("Link copied")}>Copy link</DropdownMenuItem>
            </DropdownMenuSubContent>
          </DropdownMenuSub>
          <DropdownMenuSeparator />
          <DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={() => setLast("Deleted")}>
            Delete
          </DropdownMenuItem>
        </DropdownMenuContent>
      </DropdownMenu>
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground" aria-live="polite">
        {last} · grid {showGrid ? "on" : "off"} · {density}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Items

| Part                                                 | What it is                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `DropdownMenuItem`                                   | An action. `variant="destructive"` for one that deletes or discards. `disabled` greys it out.                                        |
| `DropdownMenuLinkItem`                               | A real `<a>`, so middle click and "open in new tab" work.                                                                            |
| `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem`                           | Toggles on and off. It stays open when toggled; set `closeOnClick` to change that.                                                   |
| `DropdownMenuRadioGroup` and `DropdownMenuRadioItem` | Exactly one selected.                                                                                                                |
| `DropdownMenuGroup` and `DropdownMenuLabel`          | A named group. The label is not an item, so arrow keys skip it.                                                                      |
| `DropdownMenuSeparator`                              | A divider.                                                                                                                           |
| `DropdownMenuSub`, `…SubTrigger`, `…SubContent`      | A nested menu.                                                                                                                       |
| `DropdownMenuShortcut`                               | A shortcut hint at the end of an item. It is text only: wire up the real shortcut yourself, and add `aria-keyshortcuts` to the item. |

Items keep the menu open when `closeOnClick={false}`.

### Disabled items stay focusable

Following the WAI-ARIA menu pattern, a disabled item is announced as disabled and cannot be run, but arrow keys still land on it. That is deliberate: it lets people find out an action exists, and why it is unavailable if you say so in the label.

## ContextMenu

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import {
  ContextMenu,
  ContextMenuContent,
  ContextMenuItem,
  ContextMenuSeparator,
  ContextMenuTrigger,
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@azmr/ui/menu";
import { useState } from "react";

export default function ContextBasic() {
  const [last, setLast] = useState("Right-click the card, or use the button");
  const choose = (what: string) => () => setLast(what);

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <ContextMenu>
        <ContextMenuTrigger className="flex h-28 w-72 items-center justify-center rounded-lg border border-dashed border-border text-sm text-muted-foreground">
          Right-click here
        </ContextMenuTrigger>
        <ContextMenuContent>
          <ContextMenuItem onClick={choose("Copied")}>Copy</ContextMenuItem>
          <ContextMenuItem onClick={choose("Pasted")}>Paste</ContextMenuItem>
          <ContextMenuSeparator />
          <ContextMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={choose("Deleted")}>
            Delete
          </ContextMenuItem>
        </ContextMenuContent>
      </ContextMenu>

      {/* The same actions on a visible button: a context menu must never be the only way in. */}
      <DropdownMenu>
        <DropdownMenuTrigger
          render={
            <Button variant="outline" size="sm">
              Actions
            </Button>
          }
        />
        <DropdownMenuContent>
          <DropdownMenuItem onClick={choose("Copied")}>Copy</DropdownMenuItem>
          <DropdownMenuItem onClick={choose("Pasted")}>Paste</DropdownMenuItem>
          <DropdownMenuSeparator />
          <DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={choose("Deleted")}>
            Delete
          </DropdownMenuItem>
        </DropdownMenuContent>
      </DropdownMenu>
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground" aria-live="polite">
        {last}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

A context menu opens at the pointer on right click (and, on touch, a long press: Base UI provides that and it is not tested here). Once open it behaves exactly like a dropdown, and it takes the same item parts.

**Use it as an enhancement only.** The trigger area is not focusable, the browser's keyboard route to a context menu needs a focused element, and a long press is easy to miss. So everything in it must be reachable another way, as in the demo, where the same actions are on a visible button.

## Open a dialog from a menu

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@azmr/ui/menu";
import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogAction,
  AlertDialogCancel,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
} from "@azmr/ui/modal";
import { useState } from "react";

// Open a dialog from a menu item: control the dialog and open it from the item's onClick. The
// dialog sits next to the menu, not inside it, so it survives the menu closing.
export default function MenuOpensDialog() {
  const [confirming, setConfirming] = useState(false);
  const [deleted, setDeleted] = useState(false);

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
      <DropdownMenu>
        <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline">More</Button>} />
        <DropdownMenuContent>
          <DropdownMenuItem>Duplicate</DropdownMenuItem>
          <DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={() => setConfirming(true)}>
            Delete…
          </DropdownMenuItem>
        </DropdownMenuContent>
      </DropdownMenu>

      <AlertDialog open={confirming} onOpenChange={setConfirming}>
        <AlertDialogContent>
          <AlertDialogHeader>
            <AlertDialogTitle>Delete this item?</AlertDialogTitle>
            <AlertDialogDescription>This cannot be undone.</AlertDialogDescription>
          </AlertDialogHeader>
          <AlertDialogFooter>
            <AlertDialogCancel>Keep it</AlertDialogCancel>
            <AlertDialogAction onClick={() => setDeleted(true)}>Delete</AlertDialogAction>
          </AlertDialogFooter>
        </AlertDialogContent>
      </AlertDialog>
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground" aria-live="polite">
        {deleted ? "Deleted." : "Choose Delete… to confirm."}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Control the dialog and open it from the item's `onClick`. Keep the dialog **next to** the menu rather than inside it: it has to outlive the menu closing. Use this for any action that needs confirmation.

## Keyboard

| Key                               | Action                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter` or `Space` or `ArrowDown` | On the trigger: opens the menu on the first item.                                                          |
| `ArrowUp`                         | On the trigger: opens the menu on the last item.                                                           |
| `ArrowDown` or `ArrowUp`          | Moves to the next or previous item and wraps at the ends.                                                  |
| `Home` or `End`                   | Jumps to the first or last item.                                                                           |
| `A–Z`                             | Typeahead: jumps to the item that starts with the letters you type. Letters typed together are one search. |
| `Enter` or `Space`                | Runs the focused item and closes the menu. A checkbox or radio item toggles.                               |
| `ArrowRight`                      | On a submenu trigger: opens the submenu and focuses its first item.                                        |
| `ArrowLeft`                       | In a submenu: closes it and returns to its trigger.                                                        |
| `Escape`                          | Closes the open submenu, or the menu. Focus returns to the trigger.                                        |
| `Tab`                             | Closes the menu and moves on. Focus is never trapped.                                                      |

## Accessibility

- The popup is a `menu`; items are `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` (with `aria-checked`) or `menuitemradio`. The trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`.
- A submenu trigger announces `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`. Its chevron is decorative.
- Check and radio marks are decorative; the state is `aria-checked`.
- Destructive items use the destructive colour as text on the popover surface, which meets the contrast the tokens guarantee.

## Motion

Menus fade and scale from the trigger on `--motion-duration-fast`, and collapse to instant under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Props

| Prop        | Type                                      | Default | Required | Description                                                   |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`   | `"default" \| "destructive" \| undefined` |         | No       | `destructive` for an item that deletes or discards something. |
| `className` | `string`                                  |         | No       |                                                               |

| Prop               | Type                                                                                    | Default | Required | Description                                                                              |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `className`        | `string`                                                                                |         | No       |                                                                                          |
| `side`             | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "inline-start" \| "inline-end" \| undefined` |         | No       | The side of the trigger to open on. It flips to the opposite side when there is no room. |
| `align`            | `"center" \| "start" \| "end" \| undefined`                                             |         | No       | Alignment along that side.                                                               |
| `sideOffset`       | `number`                                                                                |         | No       | Gap between the trigger and the surface, in px. Default 6.                               |
| `collisionPadding` | `number`                                                                                |         | No       | Minimum distance kept from the viewport edge, in px. Default 8.                          |

The rest are Base UI's props, passed through (`open`, `onOpenChange`, `loopFocus`, `modal`, and so on).

---

# Breadcrumb

> A trail showing where you are and the way back up. Built from parts or from data, collapsible, router-friendly. Server-safe.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/breadcrumb

Group: Navigation · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Breadcrumb, BreadcrumbList, BreadcrumbItem, BreadcrumbLink, BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator, BreadcrumbEllipsis, Breadcrumbs,
} from "@azmr/ui/breadcrumb";
```

```tsx
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
  Breadcrumbs,
} from "@azmr/ui/breadcrumb";

export default function BreadcrumbBasic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-6">
      {/* From the parts, for full control. */}
      <Breadcrumb>
        <BreadcrumbList>
          <BreadcrumbItem>
            <BreadcrumbLink href="/">Home</BreadcrumbLink>
          </BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbSeparator />
          <BreadcrumbItem>
            <BreadcrumbLink href="/docs">Docs</BreadcrumbLink>
          </BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbSeparator />
          <BreadcrumbItem>
            <BreadcrumbPage>Breadcrumb</BreadcrumbPage>
          </BreadcrumbItem>
        </BreadcrumbList>
      </Breadcrumb>

      {/* From data. The last item is always the current page. */}
      <Breadcrumbs
        label="Breadcrumb from data"
        items={[
          { label: "Home", href: "/" },
          { label: "Projects", href: "/projects" },
          { label: "Website relaunch" },
        ]}
      />

      {/* A long trail collapses the middle. */}
      <Breadcrumbs
        label="Collapsed breadcrumb"
        maxItems={4}
        items={[
          { label: "Home", href: "/" },
          { label: "Projects", href: "/projects" },
          { label: "Website", href: "/projects/website" },
          { label: "Design", href: "/projects/website/design" },
          { label: "Tokens", href: "/projects/website/design/tokens" },
          { label: "Colours" },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

A breadcrumb is a `nav` landmark named "Breadcrumb" holding an ordered list. Links go up the hierarchy; the **current page** is plain text marked `aria-current="page"`, never a link. Separators are decorative and hidden from assistive technology. It is a Server Component.

## From parts

Compose `Breadcrumb`, `BreadcrumbList`, `BreadcrumbItem`, `BreadcrumbLink`, `BreadcrumbPage` and `BreadcrumbSeparator` for full control. A separator can be any content (`<BreadcrumbSeparator>/</BreadcrumbSeparator>`); the default is a chevron.

## From data

`<Breadcrumbs items={[{ label, href }, ...]} />` builds the same thing. The **last item is always the current page**, whether or not it has an `href`, because it is where you are. An item without an `href` is plain text.

### Long trails

`maxItems` collapses the middle: it keeps the first item, an ellipsis and the last items, `maxItems` in all (the ellipsis counts as one). The ellipsis is announced as "More pages" (change it with `ellipsisLabel`). It is a static mark; for a menu of the hidden pages, wrap `BreadcrumbEllipsis` in a `DropdownMenu` yourself.

## With your router

Pass `renderLink` so links use your router's `Link` (client-side navigation, prefetching) instead of a plain `<a>`:

```tsx
<Breadcrumbs items={items} renderLink={(href) => <NextLink href={href} />} />
```

With the parts, use `<BreadcrumbLink render={<NextLink href="/docs" />}>Docs</BreadcrumbLink>`. The element keeps its own props (the `href`) and gains our styling.

## Props

| Prop            | Type                                                  | Default | Required | Description                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`         | `readonly BreadcrumbEntry[]`                          |         | Yes      |                                                                                                                                                         |
| `maxItems`      | `number`                                              |         | No       | Collapse a longer trail: keep the first item, an ellipsis, and the last items, `maxItems` in all (the ellipsis counts as one). Default: never collapse. |
| `separator`     | `ReactNode`                                           |         | No       | Replace the chevron between items.                                                                                                                      |
| `renderLink`    | `((href: string) => React.ReactElement) \| undefined` |         | No       | Render your router's `Link`: `renderLink={(href) => <NextLink href={href} />}`.                                                                         |
| `ellipsisLabel` | `string`                                              |         | No       | The ellipsis's spoken name. Default "More pages".                                                                                                       |
| `label`         | `string`                                              |         | No       | The landmark's name. Default "Breadcrumb"; change it for translation, or with two trails on a page.                                                     |

## Accessibility

- A `nav` landmark with an accessible name (default "Breadcrumb"; rename it for translation, or when a page has two trails).
- An ordered list, so the order is announced ("list, 3 items").
- The current page is `aria-current="page"` and not a link.
- Separators are `aria-hidden`.
- Links have a full-strength focus ring.

| Key     | Action                                                                                   |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`   | Moves through the links in order. The current page and the separators are not focusable. |
| `Enter` | Follows the focused link.                                                                |

---

# Pagination

> A page control that is real links on the server or buttons for client state, with a stable-width page range the data grid reuses. Server-safe.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/pagination

Group: Navigation · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import { Pagination, getPageRange } from "@azmr/ui/pagination";
```

## Links

```tsx
import { Pagination } from "@azmr/ui/pagination";

// Link mode: every page is a real link, so it works without JavaScript and in a Server Component.
// `hrefFor` would normally build a URL like `/items?page=${p}`; here it points at the demo itself.
export default function PaginationLinks() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-6">
      <Pagination page={1} pageCount={5} hrefFor={(p) => `#page-${p}`} label="Short list" />
      <Pagination page={10} pageCount={42} hrefFor={(p) => `#page-${p}`} label="Long list" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Give `Pagination` `hrefFor` and every page is a **real link** (`<a href>`). It works without JavaScript, can be indexed, supports "open in a new tab", and renders in a Server Component. Build the URL from your search params, and pass `renderLink` to use your router's `Link`:

```tsx
<Pagination
  page={page}
  pageCount={pageCount}
  hrefFor={(p) => `/items?page=${p}`}
  renderLink={(href) => <NextLink href={href} />}
/>
```

## Buttons

```tsx
"use client";

import { Pagination } from "@azmr/ui/pagination";
import { useState } from "react";

const PAGE_SIZE = 5;
const ITEMS = Array.from({ length: 47 }, (_, i) => `Item ${i + 1}`);

// Button mode: for client state. `onPageChange` is called with the page that was chosen.
export default function PaginationState() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
  const pageCount = Math.ceil(ITEMS.length / PAGE_SIZE);
  const shown = ITEMS.slice((page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE, page * PAGE_SIZE);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
      <ul className="text-sm" aria-live="polite">
        {shown.map((item) => (
          <li key={item}>{item}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <Pagination page={page} pageCount={pageCount} onPageChange={setPage} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Give it `onPageChange` instead and every page is a button, for state held on the client. It is called with the page that was chosen (not when the current page is pressed again). Buttons are `type="button"`, so they never submit a surrounding form.

If you pass both, `hrefFor` wins.

## The current page, and the ends

The current page is filled and marked `aria-current="page"`. Each page control is named "Page 3" so it is clear which page it is, rather than just "3". **Previous** and **Next** are disabled at the ends: a link loses its `href` and is announced as disabled; a button is `disabled`.

## How many pages are shown

With more than seven pages the control shows the first and last page, the current page and one either side, with ellipses between, and it is **always seven long**, so it does not change width as you page. `siblingCount` and `boundaryCount` widen it. A skipped run of exactly one page is shown as that page instead of an ellipsis, since the ellipsis would save no space.

```
page 1 of 10:  1 2 3 4 5 … 10
page 5 of 10:  1 … 4 5 6 … 10
page 10 of 10: 1 … 6 7 8 9 10
```

### getPageRange

The calculation is exported as a pure function, so the data grid and your own paginators can use it:

```ts
getPageRange({ page: 5, pageCount: 10 });
// [1, "start-ellipsis", 4, 5, 6, "end-ellipsis", 10]
```

Out-of-range pages are pinned to an end, and no pages gives an empty list.

## Building blocks

For a custom layout use `PaginationNav`, `PaginationList`, `PaginationItem`, `PaginationLink` (`isActive`, `disabled`, `href` or `onClick`) and `PaginationEllipsis`.

## Props

| Prop            | Type                                                                                                 | Default | Required | Description                                                                            |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `page`          | `number`                                                                                             |         | Yes      | The current page, 1-based.                                                             |
| `pageCount`     | `number`                                                                                             |         | Yes      |                                                                                        |
| `hrefFor`       | `((page: number) => string) \| undefined`                                                            |         | No       | Link mode: where each page goes. Works in Server Components. Wins over `onPageChange`. |
| `onPageChange`  | `((page: number) => void) \| undefined`                                                              |         | No       | Button mode: called with the page that was chosen. For client state.                   |
| `renderLink`    | `((href: string) => React.ReactElement) \| undefined`                                                |         | No       | Render your router's `Link`: `renderLink={(href) => <NextLink href={href} />}`.        |
| `siblingCount`  | `number`                                                                                             |         | No       | Pages shown either side of the current one. Default 1.                                 |
| `boundaryCount` | `number`                                                                                             |         | No       | Pages always shown at each end. Default 1.                                             |
| `showPrevNext`  | `boolean \| undefined`                                                                               |         | No       | Show Previous and Next. Default true.                                                  |
| `label`         | `string`                                                                                             |         | No       | The landmark's name. Default "Pagination".                                             |
| `labels`        | `{ previous?: string; next?: string; page?: (page: number) => string; more?: string; } \| undefined` |         | No       | Names the controls, for translation.                                                   |

## Accessibility

- A `nav` landmark named "Pagination" (rename it with `label`) containing a list.
- The current page has `aria-current="page"`; pages are named "Page n"; Previous and Next are named "Previous page" and "Next page" (the visible words are hidden on small screens, the names stay).
- The ellipsis is announced as "More pages" and is not focusable.
- Names can be translated with `labels`.

| Key     | Action                                                                      |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`   | Moves through the page controls. A disabled Previous or Next is skipped.    |
| `Enter` | Follows a link, or activates a button.                                      |
| `Space` | Activates a button page. (Links respond to Enter only, as native links do.) |

---

# Stepper

> Shows where someone is in a fixed sequence of steps. A status display with each state said in text, horizontal or vertical. Server-safe.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/stepper

Group: Navigation · Status: stable · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Usage

```tsx
import { Stepper } from "@azmr/ui/stepper";
```

```tsx
import { Stepper } from "@azmr/ui/stepper";

const steps = [
  { label: "Account", description: "Your details" },
  { label: "Plan", description: "Choose a plan" },
  { label: "Payment" },
  { label: "Confirm" },
];

export default function StepperBasic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-8">
      <Stepper steps={steps} current={1} label="Sign-up progress" />
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-12">
        <Stepper steps={steps} current={2} orientation="vertical" label="Vertical progress" />
        <Stepper
          steps={[
            { label: "Upload" },
            { label: "Validate", status: "error", description: "2 rows failed" },
            { label: "Import" },
          ]}
          current={1}
          orientation="vertical"
          label="Import progress"
        />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx
<Stepper
  current={1}
  steps={[{ label: "Account" }, { label: "Plan" }, { label: "Payment" }, { label: "Confirm" }]}
/>
```

`current` is the index (from 0) of the step in progress. Steps before it are **complete**, the one at `current` is **current**, and the rest are **upcoming**. Below `0` nothing has started; past the last step everything is done. Mark a step as failed with `status: "error"`, which does not change the others.

It is a **status display, not navigation**: steps are not links or buttons. If people can jump between steps, build the controls yourself (or use `Tabs`) and use the stepper to show progress.

## Orientation

`orientation` is `horizontal` (default) or `vertical`. Use vertical when steps carry descriptions or the space is narrow.

## Say it in text, not only colour

Each step's state is also written in text for screen readers ("Completed", "Current step", "Not started", "Error"), alongside the visible number or check mark. Translate those words with `statusLabels`. The current step is `aria-current="step"`. The check and error marks are decorative.

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                      | Default | Required | Description                                                                                                |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `steps`        | `readonly StepperStep[]`                  |         | Yes      |                                                                                                            |
| `current`      | `number`                                  |         | Yes      | The index (0-based) of the step in progress. Below 0 nothing has started; past the end everything is done. |
| `orientation`  | `"horizontal" \| "vertical" \| undefined` |         | No       |                                                                                                            |
| `label`        | `string`                                  |         | No       | The list's name. Default "Progress".                                                                       |
| `statusLabels` | `Partial<Record<StepStatus, string>>`     |         | No       | The words spoken for each state, for translation.                                                          |

## Accessibility

- An ordered list named "Progress" (rename it with `label`).
- `aria-current="step"` on the current step only.
- State is conveyed in text as well as colour and icon.
- Connectors between steps are decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

| Key   | Action                                                       |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Tab` | Nothing in a stepper is focusable: it only reports progress. |

---

# Motion

> CSS-first motion presets driven by tokens, a Collapse that never measures height, a count-up, a ViewTransition wrapper, useReducedMotion and an optional module for the motion library. Reduced motion is built in.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/components/motion

Group: Utils · Status: new · Added in @azmr/ui 0.2.0

## Principles

- **CSS first.** Motion is a class or a `data-*` state, with its duration and easing from tokens (`--motion-duration-*`, `--motion-ease-*`). Changing a token or turning on reduced motion changes it everywhere.
- **Cheap properties only.** Animations change `transform`, `scale`, `opacity` and `clip-path`; collapse animates `grid-template-rows`; the tick draws with `stroke-dashoffset`. Nothing animates `width`, `height`, `margin` or position, because those make the browser re-layout every frame. A test scans the CSS and every component and fails on a layout animation that is not on a documented exception list.
- **Reduced motion is the default behaviour, not an extra.** Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the durations collapse to near zero, every slide and scale becomes a plain fade, staggers lose their delays, the shimmer stops and the tick appears at once.

The presets ship in `@azmr/ui/styles.css`. If you import only `tokens.css`, they are not included.

## Presets

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { motionPresets } from "@azmr/ui/presets";
import { useState } from "react";

const tiles = [
  ["Fade", motionPresets.fade.enter],
  ["Scale", motionPresets.scale.enter],
  ["Slide up", motionPresets.slideUp.enter],
  ["Slide down", motionPresets.slideDown.enter],
  ["Slide left", motionPresets.slideLeft.enter],
  ["Slide right", motionPresets.slideRight.enter],
] as const;

export default function MotionGallery() {
  const [run, setRun] = useState(0);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-4">
```
