```tsx
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setRun((n) => n + 1)}>
        Replay
      </Button>
      <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-3 sm:grid-cols-3">
        {tiles.map(([label, cls]) => (
          // The key restarts the animation each time Replay is pressed.
          <div
            key={`${label}-${run}`}
            className={`${cls} flex h-16 w-32 items-center justify-center rounded-md border border-border bg-card text-sm`}
          >
            {label}
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Each preset is a pair of classes, `enter` and `exit`. `enter` eases out and runs on `--motion-duration-base` (200 ms); `exit` is shorter (`--motion-duration-fast`, 150 ms) and eases in, because people wait for things to appear but not to disappear.

| Preset                      | Classes                                                                               |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Fade                        | `motion-fade-in`, `motion-fade-out`                                                   |
| Scale                       | `motion-scale-in`, `motion-scale-out`                                                 |
| Slide up, down, left, right | `motion-slide-up-in`, `motion-slide-up-out`, and the same for `down`, `left`, `right` |
| Shimmer                     | `motion-shimmer`                                                                      |

Use the classes directly, or take them from `motionPresets` (typed, so a typo is a compile error):

```tsx
import { motionPresets } from "@azmr/ui/presets";

<div className={motionPresets.slideUp.enter}>…</div>
```

For Base UI parts (dialogs, menus, popovers) the library already animates with `data-starting-style` and `data-ending-style` on the same tokens; these presets are for your own elements.

## Collapse

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { Collapse } from "@azmr/ui/presets";
import { useId, useState } from "react";

export default function CollapseDemo() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="flex max-w-md flex-col gap-3">
      <Button
        variant="outline"
        aria-expanded={open}
        aria-controls={id}
        onClick={() => setOpen((o) => !o)}
      >
        {open ? "Hide details" : "Show details"}
      </Button>
      <Collapse id={id} open={open}>
        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
          This panel animates its height by moving grid-template-rows between 0fr and 1fr, so no
          height is ever measured in JavaScript. While it is closed it is inert: its content cannot
          be focused or read.
        </p>
        <Button size="sm" className="mt-3">
          A focusable control
        </Button>
      </Collapse>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`Collapse` shows and hides content by animating `grid-template-rows` between `0fr` and `1fr`, so **no height is measured in JavaScript**. It is a Server Component. The content stays mounted while closed (so it keeps its state) and is `inert` and `aria-hidden`, so it cannot be focused or read.

You own the trigger: give it `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the collapse's `id`, as in the demo. For a ready-made disclosure with all of that wired, use `Collapsible` or `Accordion`; they measure the panel through Base UI instead (a documented exception to the cheap-properties rule).

| Prop       | Type        | Default | Required | Description                     |
| ---------- | ----------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------- |
| `open`     | `boolean`   |         | Yes      | Whether the content is showing. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |         | Yes      |                                 |

## Stagger

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { Stagger } from "@azmr/ui/presets";
import { useState } from "react";

const items = ["Design tokens", "Components", "Accessibility", "Motion", "Docs"];

export default function StaggerDemo() {
  const [run, setRun] = useState(0);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setRun((n) => n + 1)}>
        Replay
      </Button>
      <Stagger key={run} as="ul" className="flex flex-col gap-2 text-sm">
        {items.map((item) => (
          <li key={item} className="rounded-md border border-border bg-card px-3 py-2">
            {item}
          </li>
        ))}
      </Stagger>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`Stagger` makes the children of a list enter one after another. Each child gets a `--stagger-index`, and the delay is the index times `--motion-stagger-step` (40 ms), capped at `max` (12) so a long list does not take seconds to appear. Under reduced motion the step is zero and they fade in together. It is a Server Component; only element children are staggered.

| Prop       | Type ## Success check and shimmer

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { Skeleton } from "@azmr/ui/display";
import { AnimatedCheck } from "@azmr/ui/presets";
import { useState } from "react";

export default function CheckAndShimmer() {
  const [run, setRun] = useState(0);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-6">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <AnimatedCheck key={run} size={32} className="text-success" label="Saved" />
        <span className="text-sm">Saved</span>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setRun((n) => n + 1)}>
          Replay
        </Button>
      </div>
      <div className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-2">
        <Skeleton shimmer className="h-4 w-full" />
        <Skeleton shimmer className="h-4 w-4/5" />
        <Skeleton shimmer className="h-16 w-full" />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`AnimatedCheck` is an SVG tick that draws itself in the current text colour (`className="text-success"`); pass `label` to make it an image with a name, otherwise it is decorative. `Skeleton shimmer` sweeps a highlight across a placeholder using `transform` only, instead of pulsing.

## CountUp

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { CountUp } from "@azmr/ui/transition";
import { useState } from "react";

export default function CountUpDemo() {
  const [revenue, setRevenue] = useState(12480);
  const [rate, setRate] = useState(0.372);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-4">
      <div className="flex gap-10">
        <div>
          <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Revenue</p>
          <CountUp
            className="text-3xl font-semibold"
            value={revenue}
            locale="en-NZ"
            format={{ style: "currency", currency: "NZD" }}
          />
        </div>
        <div>
          <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Conversion</p>
          <CountUp
            className="text-3xl font-semibold"
            value={rate}
            locale="en-NZ"
            format={{ style: "percent", maximumFractionDigits: 1 }}
          />
        </div>
      </div>
      <Button
        variant="outline"
        size="sm"
        onClick={() => {
          setRevenue(Math.round(5000 + Math.random() * 95000));
          setRate(Math.random() * 0.6);
        }}
      >
        New numbers
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`CountUp` counts to its new value whenever `value` changes (set `animateOnMount` to count up on first show). Format with `Intl` options (`format`, `locale`): currency, percent, decimals. Whole numbers count in whole numbers. If the value changes again mid-count, it carries on from where it is.

**Screen readers get the final value at once.** The counting itself is hidden from them, so nobody hears a stream of numbers. The digits are tabular so the width does not jitter, and under reduced motion it jumps to the value.

| Prop             | Type                                    | Default | Required | Description                                                                          |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`          | `number`                                |         | Yes      | The number to show. When it changes, the display counts to the new value.            |
| `from`           | `number`                                |         | No       | Where to start when `animateOnMount` is on. Default 0.                               |
| `animateOnMount` | `boolean \| undefined`                  |         | No       | Count up from `from` when first shown, not only when `value` changes. Default false. |
| `duration`       | `number`                                |         | No       | Milliseconds to count over. Default 800.                                             |
| `format`         | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions \| undefined` |         | No       | `Intl.NumberFormat` options: currency, percent, decimals.                            |
| `locale`         | `string \| string[] \| undefined`       |         | No       |                                                                                      |

## Transition (page and shared-element transitions)

```tsx
import { Transition } from "@azmr/ui/transition";

<Transition name="hero">…</Transition>
```

`Transition` wraps React's `<ViewTransition>` for route changes, list changes and shared-element morphs. **That component is not in a stable React yet** (the spec expects React 19.3; React 19.2 does not have it). So `Transition` looks it up when it renders, under both its stable and experimental names, and where it is missing it renders its children and nothing else. It is safe to add today, and starts working the day you upgrade React, with no code change. It also renders nothing extra when the person prefers reduced motion. The cross-fade (opacity only) is in `styles.css`.

| Prop       | Type                           | Default | Required | Description                                                                                  |
| ---------- | ------------------------------ | ------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `children` | `ReactNode`                    |         | No       |                                                                                              |
| `name`     | `string`                       |         | No       | Gives the element a name, so the same name on another page or list item morphs between them. |
| `default`  | `TransitionClass \| undefined` |         | No       | The animation when none of the more specific ones below apply. `"none"` turns it off.        |
| `enter`    | `TransitionClass \| undefined` |         | No       |                                                                                              |
| `exit`     | `TransitionClass \| undefined` |         | No       |                                                                                              |
| `update`   | `TransitionClass \| undefined` |         | No       |                                                                                              |
| `share`    | `TransitionClass \| undefined` |         | No       | Used when this and another element share a `name` (the shared-element morph).                |

## useReducedMotion

```tsx
"use client";

import { useReducedMotion } from "@azmr/ui/hooks";

export default function ReducedMotionDemo() {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  return (
    <p className="text-sm" aria-live="polite">
      Your system is set to <strong>{reduced ? "reduce motion" : "allow motion"}</strong>. Change it
      in your operating system's accessibility settings and this updates without a reload.
    </p>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { useReducedMotion } from "@azmr/ui/hooks";

const reduced = useReducedMotion();
```

Whether the person has asked their system for reduced motion, kept up to date while the app is open. On the server and during hydration it is `false`, so there is no mismatch. The global CSS already handles CSS animations; use the hook for motion that JavaScript drives (a count-up, a canvas, a video) that CSS cannot reach.

## Tokens

| Token                                                                 | Value                   | Use                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `--motion-duration-instant` / `fast` / `base` / `slow`                | 75 / 150 / 200 / 300 ms | Press feedback, exits, enters, larger movements |
| `--motion-ease-standard` / `emphasized` / `decelerate` / `accelerate` |                         | Moves, expressive moves, entering, leaving      |
| `--motion-stagger-step`                                               | 40 ms                   | Delay between staggered items                   |
| `--motion-duration-ambient`                                           | 1500 ms                 | Loop length of ambient effects (shimmer)        |

Under reduced motion the durations become 0.01 ms (the stagger step, 0).

## The motion library (optional)

CSS covers enters, exits and state changes. For movement that follows a gesture (dragging a row, a dropped item settling, layout changes) use the [`motion`](https://motion.dev) library through `@azmr/ui/motion`. It is optional: nothing else in `@azmr/ui` imports it, and installing `@azmr/ui` does not install it.

```bash
pnpm add motion
```

`motion` is an optional peer dependency (`^14.0.0`, tested against 14.2.0). If you import `@azmr/ui/motion` without it installed, the build fails with the usual "cannot find module" error naming `motion`.

```tsx
"use client";

import { IconButton } from "@azmr/ui/button";
import { Icon } from "@azmr/ui/icons";
import { MotionProvider, Reorder, springs } from "@azmr/ui/motion";
import { ArrowDown, ArrowUp, GripVertical } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";

const initial = ["Write the brief", "Design the tokens", "Build the components", "Ship the docs"];

export default function ReorderDemo() {
  const [items, setItems] = useState(initial);

  // Dragging is not available to everyone, so every move also has buttons.
  const move = (index: number, by: -1 | 1) => {
    const next = [...items];
    const target = index + by;
    if (target < 0 || target >= next.length) return;
    [next[index], next[target]] = [next[target] as string, next[index] as string];
    setItems(next);
  };

  return (
    <MotionProvider features="max">
      <Reorder.Group
        axis="y"
        values={items}
        onReorder={setItems}
        className="flex max-w-sm flex-col gap-2"
        aria-label="Tasks, in order"
      >
        {items.map((item, index) => (
          <Reorder.Item
            key={item}
            value={item}
            transition={springs.snappy}
            className="flex items-center gap-2 rounded-md border border-border bg-card px-3 py-2 text-sm"
          >
            <Icon icon={GripVertical} className="text-muted-foreground" />
            <span className="flex-1">{item}</span>
            <IconButton
              icon={<Icon icon={ArrowUp} />}
              label={`Move "${item}" up`}
              size="sm"
              disabled={index === 0}
              onClick={() => move(index, -1)}
            />
            <IconButton
              icon={<Icon icon={ArrowDown} />}
              label={`Move "${item}" down`}
              size="sm"
              disabled={index === items.length - 1}
              onClick={() => move(index, 1)}
            />
          </Reorder.Item>
        ))}
      </Reorder.Group>
    </MotionProvider>
  );
}
```

Wrap the part of the app that animates in `MotionProvider`, then use `m` elements (or `Reorder`, `AnimatePresence`, `useAnimate` and the other re-exports):

```tsx
import { MotionProvider, m, springs } from "@azmr/ui/motion";

<MotionProvider>
  <m.div initial={{ opacity: 0 }} animate={{ opacity: 1 }} transition={springs.gentle} />
</MotionProvider>
```

`MotionProvider` sets up two things so you do not have to:

- **Lazy features.** It uses `LazyMotion`, so the animation code loads after first render instead of sitting in your main bundle. `features="dom"` (the default) covers animation, variants, hover, tap and exit. `features="max"` adds layout animation, drag and reorder, and downloads more. Either loads on demand; the wrapper itself is about 0.5 kB.
- **Reduced motion.** It sets `reducedMotion="user"`, so every animation inside follows the system setting: movement is skipped and fades still play.

By default it is **strict**: using the full `motion.div` inside it throws, so the whole library is never pulled into your bundle by accident. Use `m.div`. Pass `strict={false}` only if you accept that.

`springs` has three presets for the `transition` prop: `gentle` (a panel gliding into place), `snappy` (a control responding) and `bouncy` (a visible overshoot, used sparingly). For plain enters and exits prefer the CSS presets above, which are cheaper and follow the motion tokens.

| Prop       | Type                          | Default | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------- | ----------------------------- | ------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `children` | `ReactNode`                   |         | Yes      |                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `features` | `"dom" \| "max" \| undefined` |         | No       | What the `m` components can do. `dom` (default): animation, variants, hover, tap and exit. `max` adds layout animation, drag and reorder, at a larger download. Either loads on demand. |
| `strict`   | `boolean \| undefined`        |         | No       | Forbid the full `motion` component inside (use `m`), so the whole bundle is never pulled in by accident. Default true.                                                                  |

### Drag needs a keyboard alternative

Dragging is not available to everyone. The demo gives every row up and down buttons with names such as "Move Design the tokens up", and disables them at the ends of the list. Do the same for anything you make draggable.

## Writing your own animation

Use a token for every time and easing, animate only `transform`, `opacity`, `clip-path` (or `grid-template-rows`), and the global reduced-motion rule handles the rest. If something genuinely must keep moving under reduced motion (a progress spinner, which says "still working"), mark it `data-motion="essential"`.

## Accessibility

- Nothing is announced because it animates; motion never carries meaning on its own.
- `Collapse` content is inert while closed.
- `CountUp` exposes the final value to assistive technology immediately.
- Every preset has a reduced-motion rule, checked by tests.

---

# Packages

> Every @azmr package, what it is for, its current version and where to find its docs, changelog and source.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages

The Azmara platform is a set of small packages that work together and can each be used alone. Packages depend on each other only where they need to: `@azmr/core`, `@azmr/security` and `@azmr/db-core-interface` depend on no other `@azmr` package.

- [`@azmr/core`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/core.md): Reactive engine — signals, effects, computed values
- [`@azmr/query`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/query.md): Chainable, data-first query engine over reactive data sources
- [`@azmr/db`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/db.md): Secure SQLite persistence adapter — parameterised queries, path containment, tamper-evident audit log
- [`@azmr/db-core-interface`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/db-core-interface.md): The DbAdapter contract shared by @azmr/db and @azmr/db-supabase — types and DbAdapterError, no dependencies
- [`@azmr/db-supabase`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/db-supabase.md): Async DbAdapter implementation backed by Supabase's PostgREST query builder
- [`@azmr/ui`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/ui.md): React UI components wired to reactive Signals — Grid, useSignal
- [`@azmr/security`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/security.md): Security utilities — validation, audit logging, sanitisation, env guards
- [`@azmr/policycore`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/policycore.md): Standalone security policy engine — rate limits, auth requirements, and CORS as code for the Azmara platform
- [`@azmr/ai`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/ai.md): AI auto-fix system with capability-scoped isolated-vm sandboxing — safe code execution and analysis
- [`@azmr/cli`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/cli.md): Azmara CLI — scaffold apps, query local SQLite databases, manage your platform

---

# @azmr/core

> Reactive engine — signals, effects, and computed values.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/core

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @azmr/core
```

## Signal

A reactive value container. Any effect that reads `.get()` while active will re-run when the value changes.

```typescript
import { Signal } from "@azmr/core";

const count = new Signal(0);
count.set(1);
console.log(count.get()); // 1
console.log(count.peek()); // 1 — reads without subscribing
```

### Custom equality

`set()` uses `Object.is` by default, so setting an object/array to a new reference always notifies subscribers, even if its shape is unchanged. Pass an `equals` option to compare by shape instead:

```typescript
const shallowEqual = (a: { x: number }, b: { x: number }) => a.x === b.x;
const point = new Signal({ x: 1 }, { equals: shallowEqual });

point.set({ x: 1 }); // no-op — equals() says these are the same
```

## effect

Runs a function immediately and re-runs whenever any Signal read inside it changes. Returns a disposer that detaches the effect from every signal it read — safe to call more than once, and safe to call from inside another effect during the same flush.

```typescript
import { Signal, effect } from "@azmr/core";

const name = new Signal("Aroha");

const dispose = effect(() => {
  console.log(`Hello, ${name.get()}`);
});
// → Hello, Aroha

name.set("Tane");
// → Hello, Tane

dispose();
name.set("Mere"); // no longer logged — the effect is detached
```

> **Note**
>
> A conditional read (`cond.get() ? a.get() : b.get()`) re-evaluates its dependencies on every
> re-run, so switching branches drops the subscription to the signal in the untaken branch.

### Cleanup

The callback may return a cleanup function. It runs right before the next re-run (after stale
dependencies are dropped, before the callback runs again) and on dispose — the same shape as
React's `useEffect`.

```typescript
effect(() => {
  const id = setInterval(() => console.log(count.get()), 1000);
  return () => clearInterval(id);
});
```

## computed

A read-only Signal whose value is derived from other Signals. The returned Signal carries a `dispose()` for tearing down the derived chain.

```typescript
import { Signal, computed } from "@azmr/core";

const price = new Signal(100);
const gst = computed(() => price.get() * 0.15);

console.log(gst.get()); // 15
price.set(200);
console.log(gst.get()); // 30

gst.dispose();
price.set(9999);
console.log(gst.peek()); // 30 — frozen at its last computed value
```

### Lazy evaluation

`fn` doesn't run at creation. While the computed is unobserved — nothing reading it via `effect()`, another `computed()`, or `subscribe()` — an upstream change only marks it stale; the actual recomputation is deferred to the next `.get()`/`.peek()`, and always uses the latest values, not whatever was current when the signal changed. Once something depends on it, it switches to recomputing eagerly on every upstream change, matching the old always-eager behaviour, so an observing effect still only re-runs when the derived value itself actually changes.

```typescript
const price = new Signal(100);
const gst = computed(() => price.get() * 0.15); // fn hasn't run yet

price.set(200); // gst is unobserved — just marked stale, not recomputed
price.set(300);

gst.get(); // 45 — computes once here, from the latest value
```

> **Note**
>
> Behaviour change: a throwing `fn` used to throw synchronously from `computed(fn)` itself. It now
> throws from the first `.get()`/`.peek()` instead, since that's when `fn` actually runs.

## subscribe

Listen to a Signal from outside the reactive system — useful for bridging to React, Vue, or any non-reactive code.

```typescript
import { Signal } from "@azmr/core";

const price = new Signal(100);

const unsubscribe = price.subscribe((value) => {
  console.log(`price changed to ${value}`);
});

price.set(200); // → price changed to 200

unsubscribe(); // stop listening
```

## batch

Coalesces every `set()` call made inside a callback into a single effect flush, instead of one flush per `set()`. Values update synchronously as usual — `.get()`/`.peek()` inside the callback always see the latest write; only the effect flush is deferred. Nests correctly: an inner `batch()` completing does not trigger a flush while an outer one is still open.

```typescript
import { Signal, batch, effect } from "@azmr/core";

const first = new Signal("Aroha");
const last = new Signal("Ngata");

effect(() => console.log(`${first.get()} ${last.get()}`));
// → Aroha Ngata

batch(() => {
  first.set("Tane");
  last.set("Mahuta");
});
// → Tane Mahuta   (logged once, not twice)
```

## untrack

Runs a callback with dependency tracking suspended — any `.get()` calls made inside it (including ones buried in code you call into, not just a direct call at the top level) don't register a dependency on the currently-running effect. Unlike `.peek()`, which only works where you control the call site, `untrack()` composes through indirection — it works even when the callback calls third-party or generic code that uses `.get()` internally. A no-op outside an effect. An effect created inside the callback still tracks its own reads normally.

```typescript
import { Signal, effect, untrack } from "@azmr/core";

const count = new Signal(0);
const debugFlag = new Signal(false);

effect(() => {
  // Reacts to count, but reading debugFlag here should never itself
  // trigger a re-run — it's just checked, not depended on.
  if (untrack(() => debugFlag.get())) console.log(`count: ${count.get()}`);
});
```

## onError

Registers a handler for errors thrown by an `effect()` re-run or a `subscribe()` callback during a flush. Without this, one bad subscriber's exception propagates out of an unrelated caller's `set()` and aborts every other subscriber still pending in that flush; with a handler registered, the error is routed here instead and the flush continues. Returns a function that restores whichever handler was active before the call. Doesn't apply to `effect(fn)`'s first, synchronous run, or to a direct `fn()` call inside `batch()`/`untrack()` — those still throw normally to the caller, who is right there to catch them.

```typescript
import { Signal, effect, onError } from "@azmr/core";

const restore = onError((error) => {
  console.error("effect failed:", error);
});

const count = new Signal(0);
effect(() => {
  if (count.get() > 10) throw new Error("too high");
});

restore(); // back to the previous handler (none by default)
```

> **Note**
>
> If no handler is registered, the error is rethrown asynchronously (via a resolved Promise) so
> it isn't silently swallowed, without blocking the flush that surfaced it.

## Safety

The scheduler uses a generation counter to prevent effects from running more than once per flush cycle. An effect that reads and writes the same signal will run at most twice — the re-queue is deduplicated, preventing unbounded loops.

```typescript
const s = new Signal(0);

// Safe — deduplicated by the scheduler, never runs unboundedly
effect(() => {
  s.get();
  s.set(s.peek() + 1);
});
```

## API Reference

### `Signal<T>`

Constructor: `new Signal(initialValue, options?)`. `options.equals` replaces the default `Object.is` check `set()` uses to decide whether a write is a no-op.

| Method          | Returns      | Description                                       |
| --------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `get()`         | `T`          | Read value and subscribe current effect           |
| `set(value)`    | `void`       | Update value and notify subscribers               |
| `peek()`        | `T`          | Read value without subscribing                    |
| `subscribe(fn)` | `() => void` | Register a callback, returns unsubscribe function |

### Functions

| Function           | Description                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `effect(fn)`       | Run `fn` reactively, returns a disposer that fully detaches it                                             |
| `computed(fn)`     | Create a derived read-only Signal, computed lazily; return value has a `dispose()`                         |
| `batch(fn)`        | Coalesce `set()` calls inside `fn` into one flush; returns `fn`'s return value                             |
| `untrack(fn)`      | Run `fn` with dependency tracking suspended; returns `fn`'s return value                                   |
| `onError(handler)` | Register a handler for errors thrown during a flush; returns a function that restores the previous handler |

---

# @azmr/query

> Chainable, data-first query builder over arrays or reactive Signals.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/query

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @azmr/query @azmr/core
```

## Basic usage

```typescript
import { query } from "@azmr/query";

const customers = [
  { name: "Aroha", balance: 150 },
  { name: "Tane", balance: 0 },
  { name: "Mere", balance: 320 },
];

const result = query(customers)
  .where(c => c.balance > 0)
  .orderBy((a, b) => b.balance - a.balance)
  .limit(10)
  .select();
// → [{ name: "Mere", balance: 320 }, { name: "Aroha", balance: 150 }]
```

## With a reactive Signal

```typescript
import { Signal } from "@azmr/core";
import { query } from "@azmr/query";

const data = new Signal(customers);

const active = query(data)
  .where(c => c.balance > 0)
  .select();
```

## API Reference

| Method         | Description                                |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `.where(fn)`   | Filter rows — predicate must be a function |
| `.orderBy(fn)` | Sort with a comparator `(a, b) => number`  |
| `.limit(n)`    | Return at most `n` rows                    |
| `.offset(n)`   | Skip first `n` rows                        |
| `.select()`    | Execute and return results array           |
| `.count()`     | Return count of matching rows              |
| `.first()`     | Return first match or `undefined`          |

## Security

All predicates must be TypeScript functions — string-based queries throw a `TypeError`. This prevents eval injection at the type and runtime level.

```typescript
// ✅ Safe — TypeScript function
query(data).where(c => c.balance > 0)

// ❌ Throws TypeError — string predicates rejected
query(data).where("balance > 0" as any)
```

---

# @azmr/db

> Secure, async SQLite persistence adapter built on better-sqlite3.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/db

> **Cloud alternative**
>
> Need a hosted Postgres backend instead of local SQLite? `@azmr/db-supabase` implements the same
> `DbAdapter` interface via Supabase/PostgREST — swap adapters without changing calling code.

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @azmr/db
```

## Usage

Every method is asynchronous — `SQLiteAdapter` implements the shared, storage-agnostic `DbAdapter` interface (also implemented by `@azmr/db-supabase`'s `SupabaseAdapter`).

```typescript
import { SQLiteAdapter } from "@azmr/db";

const db = new SQLiteAdapter(".azmara/db/app.db", ".azmara/db");

await db.createTable("customers", {
  name: "string",
  balance: "number",
  active: "boolean",
});

await db.insert("customers", { name: "Aroha", balance: 150, active: 1 });
await db.insertMany("customers", [
  { name: "Tane", balance: 0, active: 0 },
  { name: "Mere", balance: 320, active: 1 },
]);

const all = await db.getAll<{ name: string; balance: number }>("customers");
```

## Filtering

`findWhere` and `deleteWhere` take a structured `Filter` — an array of `{ column, operator, value }` conditions (implicitly AND-combined) — instead of raw SQL fragments. This is the same shape `@azmr/db-supabase` compiles to a PostgREST filter chain, so query code is portable between backends.

```typescript
const active = await db.findWhere("customers", [
  { column: "active", operator: "eq", value: 1 },
  { column: "balance", operator: "gt", value: 100 },
]);

const removed = await db.deleteWhere("customers", [
  { column: "active", operator: "eq", value: 0 },
]);
// removed: number of rows deleted
```

| Prop       | Type             | Default | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `column`   | `string`         |         | Yes      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `operator` | `FilterOperator` |         | Yes      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `value`    | `unknown`        |         | Yes      | - "in" -> array of values (empty array means zero rows, matching PostgREST's \`.in(col, \[])\`) - "is" -> null \| boolean only (PostgREST's IS operator is restricted to these) - "like"/"ilike" -> string pattern, %/\_ wildcards (SQL LIKE convention) - all others -> scalar |

## The `DbAdapter` interface

`SQLiteAdapter` and `@azmr/db-supabase`'s `SupabaseAdapter` both implement this shared, storage-agnostic interface — code written against `DbAdapter` works unchanged against either backend.

| Prop            | Type                                                                            | Default | Required | Description                                                                                     |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `createTable`   | `(name: string, schema: ColumnSchema) => Promise<void>`                         |         | Yes      |                                                                                                 |
| `insert`        | `<T extends Record<string, unknown>>(name: string, row: T) => Promise<void>`    |         | Yes      |                                                                                                 |
| `insertMany`    | `<T extends Record<string, unknown>>(name: string, rows: T[]) => Promise<void>` |         | Yes      |                                                                                                 |
| `getAll`        | `<T = unknown>(name: string) => Promise<T[]>`                                   |         | Yes      |                                                                                                 |
| `findWhere`     | `<T = unknown>(name: string, filter: Filter) => Promise<T[]>`                   |         | Yes      |                                                                                                 |
| `truncateTable` | `(name: string) => Promise<void>`                                               |         | Yes      |                                                                                                 |
| `deleteWhere`   | `(name: string, filter: Filter) => Promise<number>`                             |         | Yes      |                                                                                                 |
| `close`         | `() => Promise<void>`                                                           |         | Yes      | Release any held resources. No-op for adapters without a persistent connection (e.g. Supabase). |

### Interface-only import: `@azmr/db-core-interface`

> **Note**
>
> The `DbAdapter` contract lives in its own package, `@azmr/db-core-interface`, with no
> dependencies. `@azmr/db`'s root export includes `SQLiteAdapter`, which pulls in
> `better-sqlite3` — a native, node-gyp-built module. If you only need the
> `DbAdapter`/`DbAdapterError`/`Filter` types (for example, building a new adapter, or consuming
> `@azmr/db-supabase`), depend on `@azmr/db-core-interface` and nothing else is installed.

```typescript
import type { DbAdapter, Filter } from "@azmr/db-core-interface";
import { DbAdapterError } from "@azmr/db-core-interface";
```

`@azmr/db/interface` still works and re-exports exactly the same things (the same
`DbAdapterError` class, so `instanceof` checks hold across both imports), but it installs
`better-sqlite3` with `@azmr/db`. `@azmr/db-supabase` depends on `@azmr/db-core-interface`, not on
`@azmr/db`, for exactly this reason. See [`@azmr/db-core-interface`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/db-core-interface.md).

## Security features

> **Warning**
>
> All table and column names are validated against `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*` before any SQL is
> executed. Unsafe identifiers throw immediately.

| Feature               | Detail                                                    |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Parameterised queries | No string concatenation — ever                            |
| Identifier validation | Table/column names regex-validated before SQL             |
| Path containment      | `allowedBase` prevents path traversal                     |
| WAL journal mode      | Write-ahead logging for integrity and performance         |
| `secure_delete`       | Deleted data overwritten with zeros                       |
| `foreign_keys ON`     | Referential integrity enforced                            |
| Audit log             | Every mutation written to hash-chained tamper-evident log |

## API Reference

| Method                       | Description                                                               |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `createTable(name, schema)`  | Create table if not exists                                                |
| `insert(name, row)`          | Insert a single row (parameterised)                                       |
| `insertMany(name, rows)`     | Insert multiple rows in a transaction                                     |
| `getAll<T>(name)`            | Return all rows typed as `T[]`                                            |
| `findWhere<T>(name, filter)` | Return rows matching a structured `Filter`                                |
| `truncateTable(name)`        | Delete all rows from a table (keeps schema)                               |
| `deleteWhere(name, filter)`  | Delete rows matching a structured `Filter`, returns count deleted         |
| `close()`                    | Close the database connection                                             |
| `rawSelect(sql, params)`     | SQLite-only escape hatch — not part of the shared `DbAdapter` interface   |
| `db.path`                    | Resolved path to the database file — SQLite-only, not part of `DbAdapter` |

## Column types

| Schema type | SQLite type        |
| ----------- | ------------------ |
| `"string"`  | `TEXT NOT NULL`    |
| `"number"`  | `REAL NOT NULL`    |
| `"boolean"` | `INTEGER NOT NULL` |

---

# @azmr/db-core-interface

> The DbAdapter contract shared by @azmr/db and @azmr/db-supabase — types and DbAdapterError, with no dependencies.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/db-core-interface

`@azmr/db-core-interface` is the storage-agnostic persistence contract: the `DbAdapter` interface, its filter and schema types, and the `DbAdapterError` class. It has no dependencies, so it can be installed on its own, in any runtime, without `better-sqlite3` or Supabase.

Both adapters implement it:

| Package             | Backend                                  |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `@azmr/db`          | Local SQLite (`SQLiteAdapter`)           |
| `@azmr/db-supabase` | Supabase / PostgREST (`SupabaseAdapter`) |

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @azmr/db-core-interface
```

You normally do not install it directly: `@azmr/db` and `@azmr/db-supabase` depend on it. Install it yourself when you write against `DbAdapter` without choosing a backend, or when you build a new adapter (Postgres, D1, in-memory).

## The `DbAdapter` interface

| Prop            | Type                                                                            | Default | Required | Description                                                                                     |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `createTable`   | `(name: string, schema: ColumnSchema) => Promise<void>`                         |         | Yes      |                                                                                                 |
| `insert`        | `<T extends Record<string, unknown>>(name: string, row: T) => Promise<void>`    |         | Yes      |                                                                                                 |
| `insertMany`    | `<T extends Record<string, unknown>>(name: string, rows: T[]) => Promise<void>` |         | Yes      |                                                                                                 |
| `getAll`        | `<T = unknown>(name: string) => Promise<T[]>`                                   |         | Yes      |                                                                                                 |
| `findWhere`     | `<T = unknown>(name: string, filter: Filter) => Promise<T[]>`                   |         | Yes      |                                                                                                 |
| `truncateTable` | `(name: string) => Promise<void>`                                               |         | Yes      |                                                                                                 |
| `deleteWhere`   | `(name: string, filter: Filter) => Promise<number>`                             |         | Yes      |                                                                                                 |
| `close`         | `() => Promise<void>`                                                           |         | Yes      | Release any held resources. No-op for adapters without a persistent connection (e.g. Supabase). |

Deliberately left out: `rawSelect` (arbitrary SQL, a SQLite-only escape hatch that PostgREST cannot implement) and the `path` getter. Code that needs those depends on `SQLiteAdapter` directly.

## Filters

Conditions are implicitly AND-combined. There is no OR support yet.

| Prop       | Type             | Default | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `column`   | `string`         |         | Yes      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `operator` | `FilterOperator` |         | Yes      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `value`    | `unknown`        |         | Yes      | - "in" -> array of values (empty array means zero rows, matching PostgREST's \`.in(col, \[])\`) - "is" -> null \| boolean only (PostgREST's IS operator is restricted to these) - "like"/"ilike" -> string pattern, %/\_ wildcards (SQL LIKE convention) - all others -> scalar |

## Errors

Adapters throw `DbAdapterError` when an operation fails. It carries the optional `code`, `details`, `hint` and `cause` the backend reported.

```typescript
import { DbAdapterError } from "@azmr/db-core-interface";

try {
  await db.insert("customers", { id: 1 });
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof DbAdapterError) {
    console.error(error.code, error.hint);
  }
}
```

> **Note**
>
> `DbAdapterError` is a class, so `instanceof` only works if your app ends up with one copy of this
> package. `@azmr/db` and `@azmr/db-supabase` re-use the same class, and `@azmr/db/interface`
> re-exports it, so mixing those imports is safe. If a lock file ever holds two versions of
> `@azmr/db-core-interface`, deduplicate them.

## Writing against the interface

Code that takes a `DbAdapter` runs unchanged against either backend:

```typescript
import type { DbAdapter, Filter } from "@azmr/db-core-interface";

const active: Filter = [{ column: "active", operator: "eq", value: 1 }];

export async function countActive(db: DbAdapter, table: string): Promise<number> {
  return (await db.findWhere(table, active)).length;
}
```

When you build your own adapter, implement every `DbAdapter` method and throw `DbAdapterError` (never a backend-specific error), so callers handle failures the same way against every backend.

## Requirements

- Node.js ≥ 18
- TypeScript ≥ 5 (types included)
- ESM only

---

# @azmr/db-supabase

> A DbAdapter backed by Supabase's PostgREST query builder, the cloud counterpart to the SQLite adapter in @azmr/db.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/db-supabase

`@azmr/db-supabase` implements the same [`DbAdapter`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/db-core-interface.md) interface as [`@azmr/db`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/db.md)'s `SQLiteAdapter`, but stores data in Supabase (Postgres). Code written against `DbAdapter` runs against either backend without changes.

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @azmr/db-supabase @supabase/supabase-js
```

`@supabase/supabase-js` is a peer dependency: bring your own client, so you keep full control over auth, session and cookie wiring (for example `@supabase/ssr`'s browser and server client constructors).

## Usage

```typescript
import { createClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";
import { SupabaseAdapter } from "@azmr/db-supabase";

const client = createClient(process.env.SUPABASE_URL!, process.env.SUPABASE_KEY!);
const db = new SupabaseAdapter(client);

await db.insert("products", { name: "Widget A", price: 9.99 });

const inStock = await db.findWhere("products", [
  { column: "inStock", operator: "is", value: true },
]);
```

Row Level Security is enforced by whatever JWT the `SupabaseClient` you pass in carries. This package never constructs its own client and never bypasses that.

## What is different from SQLiteAdapter

- **Async throughout.** Every method returns a `Promise`, because PostgREST is a network call.
- **No `rawSelect`.** PostgREST does not accept arbitrary SQL. Use `findWhere` with a structured filter instead.
- **`createTable` always throws.** PostgREST cannot run DDL, so this package is bring-your-own-schema: manage tables with the Supabase SQL editor, CLI migrations or the dashboard.

```ts
import { SupabaseAdapter } from "@azmr/db-supabase";

// `client` is your SupabaseClient. This call never reaches it.
const db = new SupabaseAdapter(client);

let message;
try {
  await db.createTable("products", { name: "string" });
} catch (error) {
  message = error.message;
}
// => "[azmara/db-supabase] createTable(\"products\") is not supported — PostgREST cannot execute DDL. Create/manage this table via the Supabase SQL editor, CLI migrations, or dashboard."
```

## Errors

Every `{ data, error }` result from `supabase-js` is checked. On failure the adapter throws a `DbAdapterError` that carries the original Postgres error's `code`, `details` and `hint`, with the raw error as `cause`. Nothing is swallowed.

Because the adapter only calls the client you give it, you can test code that uses it with a stub. This one fails the way Postgres does when a policy denies a read:

```ts
const denied = { message: "boom", code: "42501", details: "d", hint: "h" };
const failing = new SupabaseAdapter({
  from: () => ({ select: () => Promise.resolve({ data: null, error: denied }) }),
});

let fields;
try {
  await failing.getAll("products");
} catch (error) {
  fields = { name: error.name, message: error.message, code: error.code, details: error.details, hint: error.hint };
}
// => {"name":"DbAdapterError","message":"[azmara/db-supabase] getAll(\"products\") failed: boom","code":"42501","details":"d","hint":"h"}
```

## Filters

`findWhere` and `deleteWhere` take a `Filter`: a list of conditions that are combined with AND. There is no OR yet.

```typescript
type Filter = Array<{
  column: string;
  operator: "eq" | "neq" | "gt" | "gte" | "lt" | "lte" | "like" | "ilike" | "is" | "in";
  value: unknown;
}>;
```

See [`@azmr/db-core-interface`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/db-core-interface.md) for what each operator expects.

## Runtime footprint

`@azmr/db-supabase` depends on [`@azmr/db-core-interface`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/db-core-interface.md) (the contract) and `@azmr/security`, and **not** on `@azmr/db`. Installing it does not install `better-sqlite3` or any other native module, so it is safe to bundle into serverless and edge runtimes (Vercel, Next.js server components and actions, Cloudflare Workers).

Versions 0.2.1 and earlier depended on `@azmr/db` for the interface, which installed `better-sqlite3` even though it was never loaded.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or later
- `@supabase/supabase-js` ^2.103.0
- ESM only: `require("@azmr/db-supabase")` does not work; use `import`.

---

# @azmr/ui

> React components wired to reactive Signals.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/ui

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @azmr/ui @azmr/core react react-dom
```

`@azmr/core` is a **peer dependency**: install it yourself so your app and `@azmr/ui` share one copy. Two copies give incompatible `Signal` types and separate scheduler state.

## Styles and design tokens

`@azmr/ui` ships the design tokens and the Tailwind v4 theme mapping in two stylesheets. In your global CSS, pick one:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@azmr/ui/styles.css";   /* tokens + global base rules (new app) */
```

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@azmr/ui/tokens.css";   /* tokens only (app that already has global styles) */
```

- **`styles.css`** is `tokens.css` plus two global base rules: the page background and text colour on `body`, and our border and outline colours as the default for every element. Use it in a new app.

- **`tokens.css`** has the same tokens, themes, density, motion and utilities and **changes nothing outside our own classes**. Use it when the app already has global styles: another UI library mid-migration, or a documentation site. Components look right either way.

- **Token names follow shadcn/ui** (`--background`, `--primary`, `--ring`, `--radius`, `--sidebar-*`, ...), so shadcn components from any registry look right next to ours. Azmara adds `--success`, `--warning`, `--info`, `--chart-1` to `--chart-8`, `--motion-*`, `--elevation-*`, `--z-*` and `--density-*`.

- **Utilities** such as `bg-background`, `text-muted-foreground`, `rounded-lg`, `shadow-elevation-2` and `ease-standard` work out of the box. The stylesheets include an `@source` rule, so Tailwind scans the package's classes inside `node_modules`.

- **Light and dark** use OKLCH colours with `light-dark()`. The page follows the system by default; force a mode with `class="dark"` / `class="light"` or `data-theme="dark|light"` on any ancestor. No JavaScript, no flash.

- **Density:** set `data-density="compact"` or `"spacious"` on any ancestor to change control heights, padding and row height.

- **Reduced motion:** with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, every `--motion-duration-*` token collapses to `0.01ms` and a safety net shortens other animations. Mark genuinely essential motion with `data-motion="essential"`.

- **Accessibility is tested:** every foreground/background token pair meets WCAG AA text contrast (4.5:1) in both modes, the focus ring and chart colours meet 3:1, and the eight chart colours stay distinguishable under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia simulation.

## Theme, density and locale

For brand colours, dark mode, density and what `createTheme` guarantees, see the [Theming guide](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/theming.md); every token is listed in the [token reference](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/tokens.md).

**Server layout (Next.js App Router).** Read the stored preference from the cookie on the server and render it into `<html>`, so the first paint is already correct, with no inline script (works under a strict CSP):

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import { cookies } from "next/headers";
import { htmlAttributes, parseDensity, parseThemePreference, THEME_COOKIE, DENSITY_COOKIE } from "@azmr/ui/theme";
import { LocaleProvider, ThemeProvider } from "@azmr/ui/react";

export default async function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const jar = await cookies();
  const theme = parseThemePreference(jar.get(THEME_COOKIE)?.value);
  const density = parseDensity(jar.get(DENSITY_COOKIE)?.value);
  return (
    <html lang="en-NZ" {...htmlAttributes({ theme, density })}>
      <body>
        <ThemeProvider defaultTheme={theme} defaultDensity={density}>
          <LocaleProvider locale="en-NZ" currency="NZD">{children}</LocaleProvider>
        </ThemeProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

- `system` (the default) needs no attribute and no JavaScript: the tokens use `light-dark()`, so the page follows the operating system.
- `useTheme()` returns `{ theme, resolvedTheme, setTheme, density, setDensity }`. Changes update `<html>` immediately and are remembered in a cookie (`persist={false}` turns that off).
- Static sites that cannot read cookies on the server can inline `themeInitScript()` instead (add your CSP nonce to the tag).
- `createTheme({ primary, secondary, success, warning, info, destructive, radius, font, density })` turns brand colours (`#rrggbb`, `oklch(L C H)` or `{ l, c, h }`) into token overrides. Every colour option is optional and keeps its default when omitted (`destructive` is the "danger" colour). It guarantees WCAG AA in both modes, adjusting lightness where needed and keeping the hue:
  - each `-foreground` is at least 4.5:1 on its colour, **including on a solid button's hover surface** (a button blends with the page on hover, which can pull a colour that only just passes below 4.5:1; the derivation checks the blend);
  - `success`, `info` and `destructive` are also readable as **text** on the page and on cards (`Text tone`, form errors), and `warning` gets a separate readable `--warning-text`;
  - the focus ring is at least 3:1.
    Input is validated strictly because the output is CSS, and an error names the option that was wrong.

```tsx
import { createTheme } from "@azmr/ui/theme";
const theme = createTheme({
  primary: "#1E88E5",
  success: "#2E7D32",
  destructive: "#D32F2F",
  radius: "0.5rem",
});
// <style>{theme.css}</style>   or   <html style={theme.cssVariables}>
```

**Locale.** `LocaleProvider` defaults to `en-NZ`, `NZD` and a Monday week start. `useLocale()` gives cached `Intl` formatters (`formatNumber`, `formatCurrency`, `formatDate`, `formatDateTime`) and the strings components show (`messages`, overridable). Date-only strings such as `2026-10-15` print that calendar day in every time zone; missing or invalid values format to an empty string instead of throwing.

## Components

Components read the design tokens only (no raw colours), accept `className` (merged last, so it can override defaults), forward `ref` to the real DOM element, and follow the density tokens for height and padding. Import from the root or from a subpath; subpaths and the root are both tree-shakeable.

### Button

```tsx
import { Button } from "@azmr/ui/button";

<Button>Save</Button>
<Button variant="destructive" loading loadingText="Deleting">Delete</Button>
<Button variant="outline" startIcon={<PlusIcon />}>New customer</Button>
<Button size="icon" aria-label="Close"><XIcon /></Button>            {/* icon-only needs a name */}
<Button nativeButton={false} render={<a href="/docs" />}>Docs</Button>   {/* renders a link */}
```

- **Variants:** `default`, `secondary`, `outline`, `ghost`, `destructive`, `success`, `warning`, `info`, `link`. **Sizes:** `sm`, `md` (follows the density token), `lg`, `icon`.
- **`loading`:** shows a spinner, sets `aria-busy`, ignores clicks and keyboard activation, **stays focusable** (keyboard users keep their place). `loadingText` replaces the label while loading; `startIcon` is replaced by the spinner, `endIcon` stays.
- **`type` is `"button"` by default**, so a button inside a form never submits by accident; pass `type="submit"` explicitly.
- **Icon-only buttons are type-checked:** `size="icon"` requires `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

### Input

```tsx
import { Input } from "@azmr/ui/input";
import { useForm } from "react-hook-form";

const { register } = useForm();
<label htmlFor="email">Email</label>
<Input id="email" type="email" {...register("email")} />   {/* no Controller needed */}
```

`ref` is the real `<input>`, so `register()` works directly. Native `onChange` and the typed `onValueChange(value)` both fire. `aria-invalid="true"` styles the invalid state; focus uses a full-strength ring (WCAG 2.2 focus appearance).

### Spinner

`<Spinner />` is decorative; `<Spinner label="Loading customers" />` is announced as a status. It keeps spinning under `prefers-reduced-motion` because a frozen spinner reads as a hung page.

## Icons

`Icon` renders any icon component with consistent size, stroke, motion and accessibility. It is a **Server Component** (no hooks, no `"use client"`), so it works in `loading.tsx`, layouts and Suspense fallbacks.

```tsx
import { Icon } from "@azmr/ui/icons";
import { Search } from "lucide-react";
import { IconBell } from "@tabler/icons-react";   // optional: any set, or your own SVG component

<Icon icon={Search} />                              {/* decorative: aria-hidden */}
<Icon icon={Search} aria-label="Search" size="lg" /> {/* meaningful: role="img" + name */}
<Icon icon={IconBell} strokeWidth={1.5} />
<Icon icon={Loader} spin />                          {/* keeps spinning under reduced motion */}
```

- **Sizes:** `xs`, `sm`, `md` (default), `lg`, `xl` follow the size tokens; a number is a pixel size. `className` merges last, so `className="size-8"` wins.
- **Accessible by default:** decorative (`aria-hidden`) unless you pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. An icon-only button is named by a labelled icon.
- **Bring any set.** Lucide (ISC) is the default; Tabler (MIT) and your own SVG components work through the same `icon` prop with no adapter. `react-icons` is deliberately not bundled: it mixes licences and only tree-shakes through exact subpath imports.
- **Tree-shaking is tested:** the Icon core bundles no icon at all, and an app that imports one icon bundles that icon only.

**By name.** Three ways, from most to least isolated:

```tsx
// 1. The curated Lucide set, with typed names (about 60 everyday icons; Lucide's own kebab-case names)
import { Icon } from "@azmr/ui/icons/lucide";
<Icon name="circle-alert" />

// 2. Your own typed set: nothing global, only the icons you list are bundled
import { createIconSet } from "@azmr/ui/icons";
export const { Icon } = createIconSet({ check: Check, "my-logo": MyLogo });

// 3. A global registry for custom SVGs (names are untyped strings)
import { registerIcons } from "@azmr/ui/icons";
registerIcons({ "my-logo": MyLogo });   // then <Icon name="my-logo" />
```

An unknown name renders nothing and logs one development warning; it never crashes the page.

**Migrating from `@mui/icons-material`.** `@azmr/ui/icons/mui-map` is plain data: `resolveMuiIcon("SearchOutlined")` returns `{ name: "Search", variant: "outlined", lucide: "search", tabler: "IconSearch" }`. It covers over 300 common Material icons, strips the `Outlined` / `Rounded` / `Sharp` / `TwoTone` variants (and the legacy `Outline` spelling older MUI versions export), maps brand icons to Tabler only (Lucide has none), and lists the common names it deliberately does not map in `unmappedMuiIcons`. Every name in it is checked by tests against the real `@mui/icons-material`, `lucide-react` and `@tabler/icons-react`. The migration codemod uses it and reports anything unmapped instead of guessing.

## Entry points

| Import                   | Contents                                                                            | Directive                                              |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `@azmr/ui`               | everything (`Grid`, `useSignal`, `cn`)                                              | `"use client"`                                         |
| `@azmr/ui/hooks`         | React hooks (`useSignal`)                                                           | `"use client"`                                         |
| `@azmr/ui/theme`         | server-safe theme helpers: `createTheme`, cookies, `htmlAttributes`, `createLocale` | none, importable from Server Components and middleware |
| `@azmr/ui/react`         | `ThemeProvider`, `useTheme`, `LocaleProvider`, `useLocale`                          | `"use client"`                                         |
| `@azmr/ui/button`        | `Button`, `buttonVariants`                                                          | `"use client"`                                         |
| `@azmr/ui/input`         | `Input`                                                                             | `"use client"`                                         |
| `@azmr/ui/spinner`       | `Spinner`                                                                           | none, importable from Server Components                |
| `@azmr/ui/icons`         | `Icon`, `createIconSet`, `registerIcons`                                            | none, importable from Server Components                |
| `@azmr/ui/icons/lucide`  | `Icon` bound to the curated Lucide set, `lucideIcons`                               | none, importable from Server Components                |
| `@azmr/ui/icons/mui-map` | `resolveMuiIcon`, `muiIconMap`, `unmappedMuiIcons` (migration data)                 | none, pure data                                        |
| `@azmr/ui/lib`           | `cn()` and other server-safe helpers                                                | none, importable from Server Components                |

`cn(...classes)` merges class names and resolves conflicting Tailwind utilities, with the last one winning: `cn("p-2", "p-4")` returns `"p-4"`.

## Grid

A reactive data grid that automatically re-renders when its Signal updates.

```tsx
import { Signal } from "@azmr/core";
import { Grid } from "@azmr/ui";

const customers = new Signal([
  { name: "Aroha", balance: 150 },
  { name: "Mere", balance: 320 },
]);

function App() {
  return (
    <Grid
      signal={customers}
      labels={{ name: "Customer", balance: "Balance ($)" }}
    />
  );
}
```

When `customers.set([...])` is called, the grid updates automatically — no state management needed.

## useSignal

Hook to subscribe a React component to any Signal. Uses `Signal.subscribe()` for push-based updates — the component re-renders only when the signal value actually changes.

```tsx
import { useSignal } from "@azmr/ui";

function Counter({ count }: { count: Signal<number> }) {
  const value = useSignal(count);
  return <span>{value}</span>;
}
```

## API Reference

### `<Grid />`

| Prop           | Type                               | Description                      |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `signal`       | `Signal<T[]>`                      | Reactive data source             |
| `columns`      | `(keyof T)[]`                      | Optional column order            |
| `labels`       | `Partial<Record<keyof T, string>>` | Optional column label overrides  |
| `emptyMessage` | `string`                           | Message shown when data is empty |

### `useSignal<T>(signal)`

Returns the current Signal value and subscribes the component to updates. Built on `useSyncExternalStore`, so it's safe under React 18/19 concurrent rendering — no tearing between a signal update and a render that's mid-flight.

## Security

All cell values are rendered through React's JSX escaping. `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is never used.

---

# @azmr/ai

> AI auto-fix system with true V8 isolate sandboxing.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/ai

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @azmr/ai
```

> **Native module**
>
> `@azmr/ai` uses `isolated-vm` which requires compilation. See
> [Installation](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/guide/installation.md#native-module-note).

## Sandbox

Run untrusted code inside a V8 isolate with no access to Node.js, the file system, or the network by default.

```typescript
import { runSandbox } from "@azmr/ai";

const result = await runSandbox(`
  const x = [1, 2, 3].reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
  x;
`);

if (result.success) {
  console.log(result.output); // 6
} else {
  console.error(result.error);
}
```

Optionally expose scoped capabilities (e.g. `createFileReadCapability`) via a `capabilities` option — see [AI Sandbox](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/security/sandbox.md) for the full capabilities guide, including the current synchronous-handler-only limitation.

## Auto-Fix

AI-powered file improvement pipeline with mandatory sandbox check before applying. The platform does not supply a default model backend — bring your own `ModelAdapter`.

```typescript
import { autoFix } from "@azmr/ai";
import type { ModelAdapter } from "@azmr/ai";

const adapter: ModelAdapter = {
  async suggest(context) {
    // call your own model backend
    return "...";
  },
};

const result = await autoFix(
  "src/index.ts",
  "src",     // allowedBase — prevents path traversal
  adapter,   // your ModelAdapter — required, no default
  { autoApprove: false }, // manual review by default
);
```

> **Warning**
>
> The fix is sandboxed and logged to the audit trail before being applied.

## API Reference

### `runSandbox(code, options?)`

| Property           | Value                                               |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Memory limit       | 64 MB                                               |
| Timeout            | 5 seconds                                           |
| Node.js API access | None                                                |
| File system access | None by default — opt in via `options.capabilities` |

Returns `{ success: boolean, output?: unknown, error?: string, _sandboxEngine }`.

### `createFileReadCapability(allowedBase, options?)`

Scoped, read-only, synchronous file-read capability for `runSandbox`'s `capabilities` option.

### `autoFix(filePath, allowedBase, adapter, options)`

| Parameter | Description                                                        |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `adapter` | Your `ModelAdapter` implementation — required, no default supplied |

| Option        | Default | Description                                 |
| ------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `autoApprove` | `false` | Apply fix automatically after sandbox check |

---

# @azmr/security

> Shared security utilities — validation, RBAC, JWT, audit logging, sanitisation, and env guards.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/security

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @azmr/security
```

## Validation

```typescript
import { validate, z } from "@azmr/security";

const UserSchema = z.object({
  name: z.string().min(1).max(100),
  email: z.string().email(),
  balance: z.number().nonnegative(),
});

const user = validate(UserSchema, req.body);
// Throws structured error on failure — never leaks raw input
```

## Environment guard

Call once at startup to fail fast if required env vars are missing.

```typescript
import { validateEnv } from "@azmr/security";

validateEnv(["OPENAI_API_KEY", "AZMARA_ENCRYPTION_KEY"]);
```

## Access control (RBAC)

`createAccessControl` is a framework-agnostic role-based access control primitive: `{resource, action, params} → {can, reason}`. Policy is a static grant map keyed by role, with `"*"` wildcards for role/resource/action and fail-closed defaults.

```typescript
import { createAccessControl } from "@azmr/security";

const ac = createAccessControl({
  policy: {
    admin: [{ resource: "*", action: "*" }],
    editor: [{ resource: "reports", action: "read" }],
  },
  defaultEffect: "deny",
});

const result = await ac.can({ id: "u1", roles: ["editor"] }, {
  resource: "reports",
  action: "read",
});
// { can: true }
```

An optional `resolve` callback lets a caller back checks with a database or any other backend — the package never imports a DB client itself.

| Prop            | Type                                                                                                                                                                         | Default | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `policy`        | `Policy`                                                                                                                                                                     |         | No       | Static in-memory policy.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `resolve`       | `((subject: AccessControlSubject \| null, query: AccessCheckQuery) => Promise<AccessCheckResult \| boolean> \| AccessCheckResult \| boolean) \| undefined`                   |         | No       | Optional resolver for dynamic/DB-backed checks, consulted only when the static policy does not already grant access. This is the seam a caller uses to back checks with a Supabase RPC, a policy table, or anything else — |
| `defaultEffect` | `"allow" \| "deny" \| undefined`                                                                                                                                             |         | No       | What to return when neither policy nor resolve decide. Defaults to "deny" (fail closed).                                                                                                                                   |
| `onDecision`    | `((event: { subject: AccessControlSubject \| null; query: AccessCheckQuery; result: AccessCheckResult; source: "policy" \| "resolve" \| "default"; }) => void) \| undefined` |         | No       | Optional hook fired after every decision — wire this to createAuditLogger if you want checks audited.                                                                                                                      |

## JWT

```typescript
import { createJWT } from "@azmr/security";

const jwt = createJWT(process.env.AZMARA_JWT_SECRET!); // must be >= 32 chars

const token = jwt.sign({ sub: "u1" });
const payload = jwt.verify(token); // throws on invalid/expired
```

HMAC-SHA256, Node `crypto` only, timing-safe signature comparison, default 15-minute expiry.

## Rate limiting

```typescript
import { createRateLimiter } from "@azmr/security";

const limiter = createRateLimiter({ maxRequests: 100, windowMs: 60_000 });

const result = limiter.check(userId);
if (!result.allowed) {
  // result.remaining === 0, result.resetAt is a Date
}
```

In-memory sliding window, keyed per caller. Not distributed-safe — use a Redis-backed limiter for multi-process deployments.

## Audit logger

```typescript
import { createAuditLogger } from "@azmr/security";

const audit = createAuditLogger("my-service");
audit.log("user:login", { userId: "abc123" });
```

See [Audit Logging](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/security/audit-logging.md) for full details.

## Sanitisation

```typescript
import { assertSafeIdentifier, assertSafePath, sanitiseForLog } from "@azmr/security";

assertSafeIdentifier("customers");       // passes
assertSafeIdentifier("users; DROP TABLE"); // throws

assertSafePath("/data/user.db", "/data"); // passes
assertSafePath("../../etc/passwd", "/data"); // throws

sanitiseForLog(userInput); // strips null bytes, flattens newlines, truncates
```

## API Reference

| Export                         | Description                                             |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `validate(schema, data)`       | Zod parse with structured error                         |
| `validateEnv(keys)`            | Assert env vars present at startup                      |
| `createAccessControl(options)` | RBAC: `{resource, action} → {can, reason}`, fail-closed |
| `createJWT(secret)`            | HMAC-SHA256 sign/verify, timing-safe                    |
| `createRateLimiter(options)`   | In-memory sliding-window rate limiter                   |
| `createAuditLogger(context)`   | Hash-chained tamper-evident logger                      |
| `assertSafeIdentifier(value)`  | Validate SQL identifier                                 |
| `assertSafePath(path, base)`   | Prevent path traversal                                  |
| `sanitiseForLog(value)`        | Safe string for log output                              |
| `z`                            | Re-exported Zod instance                                |

> **Note**
>
> For a higher-level policy engine that composes rate limiting, RBAC, and CORS into a single
> per-route check, see [`@azmr/policycore`](https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/policycore.md).

---

# @azmr/policycore

> Security policy engine — rate limits, auth, CORS, request signing, secrets, API keys, and OWASP Top 10 reporting.

Source: https://platform.azmara.io/docs/packages/policycore

`@azmr/policycore` is a standalone security layer built on top of `@azmr/security`'s `createRateLimiter`, `createAccessControl`, and `createAuditLogger` — it composes them rather than reimplementing them.

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @azmr/policycore
```

## Policy engine

Composes rate limiting, an RBAC auth requirement, and CORS as code into one per-route `evaluate()` call.

```typescript
import { createPolicyEngine } from "@azmr/policycore";
import { createAccessControl } from "@azmr/security";

const engine = createPolicyEngine({
  accessControl: createAccessControl({ policy: { admin: [{ resource: "reports", action: "read" }] } }),
  policies: {
    "reports:read": {
      rateLimit: { options: { maxRequests: 100, windowMs: 60_000 } },
      auth: { resource: "reports", action: "read" },
      cors: { allowedOrigins: ["https://app.azmara.io"] },
    },
  },
});

const result = await engine.evaluate("reports:read", {
  subject: { id: "u1", roles: ["admin"] },
  origin: "https://app.azmara.io",
});
// result.allowed, result.rateLimit, result.auth, result.cors
```

| Prop            | Type                                                                                                                | Default | Required | Description                                                                 |
